Description

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history.

Northrop Grumman Mission Systems is a trusted provider of mission-enabling solutions for global security. Our Engineering and Sciences (E&S) organization pushes the boundaries of innovation, redefines engineering capabilities, and drives advances in various sciences. Our team is chartered with providing the skills, innovative technologies to develop, design, produce and sustain optimized product lines across the sector while providing a decisive advantage to the warfighter. Come be a part of our mission!

Northrop Grumman Mission Systems' Baltimore and Partnered Sites (BaPs) division is seeking a Staff Engineer Test – Lab Manager Lead to join the Tactical Fighters Business Unit. The Lab Manager Lead will provide technical and operational oversight of a team of lab managers supporting multiple integration and test laboratories, and will serve as a primary liaison between the program and the broader lab‑management community.

The candidate should have strong knowledge in integration and test, troubleshooting, manufacturing, SAP, calibration, procurement, and laboratory operations. This position is responsible for coordinating with all engineering disciplines and operations teams to meet program integration test schedules and budget, while ensuring laboratories are configured, maintained, and operated safely and efficiently through effective leadership of the lab managers.

The Lab Manager Lead will be accountable for consolidating lab status, risks, and action items across multiple labs and for tracking progress and issues using Jira and other Atlassian tools. The ideal candidate will have strong teambuilding skills and exhibit comprehensive verbal and written communication/presentation skills.

This position is based in Baltimore, MD, requires being onsite, and does not support remote or hybrid work.

What You’ll get to Do:

  • Provide leadership and day‑to‑day oversight for a team of lab managers, including setting priorities, aligning resources, mentoring staff, and promoting best practices for lab operations, safety, and configuration management.
  • Lead the architecture, design, build‑out, and ongoing maintenance strategy for the laboratory infrastructure that enables both hardware and software engineering activities, ensuring scalability, reliability, and compliance with system‑level requirements. Direct and coordinate execution of these activities through the lab managers.
  • Own the end‑to‑end engineering bench lifecycle sustainment across multiple labs at the program level, ensuring lab managers are effectively procuring, installing, qualifying, and retiring bench equipment while maintaining physical integrity, safety, and alignment with system architecture road‑maps.
  • Provide oversight of documentation for test‑fixture setups, as‑built drawings, and configuration changes to workspaces, and ensure lab managers are properly tracking all program‑, corporate‑, and customer‑owned property through Property Management.
  • Provide oversight of equipment calibrations and configuration of test equipment for bench operations, ensuring lab managers maintain calibration schedules, execute configurations, and document all configuration changes across the supported labs.
  • Provide leadership for logistics‑related activities, ensuring lab managers coordinate procurement, receipt, verification, storage, and distribution of tooling, consumables, and capital assets, and maintain inventory levels and hardware trackers for PME, GFE/BFE, and other assets.
  • Coordinate escort and access with the Security team for equipment and personnel requiring special handling or secure areas, and maintain secure storage safes in accordance with program and corporate requirements.
  • Direct and align day‑to‑day lab activities across the lab‑management team with Program Management, Systems, SEIT, I&T/IPT, Software, and TDE leadership; conduct facilities surveys and communicate aggregated lab status, utility, and growth needs to Facilities Engineering.
  • Establish and maintain consistent, program‑level views of lab readiness, utilization, issues, and risks; aggregate status from individual lab managers and present concise updates and recommendations to program and functional leadership.
  • Utilize Jira and other Atlassian tools to plan, track, and report lab‑related tasks, defects, configuration changes, and action items, and ensure lab managers and stakeholders are using these tools consistently to maintain accurate and timely status.
  • Develop, maintain, and enforce standard operating procedures for lab operations, including configuration control, access control, equipment handling, and incident reporting, and drive adherence across the lab‑management team.
  • Act as safety liaison and enforce all EHSFP directives; champion continuous improvement in lab safety culture and compliance.

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor of Science degree in a STEM discipline and 12 years of relevant experience; OR Master’s degree in a STEM discipline and 10 years of relevant experience; OR PhD in a STEM discipline and 8 years of relevant experience; an additional 4 years of relevant experience in lieu of a STEM degree (i.e., 16 years of relevant experience without a degree).
  • Active DoD Top Secret Clearance or higher and Special Access Program (SAP) clearance is required.
  • Minimum 8 years of radar‑system support and development, including hands‑on work with Common Radar Module (CRM) standard, receiver/exciter, processor, ground/airborne radars, manufacturing, operations, and systems engineering.
  • Proven ability to collaborate with business units and divisions and communicate effectively with both technical and non‑technical audiences.
  • Demonstrated experience in integration and test environments, including troubleshooting complex systems, working across multiple engineering disciplines, and supporting manufacturing and operations.
  • Experience with laboratory operations including equipment installation, calibration, configuration management, and property/inventory control.
  • Ability to work full-time onsite in Baltimore

Preferred Qualifications

  • 8+ years of systems‑engineering experience focused on laboratory operations, test‑equipment management, and logistics coordination.
  • Prior experience leading or supervising lab managers, technicians, or cross‑functional teams responsible for multiple integration or test labs.
  • Expertise in integration, test, reliability, and endurance testing of radar systems.
  • Direct experience coordinating procurement, receipt, storage, and distribution of tooling, consumables, and capital equipment, with accountability for results through a team.
  • Experience using Jira and other Atlassian tools to manage tasks, track defects, maintain action‑item lists, and provide status reporting for engineering or lab operations.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with a track record of producing clear shipping plans, inventory reports, facility‑status briefs, and program‑level lab readiness reports.
  • Demonstrated ability to work with multiple engineering specialties, cross‑functional teams, and external suppliers, and to translate program requirements into clear, actionable work for lab managers and support staff.

This position is contingent upon successful transfer of Top Secret Clearance and Special Access Program (SAP) clearance.

Mass General Brigham relies on a wide range of professionals, including doctors, nurses, business people, tech experts, researchers, and systems analysts to advance our mission. Job Summary

Join Our Team at Our New Weymouth Location!

We're excited to be opening a brand-new office in Weymouth and are looking for dedicated team members to help us launch this location successfully. Prior to the office opening, candidates must be willing to complete training at other nearby sites. This is a unique opportunity to join a growing team, contribute to the success of a new practice, and make a meaningful impact on patient care from day one.

We are seeking both new and experienced ophthalmic assistants to join our team. Certified and uncertified candidates are encouraged to apply!

Whether you are looking to begin a career in Ophthalmology or build upon existing experience, our team is committed to providing the training, mentorship, and support needed for long-term success.

title: Program Manager, Housing Stability
description:
The Housing Stability Program Manager cultivates investments and collaborations within the Gilbert Family Foundation that support housing stability, asset protection, and homeowner creation goals. The Program Manager supports strategy development, collaborates with internal team members and external community partners, and uses a data-driven approach to build a cohesive portfolio of grants. They are responsible for developing grant concepts in collaboration with others, executing on grant agreements, maintaining a reporting relationship with partners throughout the grant cycle, and managing internal processes to support that grant process (for example, marketing and communications, Salesforce, reviewing reports, and more).

About the role

  • Identify, develop, and scale investments that support organizational goals within probate; estate planning; non-profit capacity building; and supply and acquisitions.

  • Assess and inform the homebuying experience, at a system level, to enhance the homebuyer experience and infrastructure supporting the housing ecosystem in Detroit.

  • Build and nurture strategic partnerships with diverse stakeholder groups including government agencies, community development organizations, and philanthropic organizations to advance housing supply and homeowner creation initiatives.

  • Apply a data-driven approach to cultivating investment opportunities that align with the organization's strategy, mission, and values.

  • Manage grants throughout their lifespan in Salesforce and steward the relationship with grantees.

  • Set strategic, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound (SMART) goals and then implement a work plan to achieve them.

  • Proactively manage risks by identifying and escalating challenges. Stay solution oriented and support the team in implementing solutions.

  • Stay curious about the issue area, trends and changing landscape to best inform organizational strategy and investments.

  • Work closely with the operations team on program metrics, reporting, and infrastructure.

  • Maintain communication flow between community partners and internal teams.

  • Coordinate with internal teams such as Marketing and Communications to develop storytelling opportunities that build awareness of our programs, initiatives and impact.

  • Maintain alignment with mission and values with the ability to demonstrate that commitment in daily interactions.

About you

Minimum Qualifications

  • 3 years of project management experience in philanthropic, government, or non-profit spaces.

  • Experience partnering with diverse stakeholder groups such as government, community development, and philanthropic funders.

  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate with others internally and externally.

  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills and the ability to communicate with individuals at all levels of an organization, including executive leadership.

  • Demonstrated ability to understand and respond to partners’ needs in rapidly changing business or community environments in a way that also aligns with the organization’s goals and strategies.

  • Demonstrated ability to set, meet and reflect on program goals, milestones and outcomes as well as to pivot tactics when appropriate.

  • Demonstrated ability to use data to identify opportunities that drive systemic change.

Preferred Qualifications

  • 5 years of project management experience in philanthropic, government, or non-profit spaces with experience working within the housing ecosystem of Detroit or similar communities.

  • Proficiency with key technologies including Microsoft Office Suite, Slack, Salesforce, and Workday.

  • Experience in housing, real estate development, homebuying counseling, or related investment areas.

  • Demonstrated ability to think creatively about complex problems and the courage to pursue innovative solutions.

  • Experience with systems thinking approaches to complex social and economic challenges.

What you’ll get

Our team members fuel our strategy, innovation and growth, so we ensure the health and well-being of not just you, but your family, too! We go above and beyond to give you the support you need on an individual level and offer all sorts of ways to help you live your best life. We are proud to offer eligible team members perks and health benefits that will help you have peace of mind. Simply put: We’ve got your back. Check out our full list of Benefits and Perks.

About us

The Gilbert Family Foundation is a private nonprofit foundation founded by Jennifer and Dan Gilbert to accelerate a cure for neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) and build economic opportunity and equity in the city of Detroit. The Gilbert Family Foundation supports groundbreaking, cutting-edge research in hopes of eradicating NF1, a genetic disorder that causes tumors to grow on nerves anywhere in the body. Additionally, the Foundation supports the economic stability and mobility of residents in Detroit by investing in wealth-building opportunities and breaking down systemic barriers.

title: Associate Actuary-Assumptions
description:
As an Associate Actuary you will play a key role in determining Venerable’s variable annuity assumptions used to model mortality and policyholder behavior. Primary responsibilities will include monitoring experience trends, recommending assumption updates, and presenting recommendations to senior leadership for select deferred and payout variable annuity assumptions as well as playing an integral part in the transformation of Venerable’s assumption setting processes.


Primary responsibilities include:

  • Analyze and interpret policyholder experience data to identify emerging trends, behavioral patterns, and key drivers of experience.

  • Apply actuarial judgment and statistical analysis to develop assumptions used in financial reporting, risk management, and business planning.

    • Types of riders are GMDB, GMIB (Traditional and Hybrid), GMWBL, and GMWB

    • Assumptions may include, but are not limited to lapse, partial withdrawals, deferred mortality, payout mortality, GMIB annuitizations and GMWB utilization

  • Develop and present decks and detailed memorandums seeking assumption proposal approval from senior management

  • Contribute to the timely and accurate reporting of mortality and policyholder behavior experience

  • Review experience study data for accuracy and completeness and implement additional controls as necessary.

  • Drive for accuracy, consistency, and improvements within various experience studies

  • Take increasing ownership of key deliverables and workstreams, including leading analyses, driving recommendations, and collaborating with stakeholders across the organization

  • Ensure that any changes to experience study processes, particularly those in spreadsheets, are incorporated appropriately as transparent and repeatable processes with controls; maintain updated documentation on all processes

  • Collaborate with the modeling team to implement recommended assumptions into models

  • Support structural, design and process improvements to experience studies through partnering with IT and outside vendors on prioritized transformation projects

  • Provide support for internal and external audits, including walkthroughs and responses to questions from auditors/regulators

  • Interact and collaborate with highly skilled staff both internally (e.g., IT, Valuation, Finance) and externally (e.g., modeling outsourcing partner)

  • Support future transactions by performing various analyses related to experience studies

Key Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Mathematics, Actuarial Science, Finance or related business discipline

  • ASA, Career ASA or newly credentialed FSA

  • 5-6+ years financial, insurance industry, or actuarial experience

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to identify patterns, trends, anomalies, and key drivers within large and complex datasets

  • Exceptional attention to detail with a proven ability to validate data, reconcile results, investigate anomalies, and ensure the accuracy and reliability of analyses

  • Excellent computer skills are required: Advanced knowledge of Microsoft Excel, proficient in SQL Server, Microsoft PowerBI, R, or Python, experience with Microsoft PowerPoint is a plus

  • Advanced knowledge of actuarial concepts; ability to use this knowledge to lead/develop solutions to adhoc requests or issues

  • Solid understanding of insurance products, regulations, or insurance company structure from prior experience; Prior experience with variable annuity products preferred

  • Leverages strong oral and written communication skills to readily and effectively collaborate with peers, managers, shares information and asks questions

  • Ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines

  • Strong desire to learn and grow

  • Experience with improving and optimizing processes and reflecting appropriate controls

  • Ability to work in a cross-functional team environment

Note: Eligible candidates are required to hold immediate, legal U.S. work authorization without the need for current or future visa sponsorship.

title: Travel Specialist
description:
Travel Specialist

As a Travel Specialist, you will execute the program’s plan, processes, and activities for contract travel on behalf of the government. You’ll coordinate travel activities with program leaders, initiating quality, security, risk, and cost controls to maximize compliance with the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) and Joint Travel Regulations (JTR). You’ll support a Program Management Office's geographically dispersed team with significant CONUS and OCONUS travel requirements. You’ll work with program leadership, project leads, and a team of travelers to support overall travel requirements, including Travel Authorization Requests (TARs), Trip Reports (TRs), travel expense reporting, and overall quality management. You’ll also train, mentor, and advise program personnel on travel processes, activities, and business rules, providing resources such as standard operating procedures and training guides.

On our team, you will work with program leadership, project leads, and multiple stakeholders to implement travel processes and tools and identify and recommend ways to improve efficiency and streamline operations.

At Booz Allen, we recognize that we must continuously grow as a team to bring the best support to our clients, so here you’ll have all the resources to succeed. This is a chance to influence a meaningful mission while growing your career. Work with us and help our defense client achieve their goals as we help improve warfighter readiness.

  • Experience with the Department of War, Intelligence Community, or FEDSIM programs
  • Experience submitting and reviewing TARs, TRs, and expense reports
  • Experience capturing, tracking, analyzing, and reporting travel data
  • Experience working with the JTR and compliance with travel regulations
  • Experience documenting processes and procedures, and identifying improvements
  • Experience collaborating and developing effective working relationships with various teams

title: Sentinel Director 1 - System Security Engineering
description:

Description

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history.

Northrop Grumman’s Defense Systems sector is looking for a Director 1 of System Security Engineering to its Strategic Deterrent Systems Division. This position will be located in Roy, Utah and will support the Sentinel program. Northrop Grumman supports the Air Force’s sustainment, development, production and deployment of hardware and system modifications for Intercontinental Ballistic Missile (ICBM) Ground and Airborne Launch Control Systems, Launch Facilities and associated infrastructure. This position may offer relocation assistance.

What you will get to do:

Direct and lead a multi-disciplinary team in support of Program Protection and Product Protection requirements to include Supply Chain Risk Management, Supply Chain Security, acquisition risk management, and security countermeasure implementation.

You will lead a cross-functional team spanning the CONUS in the performance of System security engineering activities to include: requirements, architecture, design, threat and vulnerability analysis, development, evaluation, assessment and authorization supporting all phases of systems development and production in the areas of Information Assurance (IA) / system security engineering, security Assessment and Authorization (A&A) as per RMF (Risk Management Framework), Supply Chain Security, Operations Security (OPSEC), Protection of Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) under DFARS 252.204-7012, Hardware/Software Assurance, and protection of Critical Program Information (CPI)/Critical Technologies (CT).

Execute on strategic planning and cost / schedule focused delivery and mitigation of program risks tied to milestone execution and management of program baseline scope

Participate as an active program team member in key recurring operations, including NCTA planning and review, program management reviews, recurring status reporting, staff meetings, etc.

Support program level requirements for multi-sector interfaces and activities where required

title: Software Engineer
description:
**Candidates must reside in Indonesia and have existing authorisation to work there**

About Us

Revalue is a carbon credit development platform focused on one of the planet’s most critical but complex challenges - seeing nature regenerated at a planetary scale.

Our mission is to design the most cutting-edge and trusted nature credits for our planet.

We are bringing together a world-class team - forestry experts, ecologists, applied AI scientists, software engineers, geospatial analysts, commercial specialists, economists, and more - to create the unique DNA required to reimagine nature credits.

About the role

We are looking for a Software Engineer to join our Engineering team within Platform Intelligence.

Platform Intelligence develops the data infrastructure, machine learning, geospatial pipelines, and technical systems behind Revalue's nature and carbon intelligence products. We turn scientific and analytical work into repeatable, reliable outputs: ingesting and validating Earth observation datasets, producing the analyses and baselines that underpin our carbon methodologies, designing monitoring systems, and running the cloud platform underneath.

This role is about moving from analytical and ML prototypes to production-grade systems. You will work closely with engineers, data scientists, and analysts to build data pipelines, productionise models, and improve reproducibility, making workflows maintainable, observable, and usable by others.

Some of the most important work is deciding what to build, how to model it, and where to draw boundaries. You will work with domain experts to make those decisions rather than simply implementing predefined specifications.

It is a hands-on role at the boundary between software engineering, data science, geospatial engineering, and cloud infrastructure. You will not be expected to lead scientific model development, but you will make sure the models run reliably in production.

Who we are looking for

Please note: Candidates must have existing authorisation to work in Indonesia.

A strong mid-level or senior individual contributor who can own delivery independently and turn complex technical workflows into stable production systems.

Key skills:

  • Strong software engineering background. Design, interface, contract, data and domain modeling.

  • Scientific programming background in any domain: geospatial, remote sensing, ML, signal/audio/vision, quant, simulation, bioinformatics. We care more about the pattern of experience rather than the specific domain: translating messy, abstract, real-world structures into correct data representations and transformations.

  • Comfortable across stacks and tools: generalist disposition, able to pick up new languages/frameworks as our needs shift.

  • Familiar with modern SWE practices and product-engineering: discovery, scoping, iterative and incremental delivery, comfortable operating in ambiguity.

Hard skills:

  • Good engineering practice: testing, code review, CI/CD, modular design, documentation.

  • Experience productionising analytical, data science, or ML workflows: turning exploratory code into reliable systems, with a working understanding of batch processing, reproducibility, monitoring, and deployment.

  • Day-to-day work is in scientific Python. However, we weigh fundamentals and data aptitude above prior Python experience: if you have done this kind of work in C++, Scala, … , that counts.

  • Cloud engineering experience, ideally on GCP and AWS, including designing and operating cloud-based data systems.

  • A pragmatic mindset: knowing when to build carefully, when to simplify, and when to avoid unnecessary complexity.

Soft skills:

  • Comfortable with high-visibility, shared-ownership, collaborative work: pairing on decisions, small trunk-based commits, and real-time feedback on work in progress.

  • Comfortable running discovery sessions with domain experts before building.

  • Strong communication, including presenting technical solutions to colleagues and non-technical stakeholders.

  • Advanced proficiency in written and spoken English.

Nice to have:

Experience in any of these would be valuable, though we do not expect all of them:

  • Geospatial data, raster/vector processing, Earth observation, or remote sensing.

  • Data quality checks, lineage, observability, or reproducibility tooling.

  • Full-stack experience: a backend and frontend you have maintained or owned.

  • Applying AI tools to improve engineering, developer, or analytical workflows.

  • Tools such as Docker, GitHub Actions, Dagster, Terraform, Postgres, DuckDB, Dask, xarray, rasterio, or geopandas.

  • Scientific computing, climate, nature, carbon, or environmental data.

  • Improving an existing platform, on a team where data scientists and analysts contribute code.

What you will do

  • Make design and data-modelling calls: what a manifest has to guarantee, where a boundary sits, what belongs in a shared library and what stays out, when to defer rather than build.

  • Build and maintain the geospatial data pipelines behind our datasets: syncing sources, validating and ingesting them, and exporting project-aligned outputs for analysis.

  • Turn notebooks, prototypes, and research code into tested, modular production code, and keep it that way as requirements change.

  • Productionise our modelling pipelines and the orchestration they run on: partitioned assets, schedules, and concurrency.

  • Make runs reproducible and observable: manifests, pinned dataset versions, deterministic outputs, and monitoring that tells us when something breaks.

  • Build new data and monitoring products, including proper cataloging for our datasets.

  • Performance tuning: profiling real runs, concurrency within memory bounds, and keeping runtime/cost predictable.

  • Work on the backend (Kotlin/Spring, Postgres) and frontend (React/Remix) where results reach customers.

  • Own cloud infrastructure in Terraform across GCP and AWS: batch jobs, storage, IAM, CI/CD, and alerting.

  • Run discovery with scientists and analysts.

  • Contribute to dev tooling: ship/release scripts, agent skills that encode our engineering procedures, and repo instructions.

What success looks like

In the first few months, you will get to know our platform, cloud setup, and data workflows, and start owning productionisation work. Over time you will help build clearer patterns, more reliable pipelines, and better reproducibility and monitoring.

You will be doing well if analyses are easier to run and repeat, if analysts and scientists depend less on manual processes, if pipelines are predictable in runtime and cost, and if fewer critical systems rely on one person to keep them moving.

What We Offer

  • The opportunity to shape the future of nature-based climate finance

  • A mission-driven organisation with shared purpose, culture, and values

  • A diverse team of colleagues, partners and clients based all around the world

  • Meaningful equity in an early-stage startup with a growing and trusted brand

  • Flexible working environment with a team deeply committed to impact

  • Generously enhanced, gender-neutral parental leave policy

  • Wellbeing support, including company-funded access to therapy

🌱 If you’re ready to build our Engineering function and care about driving real impact - we’d love to meet you!

title: Physical AI Engineer (Control, Optimization, Validation)
description:
Can you build intelligent systems that understand physical environments, make autonomous decisions, and demonstrate measurable real-world value? PassiveLogic is looking for a Physical AI Engineer to develop, optimize, and validate our autonomous control system, AI models, and levels of autonomy.

About PassiveLogic

PassiveLogic is the first fully autonomous platform for buildings. We’ve reinvented the fundamental principles of automation to democratize technology, optimize buildings, and reduce the world’s carbon footprint. We are a team of technologists, engineers, and creatives dedicated to making a sustainable impact through real-world solutions.

We are looking for team members who have a passion for technology and want to work on cutting-edge problems with real-world solutions. Our culture is built on bringing together the most talented engineers, thinkers, and creatives — backed by the world’s leading investors — working together to make the future a reality.

About the Role

You will develop and validate the algorithms that enable buildings to understand their physical state, learn from experience, and autonomously optimize their operation.

This role combines control theory, optimization, machine learning, physics-based simulation, and systems validation. Your work will span digital twins, autonomous reasoning, building physics, equipment behavior, and human comfort. You will develop production-quality algorithms and test them in simulation, laboratory systems, and real buildings.

What You’ll Do

Develop Autonomous Control and Optimization

  • Design and implement autonomous control strategies that use physics-based digital twins for prediction, optimization, and decision-making.

  • Translate comfort, energy, equipment life, and operational requirements into control objectives, constraints, and cost functions.

  • Develop scalable optimization algorithms using methods such as stochastic gradient descent, coordinate descent, distributed optimization, Bayesian methods, and evolutionary algorithms.

  • Design and implement physics-based automated fault-detection and diagnosis algorithms.

  • Develop fault-tolerant control methods that support degraded operation and system recovery.

  • Integrate control and learning algorithms into production systems while meeting reliability and real-time performance requirements.

Develop AI and Learning Systems

  • Develop physics-informed predictive and learning models using deep learning, reinforcement learning, and transfer learning.

  • Develop autonomous agents, state-estimation methods, model adaptation, and control-correction algorithms.

  • Create learning methods that remain reliable under noise, outliers, sparse data, model uncertainty, and changing system behavior.

Validate Physical AI Systems

  • Define performance metrics, acceptance criteria, and automated tests for autonomous capabilities and levels of autonomy.

  • Test system behavior under disturbances, incomplete observations, model divergence, and equipment, sensor, or communication failures.

  • Verify fault-detection accuracy and validate fault-tolerant control, degraded operation, and recovery behavior.

  • Compare simulation results with analytical solutions, laboratory measurements, and real-building data.

What You’ll Bring

If your experience does not meet all our posted requirements below, we’d still love to hear from you. We are looking for practitioners who are passionate about understanding people, committed to lifelong learning, and driven by the love of what they do. If that’s you, please apply!

You Must Have

  • MS or PhD in control engineering, computer science, robotics, applied mathematics, mechanical engineering, or a related field.

  • Demonstrated expertise in AI development, scientific machine learning, optimal control, reinforcement learning, multi-agent systems, physics-informed machine learning, and optimization theory.

  • Strong technical background in control theory, model predictive control, state estimation, and system identification.

  • Strong programming skills in Python, C++, Swift, or a similar language.

  • Strong analytical, debugging, root-cause analysis, communication, and collaboration skills.

You Should Have

  • Experience with automatic differentiation and differentiable programming.

  • Experience with software design, design patterns, and software architecture.

  • Knowledge of building science, HVAC systems, thermodynamics, energy modeling, or grid-interactive controls.

It’s Helpful to Have

  • Experience with software-in-the-loop and hardware-in-the-loop testing.

  • Experience with formal methods, probabilistic modeling, and graph neural network.

  • Experience with building energy-modeling tools such as Dymola and EnergyPlus.

  • Experience in vector, SIMD, and tensor computational methods.

We know there are candidates who might not fit everything we’ve described above, or who might have experience and skills we haven’t considered. PassiveLogic can sometimes be flexible enough to shift responsibilities to the right person, or otherwise identify open or upcoming roles that may better fit your professional background. Even if you don’t meet all the requirements above, we still want to hear from you.

title: Senior Quality Control Data Scientist
description:
Build our future together:

Regeneron is building the digital Quality Control laboratory, and looking for a QC Data Scientist to keep that data layer running: validating that what reaches LIMS is what left the instrument, maintaining the statistical control limits behind Review by Exception, and turning QC data into information leaders can act on. Working across the orchestration, LIMS, and instrument software, helping to bring Industry 4.0 laboratories into practice, this role delivers the QC scientific data framework day to day, with strong scientific judgment.

When & where:

  • Monday–Friday, 8:00am–4:30pm
  • Location: Rensselaer, New York, United States

Discover your role:

  • Execute daily validation and reconciliation of instrument-to-LIMS data flows across the lab bus confirming the completeness, accuracy, and integrity of data transferred from instruments (Empower and others) into LIMS and data lake solutions.
  • Maintain and monitor statistically valid control limits and Review by Exception (RBE) logic; triage flags and out-of-trend signals with method-specific scientific judgment and escalate issues.
  • Validate parsing and data-transformation configurations for every new method onboarding, instrument qualification, and software release ensuring the pipeline interprets analytical outputs correctly before they reach LabWare.
  • Build and maintain dashboards, reports, and analytics that translate QC data into actionable information for analysts, managers, and stakeholders.
  • Apply statistical and machine-learning-supported tools (multivariate analysis, trending, anomaly detection) to support performance-monitoring programs and technical investigations.
  • Troubleshoot data-transfer discrepancies at the scientific level distinguishing formatting and rounding artifacts from true signal-integrity issues and driving them to resolution.
  • Support GxP data integrity (ALCOA+) for the scientific data layer; contribute to investigations, CAPAs, and inspection readiness.
  • Partner with QC analysts, laboratory informatics / IT, and OT to keep the scientific data pipeline healthy leading the scientific and data-quality dimension while infrastructure and platform administration remain with IT / OT.
  • Use LLMs (Claude, ChatGPT, etc.) to accelerate drafting, coding, and analysis with the judgment to keep probabilistic AI out of validated GxP data and quality decisions.

This role requires:

  • BS/BA Biochemistry, Chemistry, Biology, Data / Computational Science, or a related field; with 6+ years relevant analytical or QC data experience — preferably in the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industries. PhD strongly preferred with 2+ years relevant experience.
  • Proven understanding of analytical and bioassay variability and the statistical basis for control limits, trending, and Review by Exception.
  • Applied statistics and data analysis: multivariate methods (PCA / PLS), trending, and anomaly detection; exposure to machine-learning tools.
  • Strong SQL and data-modeling skills (ETL, data cleansing, transformation) and programming for data manipulation (Python and/or R).
  • Specialized statistical / modeling software (e.g., JMP, Minitab, SIMCA, Discoverant, MATLAB).
  • Experience with Tableau, Spotfire, and Power BI.

The Mass General Brigham Development Office represents a team of 450+ vibrant, collaborative, and skilled fundraising professionals. We are dedicated to inspiring visionary philanthropy that advances caring and curing for patients in Boston and around the world. Philanthropy enables Mass General Brigham to deliver the highest quality patient care, pursue the most innovative and promising research, train the brightest minds to become the next generation of healthcare leaders, and expand and improve our world-class facilities. Join us in our mission to transform the future of medicine. The Mass General Brigham Development Office offers excellent benefits, competitive salaries, and a hybrid flexible work schedule.

To Apply:
Applications must include a current resume and a cover letter detailing applicable experience and accomplishments.

Summary:
The Assistant Director of Development plays an integral role in strengthening Mass General Brigham’s philanthropic program. Working in close collaboration with colleagues in Philanthropic Relations and across the department, the Assistant Director is focused on the qualification, cultivation, and solicitation of gifts below $250K, to build out the pipeline of high-level unrestricted support and future major gift donors.

The Assistant Director will manage a portfolio of prospects and donors and meet annual fundraising and performance metrics as established by the department.

Essential Functions:
• Under the direction of the Senior Director of Leadership Giving, execute a process of personalized and systematic cultivation resulting in the solicitation and closing of annual unrestricted gifts from prospects with the capacity to support the hospital with a gift of $25,000, up to $250K.
• Manage a pool of prospects and donors and meet annual performance metrics of dollars raised, and meaningful donor contacts, including completed and documented calls, individualized letters, emails and personal visits. Fundraising and performance metrics are reestablished annually.
• Document all activity in database.
• Work closely with assigned beat area(s) colleagues to align restricted fundraising efforts within the clinical area, advocate for blended asks of both unrestricted and restricted support and serve as a resource on unrestricted giving.
• Successfully solicit and close new and renewed gifts, including outright, planned gifts and gifts of assets, partnering with other gift officers, hospital and department leadership, and faculty, as appropriate
• Actively advocate for and raise awareness of unrestricted giving within both internal and external audiences.
• Develop an understanding of and stay abreast of Mass General Brigham’s breadth of research, clinical, teaching, and community service programs.
• Be an engaged and active participant and collaborator within the team and across the department and institution, engaging in healthy and productive activities and contributing to the overall positive office environment.
• Participate in professional development and stay well-informed of annual giving and overall fundraising trends and practices.
• Collaborate with appropriate directors of development and physicians to champion and execute agreed upon activities and strategies.
• Demonstrate high integrity and professionalism.

Bachelor’s degree required and 3-5 years of fundraising or related experience. In addition, the ideal candidate will possess the following skills, abilities and competencies:

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, attention to detail, strong work ethic and strategic thinking skills

title: Geologist – Water Infrastructure Projects
description:
Company Overview:

We are a dynamic organization committed to the development, rehabilitation, and expansion of water infrastructure projects across Nigeria. We collaborate with government institutions, NGOs, and donor agencies to deliver sustainable and impactful water supply solutions nationwide.


Job Summary:

We are seeking an experienced Geologist to support groundwater investigations, borehole development, hydrogeological assessments, and geotechnical evaluations for water infrastructure projects.

The ideal candidate must have hands-on experience in groundwater exploration, borehole siting and supervision, aquifer testing, and geological investigations related to water supply projects. Experience handling donor-funded, NGO-sponsored, or government water projects is highly desirable.

The role requires strong technical expertise in hydrogeology, subsurface investigations, and reporting, as well as the ability to work closely with engineers and contractors during drilling and construction activities.


Key Responsibilities:

Hydrogeological Investigation & Borehole Siting:

  • Conduct geological and hydrogeological surveys for groundwater development projects.

  • Identify suitable borehole locations using geophysical and geological data.

  • Supervise borehole drilling operations and ensure proper well construction.

  • Log boreholes and prepare detailed lithological and hydrogeological reports.


Aquifer Testing & Analysis:

  • Conduct and interpret pumping tests and step-drawdown tests.

  • Analyze groundwater yield, recharge capacity, and sustainability.

  • Recommend appropriate borehole design, casing, and screen placement.

  • Evaluate groundwater quality and suitability for intended use.


Geotechnical & Site Assessment:

  • Provide geological input for construction of reservoirs, treatment plants, and transmission infrastructure.

  • Assess soil and subsurface conditions affecting civil works.

  • Identify potential geological risks and recommend mitigation measures.


Project Coordination & Compliance:

  • Work closely with Civil, Mechanical, and Electrical Engineers during project implementation.

  • Ensure compliance with Nigerian water resource regulations and environmental standards.

  • Prepare technical reports for submission to regulatory bodies and donor agencies.

  • Participate in project meetings, site inspections, and technical reviews.



Requirements

Qualifications & Requirements:

Education & Experience:

  • BSc/MSc in Geology, Hydrogeology, or related field.

  • Minimum of 7 years of relevant experience in groundwater development and water infrastructure projects.

  • Proven experience in borehole drilling supervision and aquifer testing is required.

  • Experience handling donor-funded, NGO-sponsored, or government projects is highly desirable.


Professional Certification (Compulsory):

  • Registered with COMEG (Council of Nigerian Mining Engineers and Geoscientists) – Mandatory.

  • Membership of relevant professional bodies (e.g., NMGS) is an added advantage.


Technical Competencies:

  • Strong knowledge of hydrogeological investigation techniques.

  • Experience with geophysical survey methods (VES, resistivity, etc.).

  • Ability to interpret geological maps and subsurface data.

  • Familiarity with groundwater modeling and reporting tools is an advantage.

  • Good understanding of Nigerian water resource regulations.


Personal Attributes:

  • Strong analytical and field investigation skills.

  • Detail-oriented with strong reporting ability.

  • Ability to work in remote field locations.

  • Good communication and teamwork skills.

  • Willingness to travel extensively across project sites in Nigeria.




Benefits

title: Surgery Scheduler
description:
Classification: This is a full-time, non-exempt position with benefits.


Description

As an orthopedic office surgery scheduler, your primary responsibility is to effectively manage and coordinate the scheduling of surgical procedures for patients. You will work closely with orthopedic surgeons, patients, and other healthcare professionals to ensure efficient scheduling, accurate documentation, and timely communication. Your attention to detail, organizational skills, and ability to handle sensitive information will contribute to the smooth operation of the orthopedic office.


Primary Responsibilities


1. Surgical Procedure Scheduling:

  • Collaborate with orthopedic surgeons to schedule surgical procedures, considering the surgeon's availability, operating room availability, and patient preferences.
  • Communicate with patients to explain the surgical scheduling process, provide preoperative instructions, and answer any questions or concerns.
  • Gather necessary patient information, including medical history, insurance details, and surgical consent forms.
  • Coordinate with hospitals, surgical centers, and other facilities to secure operating room time and necessary resources for each surgical procedure.

2. Preoperative Preparation:

  • Ensure all preoperative requirements are fulfilled, including scheduling preoperative tests, consultations, and clearances as required.
  • Communicate with patients to provide preoperative instructions, including fasting guidelines, medication adjustments, and any necessary pre-procedure preparations.
  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date records of preoperative tests, clearances, and consultations in the patient's electronic health record (EHR).

3. Communication and Coordination:

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for patients, surgeons, and other healthcare professionals regarding surgical scheduling.
  • Coordinate with the medical office staff, including medical assistants, and front desk personnel, to ensure smooth patient flow and timely communication.
  • Communicate surgical schedule changes, updates, and cancellations to all relevant parties promptly.
  • Collaborate with Prior authorization team to obtain necessary authorizations and ensure accurate billing information for surgical procedures.

4. Documentation and Record-Keeping:

  • Accurately enter and update surgical procedure details in the electronic health record (EHR) system, including surgical codes, dates, and relevant notes.
  • Maintain organized and up-to-date surgical schedules, ensuring they are easily accessible and confidential.
  • Prepare and distribute surgical schedules, reports, and other relevant documents as needed.
  • Assist in compiling statistical data or reports related to surgical scheduling and patient outcomes.

5. Follow-Up and Postoperative Coordination:

  • Schedule postoperative appointments and follow-up visits for patients, coordinating with surgeons and other healthcare professionals.
  • Provide postoperative instructions to patients, including wound care, medication management, and physical therapy recommendations.
  • Assist in arranging any necessary postoperative tests, imaging, or rehabilitation services.

6. Pre-Authorization

  • Obtains the necessary authorization from the insurance payer before the procedure.
  • Coordinates with providers, clinical teams, and insurance companies to obtain missing information.
  • Tracks authorization status, approval/denial, and authorization numbers or expiration dates.
  • Communicates any issues or denials to the appropriate team for resolution or peer-to-peer/appeal.
  • Ensures authorization is completed before the scheduled procedure to minimize denials, cancellations, delays, and unexpected patient financial responsibility.

description:

POSITION OVERVIEW:

Transport freight across dock area to/from trailers for loading to trailers.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

  • Perform freight handling using appropriate motorized and manual equipment, including but not limited to: forklift, pallet jack and hand truck.

  • Verify documentation matches freight description (e.g. type, weight, hazardous materials), using current electronic or manual system.

  • Secure freight inside trailers using appropriate tools and supplies (e.g. pallets, straps, rope).

  • Verify and complete required documentation and reports.

  • Assist customers with freight and freight documentation as needed.

  • Perform hostling duties if required.

  • Comply with all applicable laws/regulations, as well as company policies/procedures.

DISCLAIMER: This job description is general in nature and is not designed to contain or to be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, essential functions and qualifications required of employees assigned to the job.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • High school diploma or equivalent, preferred.

  • Must be at least 18 years of age.

  • Prior experience in warehousing, freight handling and/or fork lift operations preferred.

Who we are

SBCS (formerly South Bay Community Services) transforms communities to support the well-being and prosperity of children, youth, and families. For more than 50 years, we’ve worked throughout San Diego to provide safe shelter, transitional housing, intervention prevention programs, mental health support, and many other services that meet the ever-changing needs of our communities.


Our organization is dedicated to offering high-quality services and ensuring all services align with the community's needs. To best serve our communities, SBCS partners with various grassroots organizations throughout California to develop innovative strategies that enhance services, empower clients, and ensure that culturally appropriate and trauma-informed care is offered. SBCS provides a wide range of services tailored to meet each client's unique needs. At SBCS, our client-centered approach highlights the importance of respect, empathy, and compassion when interacting with all community members.


About YOU

You are an advocate and champion of nurturing communities where families can pursue their dreams and fulfill their potential.


You are dedicated to and energized by engaging directly with individuals and communities.

You care deeply about the well-being and prosperity of ALL children and youth throughout San Diego.


You want to become a part of an energetic and effective team, and contribute your expertise, creativity, and insights to a unique role encompassing program management, development, and direct counseling services for at-risk children, adolescents, and families.


About our organization

SBCS is home to a committed team of 470 dedicated employees and volunteers who diligently serve all of San Diego County. Having offered services for 52 years, SBCS is committed to providing hope and support for numerous young children, individuals, and families facing adversity. With an annual budget of $68 million, SBCS continues to be a beacon of assistance in the community.


Competitive and Sustainable Employee Pay Package:

SBCS offers competitive pay and additional benefits for full-time employees, including generous vacation time, holidays, health, vision, dental, flexible spending accounts, an employee assistance program, discount programs, public service forgiveness loan, and an excellent retirement plan with matching contributions.


Responsibilities:

Under the supervision of the Program Director, and Department Director, Clinician is responsible for providing evidence-based social-emotional and mental health services to students within the San Ysidro School District, and their families. This position will include on-site services and may include frequent travel between school sites throughout the week. Other responsibilities include working closely on a day-to-day basis with teachers, administrators, nurses, counselors, and caregivers to create a school environment which results in improved behavior and academic achievement for all students. Services will be in keeping with the agency goals, objectives, mission, and style provided within a team framework.


Duties:

  • Provide crisis intervention, safety planning, and consultation on school campuses, in keeping with SYSD and school policy.
  • Maintain accurate and timely electronic case records, including data entry, assessments, treatment notes, and service documentation, in accordance with agency, program and school district requirements.
  • Utilize the SYSD-approved EHR system, including the Care Solace platform to complete and maintain required documentation.
  • Develop expertise on CYBHI billing procedures and provide training and guidance to staff.
  • Expected to meet required productivity and billable hour expectations.
  • Utilize evidence-based strategies to provide social emotional learning through developing social skills and conflict resolution.
  • Conduct intakes, assessments, and treatment plans with clients.
  • Conduct assessments with students and their families, as indicated by referrals.
  • Provide individual, group, and/or family therapy, as well as case management, and collateral services, as indicated by assessments.
  • Provide therapeutic, case management, and crisis intervention services to clients and their families.
  • Process program referrals from designated school site.
  • Travel between multiple school sites may be required.
  • Conduct training for program staff and caregivers.
  • Communicate with school personnel regarding referrals, waitlist times, and students’ participation.
  • Participate in team meetings, training, individual supervision, and clinical group supervision.
  • Participate in agency required trainings, staff meetings, and activities.
  • Participate in school and community-based meetings as requested or required
  • As other duties assigned.

​

POSITION SPECIFICS​

Your working location will be fully on-site in Reston, VA, but options exist for limited hybrid of on-site/work from home, based on project-dependent ability. This role requires frequent travel to sponsor locations in the Beltway area and to associate contractor and second party locations within and outside the continental United States. Trip lengths may be up to 2 weeks in duration.

We are searching for analytical software engineers to join the Strategic Systems Operation Division within the Information Advantage Office at the Applied Research Laboratory (ARL) at Penn State. This role will focus on software implementation, test, and productization.

ARL is an authorized DoD SkillBridge partner and welcomes all transitioning military members to apply.

You will:

  • Apply your expertise in software to contribute to programs of national or international impact by identifying emerging challenges, research trends, and future opportunities

  • Ensure technical excellence and on-time completion of all project tasks

  • Develop and deliver clear updates on program status to Fleet-level personnel at both individual and community meetings

  • Interact and collaborate regularly with the engineering team, principal investigator, sponsors, and other stakeholders

  • Embrace ARL’s mission to discover, demonstrate, transition, and educate while contributing as a key member of a multi-disciplinary engineering team

Required Skills/Experience areas include:

  • Proficiency in one or more modern programming languages such as Python, C++, Java, or Rust

  • Ability to design, implement, and maintain high-quality, scalable software solutions across the full development lifecycle

  • Strong understanding of software development principles, including object-oriented design, modular architecture, and version control

  • Experience developing, testing, and maintaining software in Linux and/or Windows environments

  • Working knowledge of modern development tools (Git, CI/CD pipelines, automated testing frameworks)

  • Knowledge of data structures, algorithms, and performance optimization

  • Experience with cloud platforms, distributed systems, or container technologies (Docker, Kubernetes)

  • Ability to produce clear, maintainable, and well-documented code

  • Systematic troubleshooting of operating systems and input-output debugging

  • Understanding of the network protocol stack

Preferred Skills/Experience areas include:

  • Prior success collaborating with product owners, researchers, system engineers, and other stakeholders to translate requirements into well-architected technical designs

  • Success in environments where various forms of communication and organizational skills were crucial to be effective

  • Demonstrated capacity to balance detail-oriented thinking while maintaining the ability to see the “big picture”

  • Demonstrated experience supporting transitional efforts

  • Current eligibility for access to classified information at the Secret level or higher and may be subject to a government background investigation to upgrade clearance eligibility to the TS/SCI level

  • Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD degree in Computer Engineering or Computer Science

title: Security Officer
description:
Company Overview:

We are a dynamic organization committed to the development, rehabilitation, and expansion of water infrastructure projects across Nigeria. We collaborate with government institutions, NGOs, and donor agencies to deliver sustainable and impactful water supply and treatment solutions nationwide.


Job Summary:

We are seeking a highly experienced and disciplined Security Officer to oversee the security of personnel, assets, and operations across multiple project locations, including security challenged and high risk regions.

The ideal candidate should preferably have prior experience in the armed forces, police, civil defence, or similar security agencies. The role focuses on strategic security planning, risk management, and coordination.

Experience managing security in conflict-prone, remote, or high-risk environments is highly desirable.


Key Responsibilities:

Security Strategy & Oversight:

  • Develop and implement security strategies for projects across multiple locations.

  • Provide oversight of site-level security arrangements and personnel.

  • Establish standard security protocols and procedures across all project sites.

  • Advise management on security risks and mitigation strategies for operations.


Risk Assessment & Threat Management:

  • Conduct security risk assessments for project locations, especially in high-risk regions.

  • Monitor evolving security situations and provide regular intelligence updates.

  • Develop contingency and emergency response plans.

  • Recommend risk mitigation measures for staff movement and field operations.


Coordination with Security Agencies:

  • Maintain relationships with military, police, NSCDC, DSS, and other relevant agencies.

  • Facilitate security clearances, escorts, and interventions where necessary.

  • Engage with local authorities and community stakeholders to enhance security cooperation.


Operational Support & Field Coordination:

  • Provide guidance on safe deployment of staff to project locations.

  • Support field teams with travel risk assessments and movement plans.

  • Periodically visit project sites to assess security arrangements and provide recommendations.

  • Coordinate security logistics for operations in remote or volatile areas.


Incident Management & Reporting:

  • Lead response to security incidents affecting personnel or assets.

  • Investigate incidents and prepare detailed reports with recommendations.

  • Maintain centralized security logs and documentation across projects.


Compliance & Safety:

  • Ensure alignment with company security policies and donor requirements.

  • Support HSE compliance in relation to security risks.

  • Participate in audits and donor compliance reviews where required.


Training & Awareness:

  • Train staff on security awareness, personal safety, and travel protocols.

  • Conduct briefings for teams working in high-risk areas.

  • Promote a culture of security consciousness across the organization.



Requirements

Qualifications & Requirements:

Education & Experience:

  • Minimum of OND/HND/BSc in any relevant field (Security Studies or related discipline is an advantage).

  • Minimum of 7–12 years of experience in security operations or security management.

  • Experience managing security in high-risk, conflict-prone, or remote environments is required.

  • Experience with NGOs, donor-funded, or large-scale infrastructure projects is an added advantage.


Professional Background (Preferred):

  • Experience working with:

    • Nigerian Armed Forces

    • Nigeria Police Force

    • Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC)

    • Department of State Services (DSS) or similar agencies


Technical Competencies:

  • Strong expertise in security risk assessment and threat analysis.

  • Experience in regional security coordination and advisory roles.

  • Knowledge of security protocols for high-risk and conflict environments.

  • Familiarity with security reporting, incident management, and crisis response.

  • Strong understanding of Nigeria’s security landscape and regional dynamics.


Personal Attributes:

  • High level of discipline, integrity, and professionalism.

  • Strong strategic thinking and decision-making skills.

  • Excellent situational awareness and crisis management ability.

  • Strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills.

  • Ability to work independently and provide leadership across dispersed teams.

  • Willingness to travel across Nigeria as required.

title: Technical Business Analyst

ScottishPower HQ, Glasgow (hybrid)

Salary from £50,400 + up to 10% bonus & other excellent benefits

Help us create a better future, quicker!

Are you passionate about solving complex business challenges and turning ideas into products that make a real difference?

ScottishPower is looking for a Technical Business Analyst to join our Centre of Excellence. This is an opportunity to shape products, services and experiences that support millions of customer interactions and thousands of colleagues across the business.

What you will be doing

Working at the intersection of business, technology, operations and customer experience, you'll play a key role in identifying opportunities, solving complex problems and delivering meaningful change. You'll collaborate with stakeholders across a wide range of functions, bringing people together around a shared vision and helping to translate ideas into measurable outcomes.

This role goes beyond traditional business analysis. You'll influence product direction, shape strategic decisions and drive initiatives from concept through to successful delivery. Whether improving customer journeys, simplifying operational processes or supporting digital transformation, your work will have a visible impact across ScottishPower.

We're looking for someone who enjoys tackling complexity, challenging assumptions and finding better ways of working. You'll use insight, data and stakeholder collaboration to uncover opportunities, prioritise investment and deliver solutions that create lasting value.

What you will bring

You'll have experience in Business Analysis, Product Ownership, Product Management, Business Change or a similar role, with a strong understanding of customer-focused environments and complex business operations. You'll be comfortable working in Agile teams, managing stakeholders at all levels and balancing strategic thinking with hands-on delivery. Experience with tools such as Jira and a track record of leading change from vision through to implementation will be key.

Knowledge of utilities, energy, customer service or digital environments would be beneficial, along with experience of enterprise platforms, data-driven decision making and modern application architectures.

If you're someone who enjoys turning complexity into simplicity, bringing people together to solve meaningful challenges and delivering solutions that improve customer and colleague experiences, we'd love to hear from you.

Join ScottishPower and help shape the future of customer and operational experiences.

What’s in it for you

As well as a competitive salary which is reviewed annually, you can also enjoy a number of other benefits. With our pension scheme, we’ll double match your contribution up to a company contribution of 10%.

At ScottishPower, we believe it’s the little things we do in life that make a big difference. From helping you look after your family’s wellbeing, save for your future and take personal steps for climate action – our benefits are designed to help you do just that - so that you have everything you need to take care of your world – today and tomorrow. That’s why our benefits include:

  • 36 days annual leave

  • Holiday purchase – perfect your work/life balance with extra annual leave

  • Share Incentive Plan and Sharesave Scheme

  • Payroll giving and charity matched funding

  • Technology Vouchers – save more and spread the cost of your technology purposes

  • Count us in – pledge to reduce carbon emissions and help fight climate change

  • Cycle to Work scheme and public transport season ticket loans

  • Life Assurance (4x salary)

  • Plus shopping, leisure, restaurant and gym discounts, and unique employee deals on travel insurance and more

Why ScottishPower

ScottishPower is part of the Iberdrola Group, one of the world’s largest integrated utility companies and a world leader in wind energy. With a commitment to generate all of our energy from renewable resources and a drive to create the energy infrastructure of the future, we’re at the forefront of the journey to Net Zero and investing over £6m every working day to make this happen. With diverse opportunities across our businesses and a commitment to invest in our own internal talent, ScottishPower can offer people real career opportunities that meet personal and professional goals, in a global organisation.

title: EHS Professional
description:
Grand Canyon University! One of Arizona’s leading institutions of higher learning. Located in the Valley of Sun in the heart of Phoenix, Arizona, GCU is an institutionally accredited, private, nondenominational Christian University.

The Health and Safety Specialist supports day-to-day operations by managing a number of critical EHS processes including performing workplace audits and inspections, coaching employees on safety practices, and delivering health and safety training. The Health and Safety Specialist will play a key role in the incident and injury reporting process by working with Supervisors and Managers across multiple departments.

  • Assist in the implementation and maintenance of a comprehensive EHS Management System.
  • Assist in the development of and compliance to Safe Work Practices (SWP), regulatory standards (OSHA, EPA, ADEQ, Fire Code, U.S. Department of Education, etc.) and university policies and procedures.
  • Assist in developing means and methods to ensure active employee engagement in the EHS Management System such as leading or participating in safety committees, responding to employee safety concerns in a timely manner or gathering input from employees when developing safe work practices.
  • Plan and conduct routine and periodic workplace audits and inspections to assess existing conditions and to determine compliance with policies, procedures, and applicable regulations and based upon the assessment, developing recommendations for corrective actions.
  • Conduct Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) assessments; research safety equipment which meets business and regulations and recommends safety equipment/supply purchases.
  • Work with management team to perform investigations to determine causal factors and develop preventative and corrective actions.
  • Assist in implementing and maintaining EHS Programs such as LOTO, Electrical Safety, Fall Protection, Confined Space Entry, Respiratory Protection, Hazard Communication, Hearing Conservation, Bloodborne Pathogens, Chemical Safety, Laboratory Safety, Waste Management, Emergency Response, Powered Industrial Trucks, Mobile Elevated Work Platforms, etc.
  • Assist with follow up actions from insurance carrier audit recommendations.
  • Conduct EHS Inspection Program tasks including but not limited to safety shower and eyewash stations, fixed ladders, portable ladders, chemical storage, spill control, fall protection equipment, gas detection equipment, PPE, forklifts, MEWP, work vehicles, etc.
  • Maintain logs and documentation associated with EHS Inspection Program.
  • Perform regulatory liaison and ensure inspections by regulatory agencies are coordinated and deficiencies minimized and corrected rapidly.
  • Maintain detailed records associated with the specific duties within the EHS program.
  • Keep current with EHS-related policy changes to quickly perform applicable GCU policy and procedure adjustments.
  • Perform EHS-related training to GCU staff, students, and contractors which meets regulatory and campus policy.
  • Performs other duties as requested.

QUALIFICATIONS: The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skills, and/or abilities required to successfully perform the job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  • Knowledge of the principles and practices of occupational health and safety.
  • Knowledge of federal, state, and local laws and regulations governing occupational health and safety (i.e. OSHA).
  • Skill in interpreting and applying federal, state and local safety laws and regulations.
  • Skill in developing and conducting health and safety training classes for staff, faculty and students.
  • Skill in investigating and analyzing accidents and their causes.
  • Knowledge of principles and practices of industrial hygiene to include applicable measurement and/or sampling methods and technologies.
  • Apply the principles of industrial hygiene to include recognition, evaluation and control of recognized hazards.
  • Ability to work directly with local, state and federal regulatory agencies.
  • Proficient in verbal communication with individuals in face-to-face, one-on-one setting or by telephone.
  • Speaks and writes clearly, concisely and effectively; listens to, and understands information and ideas as presented verbally or in writing.
  • Establishes and maintains effective working relationships with employees at all levels of the University’s organization.
  • Establishes priorities for own workload based upon such factors as need for immediate action, work objectives, work schedule, knowledge of future needs, etc.
  • Ability to comprehend and make inferences from written material.
  • Ability to use a personal computer and other office equipment.
  • Strong organizational and time management skills with a demonstrated ability to handle, prioritize, coordinate and complete competing tasks within deadlines.
  • Willingness to adapt to GCU’s four pillars: Academic Advancement, Christian Camaraderie, Extracurricular Excellence and Wellness/Well Being.
  • Willing to work outside normal business hours on days or weekends, if an emergency situation exists.

Education and/or Experience:

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor or Associate degree in occupational health and safety or other health and safety related field.
  • Minimum of 7 years’ experience in the occupational health and safety field.
  • Significant knowledge of OSHA regulations.
  • Able to pass pre-employment background check.
  • Must have valid driver's license and clean driving record

Additional Preferred Qualifications:

  • Subject Matter Expert in all applicable federal, local and state EHS regulations.
  • Occupational health and safety experience in a college or university environment.
  • OSHA 511
  • OSHA 501
  • Professional certification (ASP, ASHM, etc)
