description:
McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.

What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.

Role Summary

The Principal Product Manager translates McKesson’s HR product and employee experience strategy into an enterprise product portfolio. Reporting to the VP, HR Product Management & Employee Experience, this role shapes product strategy across multiple HR products, employee journeys, workforce capabilities, and AI-enabled employee experiences; influences enterprise prioritization and investment decisions; and ensures measurable value realization for employees, managers, HR teams, and the business.

This is a senior individual contributor role that operates as a product thought leader and strategic connector across HR, Technology, Employee Experience, Operations, Legal, Privacy, Risk, and Change teams. The role is accountable for portfolio-level product direction, outcome definition, cross-product sequencing, and maturity of product management practices — without formal people-management responsibility.

Enterprise Product Portfolio Strategy

  • Define and evolve the product strategy across multiple HR product domains, employee journeys, and workforce capabilities.

  • Translate enterprise workforce priorities, employee insights, technology trends, and business needs into multi-year product roadmaps and investment recommendations.

  • Identify opportunities to simplify experiences, reduce fragmentation, improve adoption, and create more connected end-to-end HR experiences.

  • Shape portfolio decisions based on measurable value, risk, adoption, compliance, feasibility, and business impact.

Product Governance, Prioritization & Decision Support

  • Establish portfolio-level prioritization approaches that help leaders make clear trade-offs across products, journeys, and capabilities.

  • Frame decision-ready recommendations for senior leaders, including outcomes, dependencies, risks, investment needs, and sequencing options.

  • Manage strategic dependencies across HR Product, HR Technology, Employee Experience, HR Services, COEs, and enterprise governance forums.

  • Surface enterprise-level risks and decisions early, escalating only when broader leadership alignment or investment decisions are required.

AI-Enabled HR Product Innovation

  • Lead identification, evaluation, and scaling of AI-enabled HR capabilities across assigned product portfolios.

  • Define product expectations for responsible AI use, including trust, transparency, human-in-the-loop controls, quality monitoring, and escalation paths.

  • Partner with Legal, Privacy, Risk, Technology, and Compliance teams to ensure AI-enabled capabilities meet enterprise standards and jurisdictional requirements.

  • Evaluate vendor releases, emerging technologies, and external product trends to inform future HR product strategy.

Product Performance & Value Realization

  • Establish portfolio-level success measures tied to adoption, employee experience, operational effectiveness, self-service, cycle time, containment, and business value.

  • Maintain visibility into product performance, benefits realization, portfolio costs, and return on investment.

  • Use analytics, listening signals, service trends, workforce insights, and product adoption data to inform roadmap decisions and continuous improvement.

  • Ensure product teams move beyond feature delivery to measurable outcomes and sustained value realization.

Product Management Maturity & Operating Model Discipline

  • Serve as a thought leader for HR product management practices, reinforcing consistent standards, artifacts, and operating routines.

  • Create reusable frameworks for product one-pagers, decision logs, roadmap visibility, scope boundaries, success metrics, and release-readiness expectations.

  • Mentor Product Managers and matrixed partners to strengthen product thinking, prioritization discipline, and outcome orientation across HR.

  • Advance maturity of McKesson’s HR product operating model by reinforcing single intake, backlog discipline, clear decision rights, and transparent trade-offs.

What Success Looks Like

  • HR product portfolios are clearly aligned to enterprise workforce priorities, employee experience standards, and measurable business outcomes.

  • Senior leaders have decision-ready visibility into product priorities, dependencies, risks, investments, and value realization.

  • AI-enabled HR capabilities are adopted responsibly and reinforce trust, compliance, usability, and business value.

  • Product roadmaps reflect integrated experiences rather than isolated tools or projects.

  • Product management practices become more consistent, scalable, and outcome-oriented across HR.

  • Employees, managers, and HR teams experience more connected, efficient, and trusted HR products over time.

Required Experience

  • 12+ years of progressive experience in product management, digital strategy, transformation, HR technology, employee experience, or related disciplines.

  • Demonstrated experience shaping enterprise-scale product portfolios, multi-year roadmaps, or complex digital transformation initiatives.

  • Experience influencing senior leaders and enterprise prioritization or investment decisions without formal authority.

  • Experience operating in large, matrixed organizations with significant cross-functional dependencies.

  • Exposure to HR, workforce technology, employee experience, service delivery, or regulated environments preferred.

Required Skills & Competencies

  • Strategic product leadership — connects workforce strategy, employee experience, technology, data, and business outcomes into a clear product direction.

  • Portfolio management — balances competing priorities, dependencies, sequencing, risk, and investment trade-offs across multiple product domains.

  • Executive influence — frames decision-ready recommendations and aligns senior stakeholders without formal authority.

  • Systems thinking — understands how journeys, platforms, processes, data, and operating models interact across the enterprise.

  • AI and digital fluency — understands how to identify, prioritize, govern, and scale AI-enabled capabilities that improve employee experience, productivity, and business outcomes.

  • Outcome orientation — defines success measures, knows the numbers, and manages products toward adoption, value, and continuous improvement.

Leveling Note

Positioned as an individual contributor at Professional P6 (Principal), subject to Compensation confirmation. This role is broader than a single product or journey owner and is intended to provide enterprise-level product leadership across multiple HR product domains, influence portfolio investment decisions, and mature HR product management practices. Distinguished from M5 by the absence of formal people leadership; impact is delivered through enterprise influence, thought leadership, portfolio strategy, and cross-functional product accountability.

title: Senior Software Engineer
description:
Job Description

Senior Software Engineer — IT Cluster Platform Location: Remote, India About the Role Our client's IT Developer Enablement Applications team is seeking two Senior Software Engineer contractors for a role that blends full-stack development, DevOps, and systems engineering. The successful candidates will build intuitive developer interfaces while ensuring that the underlying infrastructure is automated, secure, and scalable, and will help create, modify, and modernize applications for internal stakeholders. Key Responsibilities Execute the full software development lifecycle (SDLC) within an agile environment. Design, implement, and maintain scalable, reliable, and highly available infrastructure systems supporting business applications and services. Automate repetitive tasks and processes using scripting and configuration management tools (e.g., Python, JavaScript/React, Bash, Terraform, Ansible, Ansible Tower). Manage cloud-based infrastructure (OpenShift) and optimize resources for reliability, performance, and security. Monitor system performance, troubleshoot issues, and maintain uptime and reliability through proactive alerting, metrics, and incident response. Partner with development teams to build seamless CI/CD deployment workflows using GitLab Pipelines, GitHub Actions, and Jenkins, ensuring code moves to production safely and efficiently. Conduct root cause analysis (RCA) for incidents, document findings, and implement preventive measures to minimize downtime. Continuously improve system architecture, deployment processes, and tooling to enhance operational efficiency and scalability. Apply security best practices across infrastructure, including access controls, network configurations, and compliance requirements. Communicate effectively with stakeholders and project team members to maintain visibility into development efforts. Respond promptly and professionally to customer tickets and inquiries. Monitor system health through advanced metrics and alerting, and lead incident response efforts to maintain strict uptime SLAs. Required Qualifications 5+ years of experience delivering enterprise software applications. 5+ years of experience with JavaScript/React, AngularJS, Node.js, and Ansible. 5+ years of experience in cloud service development, compute engineering, automation, architecture, and implementation on AWS. 3+ years of experience with OpenShift. Expert-level proficiency with GitLab/GitHub CI/CD. Experience with Backstage plugins. Working knowledge of SQL and database coding. Demonstrated experience across the full SDLC. Experience with containers and container orchestration tools (Docker, Podman, Kubernetes, OpenShift, etc.). Advanced knowledge of CI/CD pipelines and tooling (GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, etc.). Experience with configuration management tools (Ansible, Terraform, etc.). Preferred Qualifications 5+ years of experience with Linux administration (RHEL, CentOS, etc.). Strong Linux/RHEL system administration skills. Interview Process Recruiter Screen — background, logistics, and overall fit. Panel Interview — with representatives from Engineering, DevOps, and Platform Architecture.

title: Subcontracts Administrator
description:
Be visionary

Teledyne Technologies Incorporated provides enabling technologies for industrial growth markets that require advanced technology and high reliability. These markets include aerospace and defense, factory automation, air and water quality environmental monitoring, electronics design and development, oceanographic research, deepwater oil and gas exploration and production, medical imaging and pharmaceutical research.​

We are looking for individuals who thrive on making an impact and want the excitement of being on a team that wins.

Job Description

Job Summary:

Teledyne Brown Engineering (TBE) is seeking a Subcontract Administrator to solicit subcontractor proposals, conduct negotiations, subcontract administration, and manage close-out activities of subcontracts issued under government and/or commercial contracts. The Subcontract Administrator acts as the Company’s primary representative to the supplier on contractual matters to ensure contractual requirements of the Company are met. This position will be responsible for supporting the preparation of supply chain procurement strategies; analyzing terms and conditions of subcontracts; review proposals for compliance with regulations and policies; negotiate costs, price, and terms of subcontracts and modifications; initiate internal documentation and communicate subcontract requirements internally; support the control of subcontract costs and profits; coordinate closeout of completed subcontracts; ensure compliance with schedules for all deliverables; and prepare special reports and analyses as required. Learning and understanding overarching company operations, processes, and procedures and how the Subcontracts Administrator supports and enhances these operations are key to the success of this role. Tasks and assignments tend to be complex, non-routine and/or require a greater level of expertise. Receives assignments in the form of objectives with goals and process to meet goals outlined. Duties are performed under very limited supervision.

Detailed Description:

  • Responsible for participating in the preparation, negotiation, and implementing or managing supply chain risk management requirements.
  • Experience with subcontract/purchase order negotiations and solving issues associated with subcontract execution.
  • Independently negotiates with the subcontractors regarding various issues to include contract terms and conditions, pricing, technical requirements, and scope.
  • Conducts supplier surveillance on a regular basis.
  • Interfaces with senior supplier representatives to conduct proposal evaluations, supplier performance, and translating material to various suppliers, internal and USG audiences.
  • Identifies risks and obstacles to achieving business goals and provides solutions or seeks assistance.
  • Frequently interacts/collaborates with contracts administrators, program managers, proposal pricing, finance, business analysts, and supplier representatives.
  • Responsible for overseeing, documenting, implementing and maintaining the improvements they contribute.

Requirements:
Requires a bachelor's degree (BA or BS) in business administration, contracts, or related field, plus five (5) years of related experience.

Preferred Skills/Experience:

  • Experience with subcontract/purchase order negotiations and solving issues associated with subcontract execution.
  • Must have strong communication (written and verbal) skills and the ability to manage complex projects.
  • Professional certifications are desirable, but not required.
  • Candidate must have experience with various contract types and have strong working knowledge of the FAR, DFARS, related supplements, and TINA.
  • Must be able to obtain a Security Clearance.

Teledyne and all of our employees are committed to conducting business with the highest ethical standards. We require all employees to comply with all applicable laws, regulations, rules and regulatory orders. Our reputation for honesty, integrity and high ethics is as important to us as our reputation for making innovative sensing solutions.

Teledyne is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or veteran status, age, or any other characteristic or non-merit based factor made unlawful by federal, state, or local laws. ​

title: DSP 2
description:

Join our team, and provide support to people that have disabilities! Are you passionate about helping and caring for people? Are you now or have you ever been a caregiver? Then apply now!

Provide support in group homes. $21/hr.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTION:

Ability to walk, stand, stoop, and kneel for extended periods of time. Ability to push/pull wheelchairs on a variety of terrain

title: Senior Software Engineer (AWS)
description:
This is a remote position.

  • Partner with Product, Design, Quality Engineering, and other stakeholders to understand business requirements and translate them into practical technical solutions.
  • Contribute to the design and development of software components, applications, services, and integrations across the platform.
  • Build and maintain production software across the full stack, currently using React, TypeScript, Python/Flask, PostgreSQL, and AWS.
  • Develop accessible, intuitive web experiences in React, working closely with Product and Design to translate UI concepts into production-ready interfaces.
  • Design and implement APIs and third-party integrations while maintaining and improving existing integrations and partnerships.
  • Design, deploy, and maintain cloud infrastructure and services on AWS (e.g., EC2, S3, Lambda, RDS, CloudWatch), ensuring solutions are scalable, secure, and cost-effective.
  • Take ownership of features and initiatives across the full development → testing → deployment → launch lifecycle, including cloud deployment pipelines.
  • Write clean, maintainable, and well-structured code that other engineers can understand, extend, and support.
  • Develop and maintain unit and integration tests to validate functionality and protect product quality.
  • Participate in and lead technical design discussions and peer reviews, helping the team make sound engineering decisions.
  • Review pull requests and provide constructive technical feedback that improves code quality, consistency, and maintainability.
  • Investigate, debug, and resolve significant software defects and production issues across the application, including cloud infrastructure issues.
  • Identify technical risks in larger initiatives and work with the team to address them early.
  • Break larger technical initiatives into manageable tasks and help establish practical implementation plans.
  • Apply appropriate software design patterns and architectural approaches to solve complex engineering problems.
  • Contribute to technical specifications, implementation documentation, validation plans, and other engineering documentation.
  • Help improve engineering processes and establish repeatable software patterns, including AWS-based infrastructure-as-code practices, that make development more efficient and reliable.
  • Mentor and support other engineers when needed, contributing to the overall growth and technical standards of the team.
  • Communicate technical concepts, decisions, risks, and trade-offs clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.


Requirements

What you bring


  • 5+ years of professional software engineering experience preferred, with a track record of building and supporting production software.
  • Strong hands-on experience with React and TypeScript, including building maintainable and accessible web applications.
  • Professional experience with Python, ideally using Flask or a similar web framework.
  • Strong experience working with PostgreSQL or other relational databases.
  • Hands-on experience with AWS (e.g., EC2, S3, Lambda, RDS, CloudWatch) or a comparable cloud platform, including deploying and maintaining production workloads.
  • Strong understanding of HTML and CSS and how they contribute to accessible, reliable web experiences.
  • Experience designing, building, and maintaining REST APIs and third-party integrations.
  • Experience writing and maintaining unit and integration tests.
  • Strong understanding of software design principles, patterns, and maintainable application architecture.
  • Experience participating in code reviews and providing constructive technical feedback to other engineers.
  • Ability to own features through the full development → deployment → launch lifecycle and provide production support when needed.
  • Ability to review existing code and designs, identify weaknesses, and make improvements to efficiency, maintainability, and scalability.
  • Strong debugging and problem-solving skills, including the ability to investigate and resolve significant production issues, including in cloud environments.
  • Ability to break complex technical initiatives into smaller, actionable tasks and contribute to implementation planning.
  • Experience writing technical specifications, implementation documentation, and validation plans.
  • Ability to work effectively with Product, Design, Quality Engineering, and other cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts and trade-offs clearly to non-technical audiences.
  • Willingness and ability to mentor and support other engineers and contribute to raising the team's overall engineering standards.

Helpful, but not essential

  • AWS certification (Certified Developer or Solutions Architect – Associate).
  • Experience working in healthcare technology, telemedicine, or another regulated industry.
  • Experience building patient-facing, clinician-facing, or other high-trust applications.
  • Experience working with accessibility standards and accessible web applications.
  • Experience working in a high-growth startup or product environment.
  • Experience with Agile/Scrum development methodologies.
  • Experience working on systems involving sensitive or regulated user data.

Benefits

How the engagement works

This is a remote fulltime role with a confidential healthcare technology client operating a telemedicine platform across all 50 U.S. states. ONLY FOR CANDIDATES BASED IN THE US.

Day to day, you will work closely with Software Engineers, Quality Engineers, Product Managers, Designers, and other stakeholders, contributing across the full software development lifecycle.

The hiring process begins with a conversation with the client to discuss your experience, technical background, and mutual expectations.

Candidates then complete a short, scoped technical exercise designed to reflect the type of practical engineering work they would encounter in the role.

The final stage is a technical interview with the engineering team focused on software architecture, problem-solving, hands-on development experience, and technical judgment.

For a consultant/contractor engagement, your work will be based on the agreed scope and deliverables. You are expected to provide your own laptop and basic equipment, maintain reliable connectivity and a secure working environment, and follow required security controls, including two-factor authentication.

Apricot is a nonprofit sourcing firm connecting displaced and underserved professionals from Palestine and the wider MENA region with global employment opportunities. We combine a clear social-impact mission with fast, high-quality recruitment delivery for international clients.

title: Clinical Associate Program Manager 1
description:
Easterseals Southern California transforms lives every day. For over a century, Easterseals has championed inclusion and independence—delivering essential services like early childhood programs, autism services, employment and independent living support to more than 29,000 people each year. Through advocacy and education, we break barriers and create opportunities for the one-in-four Americans with disabilities.

Starting hourly rate: $29.33/hour

OVERVIEW OF POSITION: Under direct supervision, provides specialized behavior intervention services, parent education, and program supervision according to the goals described in the Individualized Treatment Plan and monitors the development of children in the home, the community, and/or other natural settings. Associate Program Managers work closely with the Board-Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA) and Behavior Interventionists to provide intervention, conduct assessments, write progress reports and develop programs for assigned cases.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTION:

  • Provides specialized behavior intervention services to children diagnosed with autism spectrum disorders (ASD) in the home, the community and/or other natural settings. Provides parent education and coordinates specialized training and instructional materials for caregivers.
  • Completes necessary documentation including evaluations, treatment notes, progress reports and exit summaries. Remains current with program and participant-related documents and reports. Provides participant related communication to caregivers, the program team, physicians and other health care providers, as appropriate.
  • May supervise Behavior Interventionists to ensure all recorded data are correct and accurate. Manages, maintains and creates reports from program records. Maintains data reliability and fidelity checks regularly. Plans and leads monthly progress updates for each family served with program team.
  • Assists with the creation and delivery of specific intervention activities. Provides parent education according to treatment plan or other individualized assessments. Monitors skill acquisition of children diagnosed on the autism spectrum in natural settings, under the direction of a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA).
  • Remains current regarding new research, current trends and developments in autism, special education and related fields.
  • Attends staff meetings, in-services, treatment planning, trainings, and other meetings as requested.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

EDUCATION:

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university with a concentration in early childhood education, psychology, nursing or related field.
  • Must be enrolled in a Master’s degree program in Applied Behavior Analysis or closely related field or in coursework series that meets the educational requirements for the BCBA or BCBA examination.
  • Must possess and maintain a current CPR certification.

EXPERIENCE:

  • 1 year of ABA experience with children with autism spectrum disorders and/or other related developmental disabilities

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, ABILITIES:

  • Familiar with the approaches to intervention based on the science of Applied Behavior Analysis. Competent in employing and directing behavior analytic methodologies including Pivotal Response Training (PRT), Natural Environment Teaching (NET), Picture Exchange Communication System (PECS), Behavior Skills Training (BST), and Experimental Functional Analysis (EFA).
  • Knowledge of evidence-based practices found to benefit children with Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASD). Familiar with the field of early intervention.
  • Strong clinical, administrative, and leadership skills.
  • Able to consistently demonstrate good judgment and decision-making skills.
  • Demonstrated proficiency with Microsoft Office applications (i.e. Outlook, Word, Excel, Skype, etc.) and related software applications.
  • Knowledgeable in licensed area of practice, interdisciplinary early intervention theories, and rehabilitation principles and practices.
  • Ability to maintain positive customer interaction and professionalism, communicate effectively through oral and written skills, and work cooperatively with a variety of individuals and groups; demonstrated ability to interact well with children and their families, and to maintain a positive affect.
  • Ability to interpret and implement policies, procedures and regulations; ability to exercise discretion and maintain a high level of confidentiality in handling sensitive situations and documentation.

title: Sickle Cell Program Coordinator
description:
Our Mission: At The Cancer & Hematology Centers we are dedicated to help, healing and hope for cancer patients and their families.


We provide our patients with advanced treatments, innovative research and, above all else, compassionate care. Our patients receive the most comprehensive, contemporary cancer care balanced with the compassion of a dedicated nursing and support staff. Treating cancer requires a team of committed and caring health care professionals working together to understand and address your needs. In addition to caring physicians, we have a full range of support staff available to assist you and your family, such as oncology-certified nurses, social workers, experienced lab and pharmacy personnel and a psychologist. Our focus is not just on healing but also on helping and offering hope. We know that being diagnosed with cancer is a life-changing event, and it takes a lot of adjustment to accept the emotional and physical realities of this disease. Our staff understands what you’re going through and can offer compassion and resources to help. To us, it’s important that healing isn't just centered on your disease site. Our cutting-edge cancer care is available close to home. Our medical staff have close ties to prominent hospitals and ongoing cancer research, and we bring those breakthrough advances to our regional centers to progress the level of care that is offered right here at home.

Why Join Us? We are looking for talented and high-motivated individuals who demonstrate a natural desire to support the meaningful work of community oncologists and the patients we serve.

Job Description:

Sickle Cell Program Coordinator

Position Summary:

The Sickle Cell Coordinator is a registered nurse responsible for coordinating comprehensive, patient-centered care for individuals living with sickle cell disease (SCD). This role serves as a clinical liaison, educator, advocate, and navigator across the continuum of care to improve access, reduce avoidable hospitalizations, enhance patient outcomes, and support quality-of-life initiatives.

The coordinator works collaboratively with hematologists, primary care providers, emergency departments, infusion services, social work, and community partners to ensure timely, evidence-based, and equitable care delivery.

Program Coordinator Role:

The Sickle Cell Program Coordinator supports the planning, implementation, daily coordination, and ongoing development of the sickle cell program. This role helps ensure that clinical operations, patient navigation, education, quality improvement, grant-related activities, and community partnerships are aligned to support accessible, coordinated, and high-quality care for patients and families affected by sickle cell disease.

Key Responsibilities:

1. Care Coordination & Navigation

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for patients with sickle cell disease.
  • Coordinate outpatient, inpatient, infusion, and specialty appointments.
  • Facilitate transitions of care (ED to home, inpatient to outpatient, pediatric to adult care).
  • Monitor high-risk patients and proactively intervene to prevent avoidable admissions.
  • Ensure adherence to individualized care plans and pain management protocols.

2. Clinical Support:

  • Conduct nursing assessments and symptom triage.
  • Collaborate with hematology providers on disease management plans.
  • Assist with infusion coordination (e.g., transfusions, disease-modifying therapies).
  • Monitor patients on hydroxyurea and other SCD-related therapies.
  • Support chronic pain management strategies within scope of practice.

3. Patient & Family Education:

  • Provide education on:
    • Disease process and complications
    • Medication management
    • Pain crisis prevention and early intervention
    • When to seek emergency care
  • Promote self-management and health literacy.
  • Support adherence to preventive care and vaccination schedules.

4. Emergency Department Collaboration:

  • Partner with ED teams to support standardized sickle cell protocols.
  • Advocate for evidence-based pain management.
  • Assist in developing individualized ED care plans.

5. Psychosocial & Community Resource Support:

  • Identify social determinants of health impacting care.
  • Collaborate with social work to connect patients to transportation, financial assistance, behavioral health, and community resources.
  • Support transition readiness for adolescent-to-adult care.

6. Quality & Program Development:

  • Track quality metrics (ED utilization, admissions, readmissions).
  • Grant writing to support program and patient funding
  • Participate in performance improvement initiatives.
  • Assist in development of standardized care pathways.
  • Contribute to program data collection
  • Coordinate program activities, meetings, workflows, and communication across clinical, operational, and community partners.
  • Maintain program documentation, patient tracking tools, referral logs, and outcome reports to support program monitoring and growth.
  • Support grant reporting, funding requests, community outreach efforts, and preparation of materials for internal and external stakeholders.

Qualifications:

Required

  • Current Registered Nurse (RN) license in state of practice
  • Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) preferred
  • Minimum 3–5 years clinical nursing experience
  • Experience in hematology, oncology, infusion, or chronic disease management
  • In person only

Preferred

  • Certified Pediatric Hematology Oncology Nurse (CPHON) or Oncology Certified Nurse (OCN)
  • Case management or care coordination experience
  • Experience working with underserved or medically complex populations
  • Grant writing experience

Core Competencies:

  • Strong clinical assessment and triage skills
  • Cultural humility and trauma-informed care approach
  • Excellent communication and interdisciplinary collaboration
  • Patient advocacy and system navigation expertise
  • Data tracking and quality improvement understanding
  • Ability to manage high-risk, high-utilization populations

Work Environment:

  • Combination of outpatient clinic, infusion center, and hospital settings
  • May require occasional evening or on-call support depending on program structure
  • High degree of patient interaction and care coordina

title: Senior Plant Cost Analyst
description:
Who We Are

Johns Manville is a leading manufacturer and marketer of premium-quality insulation and commercial roofing, along with glass fibers and nonwovens for commercial, industrial and residential applications. Our products are used in a wide variety of industries including building products, aerospace, automotive and transportation, filtration, commercial interiors, waterproofing and wind energy.

A proud member of the Berkshire Hathaway family of companies, we serve customers in more than 80 countries around the globe. We are committed to delivering positive and powerful experiences, because we are successful only when our employees and customers thrive. We are passionate, we care about people, we perform at a superior level, and we protect others and our environments.

Pay Range

$98,600.00-$135,500.00 Annual

This is the base salary pay range that an applicant can expect to make upon hire. Pay within this range will vary based upon relevant experience, skills, and education among other factors. In addition, this position is eligible for an incentive bonus.

The Senior Plant Cost Analyst is a highly visible business partner who helps drive financial performance and operational excellence across our manufacturing operation. This individual works side-by-side with plant leadership, operations teams, and corporate finance to identify opportunities, solve problems, and improve profitability.

Success in this role requires more than strong accounting and analytical skills. The ideal candidate is an effective communicator who can build credibility at all levels of the organization, from production associates on the manufacturing floor to senior corporate leaders. They are curious, proactive, comfortable challenging assumptions, and willing to spend time in the plant understanding how operations truly work.

This role serves as a financial advisor to the business, translating operational performance into actionable insights that drive better decision-making, cost control, productivity improvements, and long-term growth.

What Success Looks Like

  • Become a trusted financial partner to plant leadership and operational teams.
  • Develop a deep understanding of manufacturing processes, cost drivers, and operational performance metrics.
  • Identify and drive meaningful cost reduction and productivity improvement opportunities.
  • Deliver timely, accurate, and actionable financial analysis that improves business decision-making.
  • Improve the quality and efficiency of forecasting, budgeting, reporting, and financial controls.
  • Partner effectively with both plant and corporate teams to ensure alignment between operational execution and financial objectives.
  • Demonstrate a visible presence on the manufacturing floor, building relationships and understanding performance at the source.

Key Responsibilities

Drive Financial Performance

  • Partner with plant leadership to identify, quantify, and execute cost savings and productivity initiatives.
  • Analyze financial and operational results to identify trends, risks, and opportunities.
  • Provide recommendations that improve profitability, operational efficiency, and resource utilization.
  • Support strategic business decisions through financial modeling, scenario analysis, and investment evaluations.

Serve as a Trusted Business Partner

  • Collaborate with leaders across Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Procurement, and Corporate Finance.
  • Communicate complex financial information in a way that is meaningful and actionable for non-financial stakeholders.
  • Influence decision-making through data-driven insights and strong business acumen.
  • Build strong working relationships across all levels of the organization.

Lead Planning, Forecasting, and Reporting

  • Support development of annual operating plans, budgets, and monthly forecasts.
  • Monitor and communicate operational and financial performance against established targets.
  • Analyze and explain manufacturing variances, inventory movements, labor performance, and overhead spending.
  • Assist with month-end and year-end close processes, ensuring accuracy and timeliness.

Maintain Strong Cost Accounting Processes

  • Develop and maintain product BOMs, routings, and standard costs.
  • Ensure the integrity of manufacturing cost data and inventory valuation.
  • Reconcile assigned general ledger accounts and support financial compliance activities.
  • Evaluate capital project spending and provide financial analysis on investment opportunities.

Support Continuous Improvement

  • Create and improve financial processes, reporting tools, and business procedures.
  • Participate in procurement and spending reviews, including invoice resolution, general ledger coding, and related controls.
  • Provide mentorship and guidance to Associate Plant Cost Analysts and other developing finance team members.

Stay Connected to Operations

  • Regularly engage with manufacturing teams on the production floor to understand processes, challenges, and opportunities firsthand.
  • Participate in physical inventories, audits, and operational reviews.
  • Translate operational realities into financial insights and recommendations.

Preferred Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate is:

  • A strong communicator who can effectively engage with both hourly operations personnel and senior leadership.
  • Comfortable working in a manufacturing environment and eager to spend time on the plant floor.
  • Confident presenting financial information to diverse audiences.
  • Skilled at influencing without direct authority.
  • Curious, hands-on, and proactive in identifying opportunities for improvement.
  • Equally capable of working independently and collaboratively.
  • Detail-oriented while maintaining a strong business perspective.
  • Energized by solving problems and driving measurable results.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or related field.
  • 8+ years of finance or accounting experience, including manufacturing cost accounting experience.
  • Strong knowledge of cost accounting, inventory management, standard costing, forecasting, budgeting, and variance analysis.
  • Advanced Microsoft Excel skills and experience with financial modeling.
  • Experience supporting annual operating plans, financial forecasts, and strategic analysis.
  • Working knowledge of SAP and/or ERP systems.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence and partner with stakeholders across multiple levels of an organization.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.
  • Proven ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

Preferred

  • Experience supporting complex manufacturing operations.
  • Continuous improvement mindset with a track record of driving process enhancements.

Associate Plant Cost Analyst Consideration

Candidates with a bachelor’s degree and approximately 2+ years of relevant finance, accounting, or manufacturing cost accounting experience may be considered for an Associate Plant Cost Analyst opportunity, with responsibilities and scope aligned to experience level.

Why This Role Matters

This position is a key link between operations and finance. The successful candidate will not simply report results; they will help shape them by partnering with leaders, influencing decisions, and driving performance improvements throughout the manufacturing operation.

#LI-MA1 #LI-ONSITE #P #D

Please Keep in Mind

If you do not meet 100% of these requirements, we at JM still want to hear from you. So, if you are interested in the role, we encourage you to apply so we can learn how your skills and talents can contribute to our team.

Benefits

Johns Manville (JM) offers a wide range of benefits to employees. Some are subsidized by the company and others are fully employee-paid. Health benefits include a choice of comprehensive medical plans, a dental plan, vision plan, wellness program and critical illness insurance. JM sponsors a 401(k) plan which includes a sizeable company match. JM offers paid vacation and also provides paid sick and parental leave for eligible employees.

Additionally, Johns Manville provides basic life Insurance, short-term and long-term disability coverage, an employee assistance program, and business travel accident coverage. Supplemental life insurance and accidental death and dismemberment insurance are available as well. The company also offers a variety of tax saving accounts; health spending account, traditional flexible spending account, and a dependent care spending account. JM also offers a tuition reimbursement program for undergraduate and certain graduate programs.

Johns Manville supports employee growth with vast educational opportunities and a company-wide mentoring program. This program pairs employees and leaders to grow skills, build stronger internal networks and strengthen the company’s succession planning process. Johns Manville also offers soft and hard skills training facilitated by internal and external presenters. Our talent management team prioritizes the holistic growth of our workforce.

Diversity & Inclusion

Johns Manville believes diversity and inclusion in our workplace is critical for the long-term success of our company. We are committed to retaining, developing and attracting a diverse workforce that fosters an inclusive work environment in which all employees are treated with dignity and respect. This is the right thing to do for our employees, our company and our communities.

description:

Mass General Brigham relies on a wide range of professionals, including doctors, nurses, business people, tech experts, researchers, and systems analysts to advance our mission. As a not-for-profit, we support patient care, research, teaching, and community service, striving to provide exceptional care. We believe that high-performing teams drive groundbreaking medical discoveries and invite all applicants to join us and experience what it means to be part of Mass General Brigham.


Job Summary

The Mass General Brigham Development Office represents a team of 450+ vibrant, collaborative, and skilled fundraising professionals. We are dedicated to inspiring visionary philanthropy that advances caring and curing for patients in Boston and around the world. Philanthropy enables Mass General Brigham to deliver the highest quality patient care, pursue the most innovative and promising research, train the brightest minds to become the next generation of healthcare leaders, and expand and improve our world-class facilities. Join us in our mission to transform the future of medicine. The Mass General Brigham Development Office offers excellent benefits, competitive salaries, and a hybrid flexible work schedule.

To Apply:
Applications must include a current resume and a cover letter detailing applicable experience and accomplishments.


The Assistant Director of Development plays an integral role in strengthening the Mass General Brigham philanthropic program, with a focus on Surgery and other related areas. Working in close collaboration with colleagues, physicians, and other faculty, the Assistant Director is an individual contributor responsible for the strategic identification, cultivation, solicitation and stewardship of prospects and donors for assigned fundraising areas.

The Assistant Director will manage a portfolio of prospects and donors and meet annual fundraising and performance metrics as established by the department.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

• Build and actively manage a portfolio of prospects and donors, and meet annual fundraising and performance metrics as established by the department. Fundraising and performance metrics are reestablished annually, including:
o Identify, cultivate, solicit and steward new donors in compliance with patient confidentiality requirements.
o Conduct donor meetings and prospect qualifications through both proactive and reactive donor identification and engagement.
o Successfully solicit and close gifts ranging from outright, life income, bequests, and gifts of assets, with appropriate guidance from supervisor.
o Formulate, document and execute prospect and donor moves management strategies.
o Fully document work in the donor database, Blackbaud CRM.
• Work with prospects to develop and enhance the relationship with the hospital, ultimately leveraging that relationship to maximize philanthropic giving.
• Collaborate with colleagues across fundraising teams to achieve team and overall Development Office fundraising goals.
• Create, maintain and strengthen collaborative relationships with hospital and institutional partners, meeting with them regularly to encourage and support their engagement in philanthropic efforts, and provide progress updates.
• Develop an understanding of the research, clinical, teaching and community missions at Mass General Brigham, and of all giving opportunities (including planned gifts and unrestricted), and cross-team disciplines, and collaborate with colleagues across the department to produce case statements and proposals.


Qualifications

QUALIFICATIONS

Bachelor’s degree required and 3-5 years of related experience. In addition, the ideal candidate will possess the following skills, abilities and competencies:

· Experience devising and implementing cultivation and solicitation strategies
· Excellent written and verbal communication skills, attention to detail, strong work ethic and strategic thinking skills
· Proficiency in data entry, data management and reporting
· Ability to motivate, engage, influence and work collaboratively with diverse internal and external audiences in a variety of situations
· Entrepreneurial, conscientious and results-oriented work style, with motivation to learn and display flexibility in a changing environment
· Experience with Blackbaud CRM (or Raiser’s Edge), Microsoft Office Suite, and video conferencing platforms (Zoom and Teams) preferred

Construction

  • Evaluates and implements new or innovative construction methods and systems to improve efficiency, productivity, and project outcomes.
  • Represents the organization in discussions and negotiations with clients, contractors, governmental or regulatory officials, and other stakeholders.
  • Identifies risk and implements insurance and risk control strategies.

Facilities

  • Plans and allocates the capital, equipment, and operating budget to support current operations and long-term facility plans.
  • Ensures the reliability of all building mechanical, electrical, fire/life safety, plumbing, and waste management systems.
  • Establishes building operations policies, procedures, and service standards to comply with all local laws and regulations.

Buncombe County Parks & Recreation is hiring a part-time, PRN (Pro Re Nata), Facility Assistant, a hands-on role supporting our daily park operations. The primary work location is Lake Julian Park, though assignments may occasionally rotate to other recreation sites across the county. The purpose of this position is to perform a wide variety of tasks to support our daily park operations within the Recreation Department.

Knowledge, Skills, Abilities:

  • Ability to speak, understand and communicate information and ideas so others may understand.

description:

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history.

Northrop Grumman Aeronautics Systems has an immediate opening for a Project Manager to join our dynamic team with 100% onsite in Palmdale, CA.

In this role, you will serve as a vital member of the Program Integration Team, directly enabling Integrated Product Team (IPT) and Chief Engineering Team leadership to achieve operational excellence. This is a high-visibility, cross-functional position requiring a proactive team player who can seamlessly bridge the gap between technical project management, planning, execution teams, and program executive leadership.

Regular responsibilities may include the following:

As a Project Manager, you will oversee all operational aspects of ongoing projects, drive problem resolution, and manage critical stakeholder deliverables. Regular duties include:

Program Control & Reporting: Monitor project health metrics, track multi-million-dollar budget variances, update master schedules, and draft data-driven executive status reports.

Risk & Opportunity (RIO) participation: Support the management of program risks, issues, and opportunities. Coordinate RIO identification meetings and maintain tracking logs to safeguard program baselines.

Business Growth Support: Provide administrative and technical writing support during new business proposal development, ensuring proposal team files and timelines remain organized.

Program Infrastructure Management: Maintain team continuity by updating organizational charts and curating data within the program’s primary SharePoint repositories.

Financial & Resource Oversight: Review financial reports and assist integration with the business management on a monthly basis, to analyze variances, and evaluate budgets.

Executive Communication: Forge enduring and reliable relationships with internal and external stakeholders to ensure alignment on high-priority deliverables.

We offer flexible work arrangements, 9/80 work schedule with every other Friday off, phenomenal learning opportunities, exposure to a wide variety of projects and customers, and a very friendly team environment. We are looking for self-motivated, proactive, and goal-oriented people to help us grow our services and become even better at what we do.

  • Demonstrated experience coordinating multi-departmental initiatives, managing execution timelines, and aligning cross-functional teams to meet organizational goals.
  • Proven track record of maintaining tracking systems, data logs, or inventory infrastructure within highly standardized or strictly regulated industries.
  • Experience documenting processes, developing workflow aids, or maintaining compliance records to ensure operational continuity.

SALARY: $135,000 - $164,600 based on years of aligned experience in a role of similar level and responsibilities, up to 10 years. We also offer a relocation stipend if you are moving from a location greater than 75 miles from Denver!

STATUS: Full time year round, benefits eligible, exempt, in-person position

The Vice President of Talent Operations plays a central role in ensuring the vision and strategy for key talent initiatives are aligned to the mission and network goals of the organization. Additionally, this individual will serve as the leader of the Talent Operations Team providing critical oversight and support for key talent functions such as benefits, compensation, performance & evaluation, HR policies, and more. This role will serve as the leader of the Talent Operations Department and directly manage a team of senior talent leaders.

  • Shapes the vision and provides leadership support for all key Talent Operations initiatives including the organization Transformational Talent Priority work.

  • Provides critical leadership to ensure the vision and execution of compensation and benefits supports retaining and attracting transformational talent.

  • Leads the network planning process related to talent including the alignment of our people cycle with our annual & long-term planning processes.

  • Operates as a subject matter expert in best practices related to employment, wellness, compensation, and benefits.

  • Partners directly with executives and School Leaders to establish and maintain a positive school, team, and organizational culture.

  • Drives change within the organization including the adoption of new technologies, workflows, staffing models, and organization structures.

  • Responsible for growth, development, and retention of a strong talent operations team.

  • Partners closely with Talent Acquisition leadership to develop and implement effective talent strategies across Talent Operations and Acquisition in order to recruit & retain top talent.

  • Responsible for overseeing the setting, enforcing, and evaluating of legally compliant people policies, procedures, and best practices.

  • Other duties as assigned based on organizational priorities.

SKILLS

People Leader:

  • Deep reservoir of commitment to being a “partner in the people space” by building meaningful relationships with DSST leaders and team members in order to support DSST’s mission of closing the achievement gap.

  • Ability to build trust with DSST leaders and team members through consistent communication and action aligned with our DSST’s view of the Human Condition.

  • Demonstrated flexibility and ability to juggle competing priorities.

DEI Leader:

  • Engages, inspires, and empowers a diverse, motivated, and high-performing team, bringing out each team member's personal best while modeling a passion for DSST's mission and delegating tasks as appropriate.

  • Holds the organization accountable for its commitments, providing clarity, fairness, and constructive feedback, and motivates team members to reach their full potential and achieve their goals. Invests in and promotes professional development and wellness for self and staff.

  • Builds and sustains a culture where every member of the team can bring their full identity and experience to their work. Partners with staff and creates a safe space as they think proactively and boldly about the future.

  • Demonstrates a deep, authentic commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion. Actively seeks ways to diversify management and the broader team.

Team Leader:

  • The ability to lead, develop, and inspire a team of HR professionals (may include leading and managing other HR Business Partners) in a high growth, rapidly changing environment

  • The ability to understand business goals as well as design and implement new approaches, policies and procedures to effect continual improvements in business objectives, productivity and development of HR within the company

  • The desire and ability to be an influential and credible senior HR leader within the team, including setting the tone, agenda, and direction of the HR team and providing the necessary support, follow up, and leadership to ensure the team achieves desired results

  • Understand the entire talent system and each stage of the employee lifecycle and applies that understanding to craft integrated solutions that are thoughtful and reinforced by upstream and downstream talent programs

  • Systems & Data: A belief in the power of systems & data to shape our understanding and help navigate an equitable & effective path forward.

    • Develop comprehensive HR systems, protocols, documentation, and guidance.

    • A desire to constantly learn in order to both problem-solve critical challenges as well as discover new approaches to supporting DSST team members.

Project Leadership:

  • Determination to independently lead high-quality network-level project work that supports critical Human Capital initiatives in a way that demonstrates our commitment to people.

  • Ability to lead assigned projects to completion including creating & executing project documentation, cross-functional project meetings, all staff communications and project reflections.

  • Displays maturity and ability to work independently

  • Detailed-oriented, strong follow-through skills

  • Strong time management skills, ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously and meet tight deadlines

  • Interest in performing a critical support role and the ability to excel in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial, results-oriented environment;

COMPETENCIES

  • Mission Driven: Is deeply connected and committed to DSST’s mission and the belief that all students can acquire a world class education.

  • Values Driven: Is deeply committed to living our core values in their daily work.

  • Influences and Motivates Others: Inspires committed action from others to live our values, get results, and accomplish our mission.

  • Drives to Results: Has a drive and urgency to achieve and sustain results over time.

  • Demonstrates Understanding of Others: Has a strong understanding of people, an inclusive lens, and leads with our view of the human condition.

  • Is Self-Aware: Has a deep, reflective understanding of self that exhibits awareness and humility.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree

  • 10-12 years of professional experience. This should include:

    • 4+ years of HR related experience

    • 4+ years of experience in a K-12 organization

    • 4+ years of progressive leadership experience

    • 6+ years experience managing multiple projects, work streams, or initiatives

    • 6+ years of demonstrated success working across multiple teams/stakeholders (both internal and external)

  • Experience with change management on the organization level

  • Experience in developing & executing systems that achieve efficiency and scalability; can lead large scale workstreams

  • Excellent organization, time management, and follow-through; a high sense of urgency

  • Outstanding problem-solving and critical thinking skills and ability to use data to drive decision-making

  • Excellent people leadership skills; able to provide timely and actionable feedback to inspire and move direct reports to action

  • Ability to take full ownership and responsibility for the success of multiple departments, priorities, and goals

  • In depth understanding of school needs in urban charter/public school contexts

This position is primarily responsible for operating the Rewinder in a safe and efficient manner.

Effectively oversees the rewinding process in order to produce a quality product consistent with product specifications and workmanship standards. Ability to run, troubleshoot, grade change all integrated downstream equipment i.e. roll wrappers, case packers, bundlers, robot cell, etc.

title: Administratief medewerker Shared Services - Waasland
description:
Met 140+ kantoren en 600+ medewerkers realiseerde ERA het afgelopen jaar meer dan 10.500 vastgoedtransacties. Als marktleider in de Belgische vastgoedsector zijn we daar uiteraard heel trots op, maar the best is yet to come! Om verder te groeien en onze ambities waar te maken, zijn we op zoek naar toptalent. Mensen die zich voor 100% inzetten en steeds verder willen ontwikkelen op zowel persoonlijk als professioneel vlak.


Als administratief medewerker ben jij een belangrijke administratieve schakel binnen het ERA Shared Service Center. Je zorgt ervoor dat verkoopsdossiers nauwkeurig, volledig en tijdig administratief worden verwerkt en opgevolgd, van opstart tot marktactivatie.

Daarnaast ben je een echte administratieve allrounder: je springt bij waar nodig, ondersteunt collega's binnen het Shared Service Center met uiteenlopende administratieve taken en bent mee verantwoordelijk voor een vlotte en professionele dienstverlening naar onze makelaars en klanten.

Je houdt van het uitvoeren van verschillende administratieve taken binnen een vaste structuur.

Functieomschrijving
  • Je staat in voor de administratieve opstart en opvolging van verkoopsdossiers: documenten verzamelen en controleren, attesten en keuringen aanvragen, gegevens nauwkeurig verwerken in het CRM-systeem en dossiers klaarzetten voor marktactivatie.
  • Je archiveert en klasseert dossiers en documenten volgens de geldende procedures, zodat alles correct en makkelijk terug te vinden is.
  • Je bewaakt de voortgang van jouw dossiers, houdt deadlines en afspraken nauwgezet bij en neemt hierin verantwoordelijkheid en ownership.
  • Je volgt facturatie en betalingen van jouw dossiers mee op en signaleert tijdig afwijkingen.
  • Je ondersteunt bij het beheer en de opvolging van marketingmateriaal, zoals brochures, flyers en immoborden.
  • Je verzorgt de administratieve briefwisseling met makelaars en externe partners zoals fotografen, EPC-deskundigen en keuringsinstanties, en plant hun tussenkomsten in.
  • Je verzorgt publicaties en aanpassingen op vastgoedportalen, bijvoorbeeld bij prijswijzigingen.
  • Je ondersteunt waar nodig de First Line Contact (telefonie en mailbox van het team) en andere onderdelen van het Shared Service Center.
  • Je verwerkt klant- en dossiergegevens nauwkeurig en foutloos in de beschikbare digitale tools en systemen.
  • Je bent flexibel inzetbaar en vindt het vanzelfsprekend om administratief bij te springen waar de werking van het team dit vraagt.

Vereisten

  • Je bent een sterke administratieve kracht die nauwkeurig, foutloos en gestructureerd werkt.
  • Je bent vlot met het Officepakket (Excel, Outlook, Word) en maakt nieuwe digitale systemen en tools snel eigen.
  • Je hebt oog voor detail bij data-invoer, klassement en dossierbeheer.
  • Je neemt verantwoordelijkheid voor je werk en zorgt ervoor dat dossiers en administratie correct en tijdig worden opgevolgd.
  • Je houdt van verschillende administratieve taken binnen een vaste structuur en krijgt energie van afwisseling zonder het overzicht te verliezen.
  • Je werkt graag zelfstandig, maar maakt ook graag deel uit van een team.
  • Je bent praktisch ingesteld en hebt een hands-on mentaliteit.
  • Ervaring in een administratieve functie, binnen vastgoed of in een CRM-omgeving is mooi meegenomen


Voordelen

  • Een stabiele en voltijdse functie binnen een groeiend en professioneel vastgoednetwerk.
  • Een afwisselende en allround administratieve functie met verantwoordelijkheid en ruimte voor eigen initiatief.
  • Een hecht team met korte lijnen en een positieve, resultaatgerichte cultuur.
  • Een marktconform verloningspakket, aangevuld met extra legale voordelen.
  • Een professionele werkomgeving waarin autonomie, initiatief en drive sterk worden gewaardeerd.
  • Volop mogelijkheden om jezelf verder te ontwikkelen en bij te leren, met opleiding en ondersteuning binnen het ERA-netwerk.
  • De kans om een belangrijke schakel te zijn in het succes van onze makelaars en hun dossiers.
  • Een organisatiecultuur die ondernemerschap stimuleert en ruimte geeft om écht impact te maken.
  • Een werkplek in één van onze bruisende hubs in de regio Gent – Waasland – Antwerpen.
Klaar voor de volgende stap?
Ben jij de Shared Services Admin die graag de handen uit de mouwen steekt, overzicht bewaart en onze makelaars en collega's optimaal ondersteunt? Solliciteer dan nu en maak deel uit van het ERA-team.

title: Staff Software Engineer
description:
Abbott is a global healthcare leader that helps people live more fully at all stages of life. Our portfolio of life-changing technologies spans the spectrum of healthcare, with leading businesses and products in diagnostics, medical devices, nutritionals and branded generic medicines. Our 122,000 colleagues serve people in more than 160 countries.

JOB DESCRIPTION:

Job Title

Staff Software Engineer

Working at Abbott

At Abbott, you can do work that matters, grow, and learn, care for yourself and your family, be your true self, and live a full life. You’ll also have access to:

  • Career development with an international company where you can grow the career you dream of.

  • Employees can qualify for free medical coverage in our Health Investment Plan (HIP) PPO medical plan in the next calendar year.

  • An excellent retirement savings plan with a high employer contribution.

  • Tuition reimbursement, the Freedom 2 Save student debt program, and FreeU education benefit - an affordable and convenient path to getting a bachelor’s degree.

  • A company recognized as a great place to work in dozens of countries worldwide and named one of the most admired companies in the world by Fortune.

  • A company that is recognized as one of the best big companies to work for as well as the best place to work for diversity, working mothers, female executives, and scientists.

The Opportunity

This position works out of our Plano, Texas location in the Neuromodulation Division. Our Neuromodulation business includes implantable devices compatible with mobile technology to help people who suffer from chronic pain and movement disorders. These non-opioid therapies allow us to provide interventional pain therapy to patients throughout the pain continuum.

For more than 135 years, Abbott has helped people around the world live fuller, healthier lives through the right combination of science and technology. We are looking for a Staff-level technical leader to architect and advance software automation, integration, and quality engineering across the full software development life cycle for safety-critical, connected medical devices.

This is a hands-on software engineering leadership role centered on scalable test automation and continuous verification—not a traditional, script-heavy QA position. You will embed quality from requirements and design through implementation, integration, release, and maintenance. You will also apply AI tools responsibly in daily engineering work, using human oversight, traceability, privacy, security, and measurable evidence to improve—not replace—engineering judgment. As a Staff Engineer, you will set technical direction, raise the engineering bar across teams, and mentor others while remaining deeply hands-on.

What you'll work on

  • Set the automation and quality strategy. Define the vision, reference architecture, and roadmap for scalable automation and continuous verification across product lines, and drive adoption as a recognized technical authority.

  • Architect lifecycle automation. Design and build reusable frameworks, services, simulators, and engineering tools that enable requirements-based and risk-based verification at the unit, component, integration, system, regression, and release levels.

  • Integrate quality into delivery. Embed automated quality controls, traceability, diagnostics, and actionable quality signals into CI/CD pipelines so teams receive rapid, reliable feedback throughout the development life cycle.

  • Engineer connected-system integration. Develop robust integration capabilities across embedded devices, clinician applications, interfaces, services, data flows, and representative hardware or simulated environments.

  • Apply AI responsibly. Incorporate Abbott’s Responsible, Safe, Transparent, Fair, and Impactful AI principles into daily automation and quality engineering. Follow established governance and intended-use boundaries; protect sensitive data; verify generated outputs; preserve source traceability; document limitations; and maintain meaningful human oversight and accountability.

  • Advance AI-enabled engineering. Use AI copilots, large language models, and agentic workflows to improve coverage analysis, automation development and maintenance, failure investigation, and engineering productivity where their use is appropriate, validated, reproducible, and auditable.

  • Lead technical quality. Partner with software, systems, quality, cybersecurity, and product teams to improve architecture, prevent defects, close coverage gaps, strengthen design reviews, and make quality measurable across programs.

  • Ensure safety, compliance, and continuous improvement. Keep automation and AI-assisted engineering aligned with applicable medical device standards, including IEC 62304, ISO 14971, ISO 13485, and 21 CFR 820. Evaluate emerging tools, measure their impact on product quality and delivery, scale proven approaches, and mentor engineers in their effective and responsible use.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field; an advanced degree is a plus.

  • 10+ years of software engineering experience with a strong focus on automation, software quality, system integration, verification, or platform and tools engineering, including technical leadership of complex initiatives.

  • Deep hands-on experience designing test automation architecture, reusable frameworks, and CI/CD-integrated quality capabilities for complex software systems.

  • Demonstrated ability to integrate quality across requirements, design, implementation, integration, release, and maintenance using risk-based coverage, traceability, and measurable evidence.

  • Strong software engineering fundamentals and proficiency in Python, with the ability to design maintainable production-grade tools, services, and automation.

  • Hands-on experience using AI copilots, large language models, or agentic workflows in daily engineering work, with disciplined validation of accuracy, security, privacy, traceability, limitations, and appropriate human oversight.

  • A track record of setting technical direction, mentoring engineers, leading design reviews, and influencing decisions across teams and product lines.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in regulated, safety-critical, or high-reliability software domains such as medical devices, aerospace, automotive, or similar industries.

  • Experience with connected products, embedded systems, mobile or desktop applications, cloud services, hardware-in-the-loop environments, or device simulators.

  • Familiarity with evaluating AI-assisted engineering workflows, including output quality, hallucination and bias risks, reproducibility, explainability, and ongoing performance monitoring.

  • Strong systems thinking with an emphasis on reliability, observability, traceability, explainability, human oversight, and the ability to influence without authority.

Apply Now

Learn more about our health and wellness benefits, which provide the security to help you and your family live full lives:

Follow your career aspirations to Abbott for diverse opportunities with a company that can help you build your future and live your best life. Abbott is an Equal Opportunity Employer, committed to employee diversity.

Connect with us at , on Facebook at , and on Twitter @AbbottNews.

Job Overview


Executive Coordinator, Office of the Senior Vice President for Strategic Engagement – Georgetown University.


The Office of the Senior Vice President for Strategic Engagement (SVP) is seeking a proactive, highly organized, and collaborative Executive Coordinator to assist with a wide range of administrative tasks and projects covering a variety of functional areas. As a dynamic and cross-functional team member, the Executive Coordinator works to anticipate needs, process sensitive information with strict confidentiality, and ensure smooth workflow in the office of the SVP. Northrop Grumman Defense Systems is seeking to hire a Staff Systems Engineer to be the Network Risk & Compliance Lead. This position will be located in Roy, Utah and supports the Sentinel Program. This role may offer a competitive relocation package.

What You'll Get To Do:
This candidate will join the Weapon System Integration (WSI) team under Sentinel Systems Engineering, Integration, & Test (SEIT), working on Network Systems Integration (NSI). Under the guidance of the Sentinel Network Lead, the selected candidate will support the NSI team which works to develop program-wide networking governance and standards, develop and/or synthesize network artifacts at the system level (including cross-segment network interfaces, program network architecture, and network documentation), perform program-wide gap assessments for network development, develop handling plans for any identified issues, and provide networking subject matter expertise to areas such as Major Program Event (MPE) reviews, modeling (architecture, simulation, analysis....), and requirements. NSI team purview includes the deliverable network architecture, incremental/test configs (lab networks), & ITF/MIF/VSFB test networks.

Specific duties to include, but are not limited to the following:

  • Drive/facilitate networking Risks, Issues, and Opportunities (RIOs) and Internal Review Teams (IRTs)
  • Implement the Risk Management Framework (RMF) across the network
  • Track open RMF tasks and ensure all findings are closed before each MPE
  • Ensure all network changes meet the RMF and other regulatory mandates
  • Coordinate Authority to Operate (ATOs) for program networks
  • Write Security Plans (SSP), conduct STIG compliance, and manage Security Assessment Report (SAR) closure
  • Prepare the System Security Authorization Agreement (SSAA)
  • Provide networking compliance SME inputs program-wide
  • Coordinate with other network development teams
  • Participate in frequent working groups to support iterative development
  • Create and ensure that appropriate network documentation exists
  • Develop and document technical processes and procedures as needed
  • Recommend and implement system/process enhancements that will improve the performance and reliability of the system
  • Influence network requirements and interfaces; translate program-level requirements into network-level deliverables
  • Support governance adherence for waveform and lower-level OSI network management, protocols, and timing
  • Assess the design, implementation, and maintenance of scalable network infrastructure to include network design, architecture, specifications, cross-segment interfaces, and equipment selection per DoD requirements
  • Support all phases of the systems lifecycle including concept, design, fabrication, test, installation, operation, maintenance and disposal
  • Provide specific and detailed information for hardware and software selection as well as implementation techniques and tools for the most efficient solution to meet business needs, including present and future capacity requirements
  • Maintain knowledge of current and emerging Industry and DoD trends and technologies in network frameworks, management, and analytics while ensuring proper utilization where applicable
  • Establish and maintain high levels of customer satisfaction according to defined objectives while adhering to established policies
  • Exhibit good communication skills, an energetic approach, and patience with customers


Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in a Science, Technology, Engineering or Mathematics (STEM) discipline from an accredited university and 12 years of experience with Bachelor's degree, 10 years of experience with Master's degree, 8 years of experience with PhD
  • Must be a US Citizen with an active U.S. Government DoD Top Secret security clearance with an ability to obtain and maintain Special Access Program (SAP) approval within a reasonable period of time as determined by the company to meet its business need
  • Familiarity with regulatory mandates such as FISMA, DFARS
  • 4+ years of experience with security assessments and STIG compliance
  • 2+ years of experience with developing network documentation such as security plans
  • 2+ years of experience coordinating/preparing authorizations such as ATOs or SSAAs
  • 2+ years of experience with facilitating RIOs and/or implementing the RMF for a network

description:

Job Title:

Part-Time Sign Language Interpreter

Agency:
