title: Data Engineer
description:
About Us

inforcer is one of the fastest growing technology organisations in the world and a leading provider of cutting-edge cybersecurity and AI solutions to support to the SMB market. We provide MSPs (Managed Service Providers) with the fundamental technology they need to manage and secure Microsoft 365 at scale and deliver AI services. Our mission is to be inforced in every MSP!

About the Role

We're looking for a Data Engineer to design, build and maintain the infrastructure that powers our internal automation and AI platforms.

You'll develop scalable data pipelines, integrate data from multiple business systems and build the foundations of a modern data lake architecture. Working closely with internal stakeholders, you'll ensure data is accessible, reliable and ready to support analytics, reporting, automation and AI-native initiatives.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys solving complex data challenges, building robust integrations and creating scalable solutions that support rapid business growth. If this sounds like you, we’d love to hear from you.

What you’ll be doing

  • Design and maintain a scalable data lake and modern data platform architecture

  • Develop efficient data storage solutions for structured and unstructured datasets

  • Support data governance, security and compliance requirements

  • Optimise data models and storage performance

  • Develop and maintain data ingestion frameworks for internal and external systems

  • Build integrations across SaaS platforms, databases, APIs and third-party applications

  • Implement batch and real-time data ingestion patterns

  • Manage data synchronisation and change data capture (CDC) processes

  • Design, develop and maintain ETL/ELT pipelines

  • Transform raw data into trusted, business-ready datasets

  • Monitor pipeline performance and proactively resolve issues

  • Improve reliability, scalability and automation across the data estate

  • Implement data validation and quality controls

  • Create monitoring and alerting mechanisms for critical pipelines

  • Troubleshoot data issues and conduct root cause analysis

  • Ensure high levels of availability and integrity across the platform

  • Work closely with business stakeholders, analysts, engineers and leadership teams

  • Support reporting, analytics and AI initiatives through reliable data delivery

  • Contribute to data architecture decisions and platform roadmaps

  • Document solutions and promote engineering best practices

What We Can Offer You

Steep Learning curve: We believe people leave organisations when learning stops. We promise a steep and continuous learning curve to both challenge and develop our people. You are responsible for your own learning, but you’ll be surrounded by exceptional people and strong enablement, if you choose to lean into it, in an environment where it’s safe to make mistakes, try new things, and improve.

Real impact: We operate in a high-trust and autonomous environment where you can make a real impact and difference in your role and across the company.

Transparency and Honesty: We believe honest and clear communication creates a highly collaborative culture. It gives you the “why” we make decisions and allows you to effectively make your own. We won’t pull the wool over your eyes, we are a fast-growing start-up that comes with its own unique challenges, but we all work hard to solve them, together, as a team.

A+ Global Team: Our people power every part of our business, and we look for individuals who bring genuine passion to their role and operate at their very best. A-players thrive when surrounded by other A-players. Our level of growth and rate of change can be hard work and challenging, but you’ll be surrounded with exceptional people that are always happy to help.

Regular Team Socials: We celebrate our team, our milestones, promotions and achievements with social events every month.

Employee Recognition: Programs to recognise and reward our top contributors for their achievements and efforts. We live our company values every day and reward those people who embody them.

Skills We Need for This Role

  • Proven experience as a Data Engineer or in a similar role

  • Strong SQL skills and experience working with large datasets

  • Commercial experience building ETL/ELT pipelines

  • Experience developing data integrations and ingestion frameworks

  • Strong Python development skills

  • Experience working within cloud-based data environments

  • Knowledge of data modelling and database design principles

  • Experience with Microsoft Azure and Azure Data Lake Storage (ADLS)

  • Experience with data engineering tools such as Azure Data Factory, Databricks, Apache Spark, dbt or Airflow

  • Experience with cloud data platforms such as Azure Synapse Analytics or Snowflake

  • Experience using Git for version control

  • Experience integrating REST APIs and working with event-driven architectures

  • Knowledge of Kafka or other streaming technologies

  • Understanding of change data capture (CDC) patterns

  • Knowledge of data governance and master data management practices

  • A collaborative approach with the ability to communicate clearly with technical and non-technical stakeholders

Inforcer is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

title: Land Surveyor – Water Infrastructure Projects
description:
Company Overview:

We are a dynamic organization committed to the development, rehabilitation, and expansion of water infrastructure projects across Nigeria. We collaborate with government institutions, NGOs, and donor agencies to deliver sustainable and impactful water supply and treatment solutions nationwide.


Job Summary:

We are seeking a skilled and experienced Land Surveyor to support site surveying, mapping, and geospatial data collection for water infrastructure projects.

The ideal candidate must have hands-on experience in topographic surveys, route alignment, construction setting-out, and boundary surveys for projects such as water treatment plants, pumping stations, borehole schemes, and transmission pipelines. Experience on donor-funded, NGO-sponsored, or government projects is highly desirable.

The role requires strong expertise in modern surveying equipment, geospatial data processing, and interpretation of engineering drawings to support design and construction activities.


Key Responsibilities:

Surveying & Data Collection:

  • Conduct topographic, control, and boundary surveys for project sites.

  • Perform route surveys for pipelines, transmission mains, and access roads.

  • Establish benchmarks and control points for construction activities.

  • Collect accurate field data using GPS, Total Station, and other surveying equipment.


Design Support:

  • Provide survey data to support engineering design and planning.

  • Prepare survey maps, contour plans, profiles, and cross-sections.

  • Assist in route selection and alignment studies for pipelines and infrastructure.

  • Ensure survey outputs meet project specifications and standards.


Setting-Out & Construction Support:

  • Carry out setting-out of structures, pipelines, and mechanical installations.

  • Provide on-site survey support during construction activities.

  • Verify alignment, levels, and positions of installed components.

  • Monitor construction progress and ensure adherence to design coordinates.


Data Processing & Reporting:

  • Process survey data using relevant software (e.g., AutoCAD, Civil 3D, GIS tools).

  • Prepare detailed survey reports, drawings, and documentation.

  • Maintain accurate records of survey data and field notes.


Quality Control & Compliance:

  • Ensure all survey activities comply with project requirements and standards.

  • Conduct periodic checks to verify accuracy of survey data.

  • Support audits and donor compliance reviews where required.


Maintenance & Rehabilitation Support:

  • Support surveys for rehabilitation and expansion of existing infrastructure.

  • Assess site conditions and provide data for upgrade planning.

  • Assist in resolving survey-related issues during project execution.




Requirements

Qualifications & Requirements:

Education & Experience:

  • BSc/HND in Surveying, Geomatics, Geoinformatics, or related field.

  • Minimum of 5–7 years of relevant experience in land surveying, preferably within water infrastructure or civil engineering projects.

  • Experience in pipeline surveys, water facilities, or construction projects is required.

  • Experience handling donor-funded, NGO-sponsored, or government projects is an added advantage.


Professional Certification (Compulsory):

  • Registered with SURCON (Surveyors Council of Nigeria)

  • Membership of Nigerian Institution of Surveyors (NIS)


Technical Competencies:

  • Proficiency in use of Total Station, GPS/GNSS equipment, and leveling instruments.

  • Strong knowledge of surveying principles, coordinate systems, and geodetic controls.

  • Familiarity with AutoCAD, Civil 3D, GIS software, and data processing tools.

  • Ability to interpret engineering drawings and site plans.

  • Understanding of Nigerian surveying regulations and standards.


Personal Attributes:

  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy.

  • Good analytical and problem-solving skills.

  • Effective communication and teamwork abilities.

  • Ability to work independently and manage field operations.

  • Willingness to travel across Nigeria for site assignments.




Benefits

Salary: ₦ 350,000 – ₦ 500,000

title: Government Relations Professional
description:
Government Relations Professional

Work as part of Booz Allen’s Government Relations team to advance key policy priorities, advocacy efforts, and strategic relationships. You’ll collaborate across the team to deepen your understanding of federal policymaking while growing your network on Capitol Hill and within the Washington policy ecosystem.

In this role, you will research, develop, and coordinate materials that effectively position Booz Allen’s business interests in government policies and programs. Responsibilities include analyzing legislation, monitoring hearings and events, conducting targeted policy research, preparing background documents, and tracking priority issues across the Government Relations portfolio. You will also monitor federal legislative and regulatory developments, providing timely insights on emerging risks and opportunities.

The Government Relations team is seeking someone who can elevate our engagement with Congress—bringing strategic focus, urgency, and strong political instincts. We need an individual who understands the broader policy landscape while managing the details that drive outcomes on Capitol Hill.

What You'll Do

  • Lead and coordinate Congressional engagement activities, including fly-ins, Hill Days, site visits, and senior executive meeting preparation.

  • Represent Booz Allen on Capitol Hill, engaging Congressional offices and staff on behalf of Government Relations Sector Leads.

  • Develop rapid‑notification strategies and communications campaigns to support timely outreach to Congress.

  • Enhance Government Relations’ use of AI, internal CRM systems, and external data platforms to increase organizational effectiveness.

  • Track legislative, appropriations, and political developments to anticipate issues affecting Booz Allen.

  • Support Sector Leads with policy research and recommendations on legislation, proposals, and advocacy priorities.

Join us. The world can't wait.

You Have:

  • Experience using Microsoft Office tools, including Excel and PowerPoint

  • Knowledge of public policy and congressional processes

  • Ability to exercise sound political judgement while navigating the legislative and political cycles of congress

  • Ability to work well independently and as a part of a collaborative team

  • Ability develop high quality written products for executive review on tight timelines

  • Ability to manage multiple projects and competing deadlines simultaneously

Individuals that do not meet the threshold are only eligible for select offerings, not inclusive of health benefits. We encourage you to learn more about our total benefits by visiting the Resource page on our Careers site and reviewing Our Employee Benefits page.

Salary at Booz Allen is determined by various factors, including but not limited to location, the individual’s particular combination of education, knowledge, skills, competencies, and experience, as well as contract-specific affordability and organizational requirements. The estimate displayed represents the typical salary range for this position and is just one component of Booz Allen’s total compensation package for employees. title: Seasonal Associate Gardener's Supply Lebanon
description:
Love plants, trees, or the outdoors? Join Gardener’s Supply Company for a seasonal role where your passion for gardening grows into real skills and lasting friendships.

We’re hiring for our seasonal garden center team now, with positions running February through October. Whether you want to work hands-on with annuals, perennials, shrubs, and trees; serve customers as a nursery expert; or keep our operations humming behind the scenes — there’s a spot for you here.


Why Gardener’s Supply?

Gardener’s Supply Company is a New England institution. Founded in Burlington, Vermont, we’ve spent decades connecting gardeners with the highest-quality plants, seeds, tools, and know-how, and our garden centers are known across Vermont for their welcoming atmosphere and deep plant expertise.

Perks include:

• Generous employee discount on garden center products and plants

• Flexible scheduling: part-time and full-time options, morning and evening shifts available

• Supportive, upbeat team environment

• Hands-on horticulture and plant knowledge — skills you keep forever

• Opportunity to transition to a year-round role based on performance and business needs


About the Role

This is a seasonal position running February through October. Our peak season — April through June — is our most exciting time of year, with the garden center buzzing with customers searching for annuals, perennials, vegetable starts, shrubs, trees, and more. High energy and team collaboration are essential during this stretch.

Note: Time-off requests cannot be accommodated during the April–June peak period.

Most positions require weekend availability and the ability to lift 30–70 pounds. Comfort working outdoors in varying weather conditions is a must.

No plant expertise? No problem — we’re happy to train motivated, enthusiastic people who bring a great attitude and a willingness to learn.


Departments — Find Your Fit

We’re hiring across five areas of our garden center operations. Many team members work across multiple departments depending on the day’s needs.

— Customer Service Team —

Do you enjoy connecting with people and creating a great experience? Our Customer Service team is the heartbeat of our garden center. You’ll assist customers across all departments, operate POS/cash register systems, promote our Gardener’s Club loyalty program, and make sure every visitor leaves happy.

Great fit for: people-oriented individuals who thrive in a fast-paced retail environment. Gardening knowledge is a bonus but not required.

— Green Goods Team —

This is the role for plant lovers. Work hands-on every day with annuals, perennials, vegetables, shrubs, and trees across our nursery and outdoor sales areas. You’ll provide plant care, assist customers with selections, and share your horticulture knowledge to help gardeners find exactly what they’re looking for.

Great fit for: anyone with a passion for plants, greenery, and horticulture — from beginners to experienced nursery workers.

— Operations Team —

Support the backbone of our garden center by coordinating with our delivery, wholesale, and green goods teams to keep everything running smoothly. Heavy equipment experience is a plus. Outstanding customer service skills are essential, as you’ll interact with both retail and wholesale customers.

Great fit for: organized, dependable team players comfortable working in a dynamic, physical environment.

— Wholesale Team —

Help landscape professionals, contractors, and nursery buyers find exactly what they need to create stunning outdoor spaces. You’ll bring strong product knowledge of trees, shrubs, and landscaping plants to assist trade customers with larger orders and specialized requests.

Great fit for: candidates with at least one year of nursery or landscaping experience and solid knowledge of landscape plants.

— Inventory Team —

Keep our garden center stocked, organized, and ready for customers. You’ll unload deliveries, receive and process new product shipments, organize stock, and collaborate with the service teams to ensure every plant, bag of soil, and garden tool is perfectly placed.

Great fit for: detail-oriented people with strong organizational skills and a love of systems and order.

What You’ll Do Day-to-Day

• Deliver exceptional customer service throughout the garden center

• Help customers identify and select plants, trees, annuals, perennials, shrubs, and vegetables

• Share product knowledge and recommend earth-friendly gardening solutions

• Promote customer loyalty by enrolling shoppers in the Gardener’s Club program

• Identify pest problems, weeds, and plant health issues across our nursery inventory

• Assist with seasonal merchandising changeovers, restocking, receiving, and cycle counts

• Stay current on all garden center promotions, sales events, and educational opportunities

• Operate POS systems and other retail technology proficiently

• Support a positive, inclusive, respectful team culture every day

• Perform carryout duties and other tasks as assigned

title: Emergency Department Technician - 24 hours - 3p-11p
description:
Summary:


Daily activities are coordinated by the RN. Performs a variety of technical tasks and bedside functions. Responsibilities include direct patient care; hygiene, skin care, mobility, transfers and monitoring. Multiskilled to needs of unit in performing duties relative to all phlebotomy, technical skills, assisting in procedures and EKGs. Expected to manage equipment in conjunction with unit leadership and perform or assist in all procedures on unit as an integral team member. Responsible for knowledge of set up and assists in laceration repair, simple procedures and patient prep for exams. Maintains room stocking in the department. Responsible for maintaining the lab area and all associated competencies for POC testing, phlebotomy and upholding regulatory requirements to maintain POC testing ability. Possesses knowledge in upholding department goals of patient care by maximizing throughput and expediting care in this emergency department setting.
This description covers the essential functions of the position. Incumbent is expected to perform other similar and related duties as assigned. Management has the right to change or add to the job responsibilities at any time.

Job Responsibilities:

1) Provides age-appropriate care to patients.
Demonstrates the knowledge of developmental stages for a variety of age groups and applies developmental theories and concepts when implementing care for patients across the lifespan.

2) Monitors basic physiological parameters.
Takes and records routine vital signs within the specified timeframe as indicated by periodic review of documentation. Obtains and documents weights/heights, abdominal girths, head circumference (Pediatric Service) as per physician/nurse order 100% of the time as indicated by monthly review of patient records. Consistently reports any significant deviations in vital signs as outlined in the procedure immediately. Records and reports, 100% of the time, any change in patient's normal drainage pattern, i.e.gastric, wound, urine, blood. Documents findings in the patients EMR.

3) Administers treatments and procedures in accordance with BMC policy/procedures.
Changes dressings within one hour of specified timeframe in accordance with established procedure. Provides postmortum care as directed by RN according to BMC policy. Performs all procedures outlined in nursing procedure manual within area of responsibility in accordance with specifications. Assists physicians with exams and simple procedures. Assures identity of patient by checking identification bracelet and identification band prior to performing any procedure consistently utilizing PPID lab collection manager system. Follows established process and protocols for phlebotomy.

4) Assists patients with elimination of body wastes.
Makes available or offers bedpan, urinal and emesis basin immediately after patient request as indicated by absence of patient complaints. Accurately labels and sends specimens of urine, feces, wound cultures and sputum with 30 minutes of specified time frame unless discussed with RN as evidenced by randon review of reports. Accurately measures and records intake and output in accordance with established policy as indicated by random review of intake and output forms and documents in the patients EMR.

5) Performs POC testing to include department specified testing, ISAT, Urisys, Glucose testing, Pregnancy testing and all QA associated with the POC testing function. Performs proficiency tests and participates in unit inspections to maintain laboratory regulatory status.

6) Assists with treatment by following specified orders as delegated by the RN or provider treatment plans. Monitors patient's condition during treatment and notifies appropriate personnel of unexpected occurences. Provides information to RN based upon observation made during patient related care. Provides treatment within the specified time frame. Documents treatments and activities consistently.

7) Communicates effectively with team and patients.
Interacts with patients in a respectful and informative manner. Clearly communicates information related to patient care to the team. Recognizes culturally based patient and family needs. Keeps the patient's experience a priority.

8) Is knowledgeable of and initiates emergency procedures.
Responds effectively in emergency situations as observed by team members. Maintains Patient safety at all times. Communicates effectively with appropriate personnel.

9) Functions as a member of the team
Assists team members with clinical activities. Provides feedback related to the team process. Assists team members with non-clinical activities.

10) Maintains knowledge on current throughput and patient progress initiatives to maximize patient flow in the Emergency department. Actively engages in patient flow initiatives.

11) Compliance with duties and responsibilities will be monitored for adherance to requirements.

12) Provide for patient safety at all times by maintaining a patient room free of clutter and waste; implementing appropriate safety practices and protocols as per nursing intervention and direction.

Required Work Experience:

1) Direct patient care experience 1-3 years

Preferred Work Experience:

1) EMT, ED/Urgent care experience or relative experience through the military medical units (Medic/Coreman training)

Skills and Competencies:

1) Proficient in reading and writing in English

GED or HiSET (Required)

description:
StraitSys Inc

Regular

Primary Function
StraitSys is seeking talented professionals to join our successful and growing team to provide support services to the FBI's Finance and Facilities Division (FFD) Huntsville Strategy Team (HST). StraitSys is tasked with coordinating the realignment of FBI resources to Huntsville, Alabama, as part of the FBI’s Strategic Realignment Initiative (SRI). Additionally, this position may explore smaller transition opportunities to Clarksburg, West Virginia, and Pocatello, Idaho. The SRI includes the potential realignment of over 3,000 positions outside the National Capital Region (NCR), with a focus on enhancing operational efficiency and creating synergies between FBI programs. The areas of emphasis necessitate the realignment of resources to include evaluating current program structure, relocating current employees, and recruiting and hiring individuals in the Huntsville area. To ensure a successful realignment of resources, the FBI has assembled the HST to focus on the change management strategy and Division support.

title: Claims Officer
description:
EML is a leading Workers Compensation and Personal Injury Claims Management business. Our goal is to help people get their lives back through ongoing support during their return-to-work journey. We continue to experience ongoing growth and now have over 4,000 dedicated employees. We foster a learning culture that allows for us to continually invest in our employees ensuring a long-term career here at EML.

THE OPPORTUNITY

Looking to start a career where you can learn, grow, and make a real difference? Join our supportive team in Adelaide, where you'll play an important role in helping people navigate the claims process while building valuable skills and experience along the way.

As a Claims Officer, you'll receive hands-on training and support from experienced team members, giving you the opportunity to develop your understanding of claims management, return-to-work schemes, and legislation. You'll work with a variety of stakeholders, gain exposure to different areas of the business, and build a strong foundation for future career opportunities, including pathways into roles such as Eligibility Officer and Claims Specialist.

No two days are the same, and you'll have the opportunity to positively impact the lives of injured workers, employers, and treatment providers while developing your communication, problem-solving, and relationship-building skills in a rewarding and purpose-driven environment.

This will be a permanent, full-time position based in our Adelaide office. Once fully trained, you'll enjoy the flexibility of a hybrid working arrangement, with the opportunity to work from home up to 2 days per week, supporting a healthy work-life balance while continuing to build your career with a supportive and colloborative team.

YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Participate in a structured learning journey, building foundational knowledge while contributing to a positive customer experience and overall business performance.

  • Review medical and supporting documentation, included complex surgical requests, to make informed, evidence-based decisions in line with legislative and policy requirements

  • Analyse surgical procedures and medical treatment plans, identifying gaps or inconsistencies and requesting additional clinical information where required.

  • Engage with workers, employers, treatment providers and key stakeholders to support injury recovery and return-to-work outcomes.

  • Proactively identify, report and escalate any emerging or potential risks to management in a timely manner.

ABOUT YOU

  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to engage confidently with medical professionals, stakeholders and customers across phone and written channels.

  • Ability to interpret and apply medical information such as reports, treatment plans or clinical notes to support informed, evidence-based decision making.

  • Demonstrated customer focus, with the ability to take a holistic approach while remaining objective, empathetic and professional in sensitive situations.

  • Experience with Salesforce and the Microsoft Office Suite is advantageous, but not essential.

  • Highly organised with strong time management skills, able to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.


WHAT WE OFFER


We stand together as equals. EML is an equal opportunity employer so by coming to work for us, you will be part of a culture that celebrates diversity and inclusion. We are committed to maintaining a workplace where everyone feels valued and where we show respect, integrity and honesty.


EML provides career opportunities and great employee benefits, including:


  • A diverse and collaborative team culture like no other
  • Flexibility to work from home to support work/life balance
  • A corporate wellbeing program with discounted health insurance and gym membership
  • Generous discounts from over 350 retailers through our RewardsHub program
  • Comprehensive learning and development opportunities to help you reach your full potential
  • Access to support and counselling services with work or personal matters, through our Employee Assistance Program
  • Companywide events to stay connected and celebrate success
  • Entitlement to annual company incentive scheme + salary reviews
  • Up to 16 weeks paid parental leave, plus super


We value our people and are committed to supporting our employees by investing in their professional development and providing generous employee benefits. If this position is of interest to you, please apply now.

Greystar is the largest operator of apartments in the United States, managing over one million units/beds globally. Across its platforms, Greystar has nearly $79 billion of assets under management, including over $34 billion of development assets and over $36.5 billion of regulatory assets under management. Greystar was founded by Bob Faith in 1993 to become a provider of world-class service in the rental residential real estate business. To learn more, visit .

JOB DESCRIPTION SUMMARY

This position is responsible for coordinating the community’s marketing, leasing, and renewal strategies to achieve occupancy, revenue, and resident retention goals by performing all activities related to leasing to new residents, providing resident satisfaction throughout the term of the lease, and securing resident lease renewals.

JOB DESCRIPTION

Essential Responsibilities:
• Performs all sales and leasing activities to achieve the community’s revenue and occupancy goals by greeting and qualifying prospects, conducting community tours and showing apartments, processing applications, credit screening, and criminal background checks, preparing the lease and move-in package, and ensuring a smooth resident move-in and lease signing.
• Inspects apartments prior to resident move-in and ensures apartments are in move-in ready condition and schedules any outstanding item to be addressed with the maintenance team.
• Stays informed about current market and competitor conditions that may impact the community’s occupancy and sales results, develops and implements short- and long-term marketing plans and goals to sustain occupancy, and follows the community’s established policies related to concessions, specials, and other programs to boost occupancy.
• Designs and executes marketing activities to create and drive traffic to the community, including implementing resident referral and employer outreach programs, using internet marketing tools (Craigslist, Facebook, e-mail, and other websites), and following other community-specific marketing plans, drives, and special programs.
• Uses the on-site property management software (OneSite, Yardi, etc.) to track apartment availability, record traffic and leasing activities, manage resident and prospect data, and capture critical demographic and other information about existing and future residents.
• Ensures that the community and show units meet the Company’s standards for show quality by daily inspecting the marketing corridor and leasing tour, communicating maintenance and upkeep needs to the community’s maintenance team members, merchandising and ensuring a physically appealing show unit and/or model and amenities, and preparing the leasing office for daily leasing activities.
• Follows-up with prospects and new residents to ensure satisfaction by sending e-mail, thank-you notes, and cards or making telephone calls or other contacts to finalize decisions to lease and/or renew.
• Executes and performs activities in support of the community’s lease renewal program by preparing lease renewal letters and packages for residents, meeting with and contacting renewing residents in advance of move-out dates, and ensuring that lease renewal documents are signed and implemented on time.

title: Grant Project Assistant, Theological Integration Center (ThInC)
description:
Grand Canyon University! One of Arizona’s leading institutions of higher learning. Located in the Valley of Sun in the heart of Phoenix, Arizona, GCU is an institutionally accredited, private, nondenominational Christian University.

The Grant Project Assistant will provide day-to-day operational and administrative support to the Executive Director of the Theological Interdisciplinary Center (ThInC), helping implement a four-year, $1,000,000 initiative to facilitate and support faith integration at GCU. The position will manage schedules and meetings, coordinate communication across colleges, and support logistics for ThInC events, travel, and programming while tracking progress toward project goals. The Assistant will also maintain project materials and records and help launch the ThInC Advisory Board and other initiatives of the Center. This 12-month position also entails responsibility for event planning and coordination, program-related communications, and assistance with networking and donor cultivation.

The Theological Interdisciplinary Center (ThInC) within the GCU College of Theology will serve as a permanent institutional hub that integrates the Christian worldview across all academic disciplines with the outcome of establishing GCU as a national leader in interdisciplinary, Christian higher education.

ThInC is funded by a grant that entails a goal of creating an endowment sufficient to sustain the work of the Center in perpetuity. This position will provide capacity and oversight during the duration of the grant term. The grant commitment dates are Aug 1, 2026, through July 31, 2029.

Location: Main Campus

Schedule: Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm

Benefits: Full benefits portfolio including tuition package

What You Will Do:

  • Provide direct administrative support to the Executive Director (prioritize tasks, manage correspondence, and keep workstreams moving across the grant period).
  • Coordinate calendars, meetings, agendas, and notes for the Center’s Executive Director, internal working groups, and grant-related partners.
  • Processes and prepares institutional data and reports in compliance with required grant reporting.
  • Support development and launch of the ThInC Advisory Board, including scheduling, materials prep, and documentation of actions/follow-ups.
  • Coordinate cross-college communication and collaboration to support interdisciplinary faith integration efforts connected to ThInC.
  • Plan and execute events and programming for the Center, including speaker coordination, space/technology needs, hospitality, and travel coordination when applicable.
  • Manages CRM data for potential donors and advisory board members.
  • Manage content, communications, and interactions for relevant webpages, social media, and email campaigns in support of Center initiatives.
  • Track progress toward grant activities and outcomes by collecting updates, documenting milestones, and flagging risks or delays for the Executive Director.
  • Maintain organized grant and program records (project files, contact lists, event documentation, outputs/products, and other required documentation).
  • Assist with annual grant reporting requirements by compiling drafts and supporting documentation for required narrative and financial reports (including tracking how funds were used and what was accomplished).
  • Support budget/expense tracking and grant compliance practices, including maintaining documentation needed for expenditures and reimbursements tied to grant-funded activities.
  • Support implementation of key ThInC initiatives outlined in the proposal (e.g., faculty/staff development and other planned activities), coordinating logistics and communications to ensure timely execution.
  • Serve as a first point of contact for routine inquiries from faculty, staff, speakers, and partners; route requests to the Executive Director and ensure timely follow-up.
  • Tracks and records grant-related expenses in support of Program Director, Barnabas events, invited speakers, church relations efforts, and training initiatives.
  • Assist with drafting and distributing announcements, invitations, event reminders, and internal updates tied to ThInC activities and grant deliverables.
  • Help build simple workflows and tracking tools (e.g., shared timelines, task trackers, templates) to improve consistency in scheduling, documentation, and reporting.
  • Other duties as assigned.

What You Will Have:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in a discipline related to theological studies is preferred, but other baccalaureate degrees may be acceptable pending relevant experience.
  • Work experience in an educational environment supporting theological and ministerial studies or church-based ministerial experience.
  • Must be able to sign and teach in accordance with the university’s Doctrinal Statement, Ethical Positions Statement and the College of Theology Covenant.
  • Must pass pre-employment background investigations.

Why work at GCU:

  • Exceptional workplace benefits include medical, dental, vision, life and disability insurance, flexible spending accounts, a 401K savings plan
  • Generous time off plan and 11 paid holidays
  • Paid time off to volunteer in the community or at GCU sponsored events
  • We also offer full-time employees, their spouses, and dependent children an Education Tuition Discount Program

title: Compliance and Risk Officer
description:
Job Description

Are you looking for your next opportunity?

Sompo has a unique opportunity for a Compliance and Risk Officer in our Legal & Compliance team.


Location: This position will be based out of our Toronto, Canada office. We strive for collaboration, which is why we offer a work environment where our employees thrive and develop long-lasting careers.


Our business, your impact, our opportunity:

What you’ll be doing:

Compliance Management and Regulatory Affairs Support:

  • Support the maintenance, execution, and enhancement of Regulatory Compliance and Policy Frameworks, including managing related tools.
  • Execute obligations under OSFI and other regulatory guidance including OSFI E-13 Regulatory Compliance Management.
  • Monitor legislative and regulatory changes, assess impacts, and communicate compliance requirements to stakeholders.
  • Lead compliance monitoring, testing, and the Ethidex review process to ensure adherence to policies and regulations.
  • Promote an ethical-based culture by developing and advising the first line of defence/business units with respect to policies (i.e. their adoption, development, implementation and maintenance), practical guidance, training, relevant controls, and processes for mitigation of risks.
  • Assess compliance risks in business activities (e.g., claims, distribution) through audits and reviews, addressing issues promptly.
  • Prepare and present compliance reports with metrics and insights for senior management and governance committees. Ensure that relevant stakeholders are informed, understand and support Compliance activities and prioritization.
  • Assist with regulatory disclosures (e.g., CCIR Annual Market Conduct Survey) and coordinate responses to regulatory requests.
  • Assist with privacy compliance (e.g., DSARs, DPIAs) and oversee sanctions screening, ensuring adherence to all regulatory requirements.

Risk Management:

  • Work with the North America CRO to oversee implementation of Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) frameworks including risk identification, assessment, monitoring, reporting, and mitigation, across financial, operational, climate, IT, cyber security, model risk and third-party risks.
  • Design and implement processes to identify, assess, and mitigate organizational risks, including the ORSA and Earthquake Data Exposure filings.
  • Assist with documenting the organization's risk register and risk appetite framework and statements and integrate it into business decision-making.
  • Establish Manage risk reporting procedures and communicate risks to senior management, governance committees, and stakeholders.
  • Collaborate with internal teams to assess business activities, address compliance risks, and integrate risk requirements into operations.
  • Engage with relevant internal / external partners, and provide Risk input to support the timely preparation, review and challenge of Branch capital requirements.
  • Execute obligations under OSFI and other regulatory guidance including E-21 Operational Risk & Resiliency. Support the identification, assessment, escalation, and remediation of operational risk events, control deficiencies, and emerging risks, providing challenge and guidance to the first line.
  • Promote a strong risk culture by providing risk advice, challenge, and education to the business. Share insights and recommendations from compliance risk assessments and assurance activities to drive continuous improvement.

The role is expected to focus predominantly on Compliance and Regulatory Affairs Support (approximately 70%), alongside Risk Management responsibilities (approximately 30%), with regular overlap between the two functions.


What you’ll bring:

  • Extensive experience in compliance and risk management roles in the insurance industry (5+ years).
  • Bachelor’s degree or designations in Risk Management, Finance, Business, Law, or a related discipline; relevant professional qualifications highly regarded.
  • Strong leadership and strategic planning skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities.
  • Advanced knowledge of regulatory frameworks, risk management practices, and compliance oversight tools (e.g., Ethidex).
  • Knowledge of enterprise risk management and operational risk frameworks, with the ability to implement them pragmatically in an agile business environment.
  • Proven ability to design and implement compliance training and awareness programs.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across teams and with senior management.
  • Proficiency in data analysis, reporting, and risk assessment methodologies.

Salary Range: $120,000 – $150,000. Actual compensation for this role will depend on several factors including the cost of living associated with your work location, your qualifications, skills, competencies, and relevant experience.

title: Mechatronics & Robotics Tech
description:

About MMS

title: Press Room, Set Up & Operate - 3rd Shift
description:
The TSUBAKI name is synonymous with excellence in quality, dependability, and customer service. U.S. Tsubaki Automotive, LLC is an international tier-one supplier of high-speed chain drive systems to the automotive industry.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities: The essential duties and responsibilities of this job are included but not limited to this job description – other tasks may be assigned and expected to be performed.

  • Perform final inspection on parts when lots are completed, record lot and charge number into logbooks to ensure traceability, and position into parts baskets in proper order on the regular carts.
  • Determine feed length and shut height of ram, and adjust miss-feed and stock thickness indicators, air or mechanical knock-out devices where ranging from 100 to 200 tons, for the purpose of blanking and piercing timing chain side plates, from coil and/or bar stock.
  • Possess basic knowledge and understanding of production tooling, which consists of multiple cavity steel and carbide dyes, understanding of related process equipment such as feeds, scrap cutters, stock straighteners, etc.
  • Obtain raw materials from storage location, utilizing FIFO, and move to temporary storage area next to machine.
  • Report all work performed on labor reporting forms as required.
  • Work from drawings, route sheets and instructions, select proper tooling, equipment and materials for the job, and remove or insert any removable sections as necessitated by individual job requirements.
  • Make necessary adjustments of press feeds. Adjust safety devices furnished as a part of the operation.
  • Secure necessary production gauges and checking devices for the specific job requirements.
  • Determine when dyes need sharpening, or repair.
  • Diagnose and remedy malfunctions to tools and equipment.
  • Perform first piece inspection and begin production run on parts per work and inspection standards.
  • Follow inspection standards (SPC) and perform all the required steps in the process inspection.
  • Record tool life, heat, and coil numbers, and other tractability information into control books. Store tooling and accessories into designated areas.
  • Provide for minor maintenance of equipment and preventative maintenance as specified in PM sheets.
  • Requires sufficient knowledge of mechanisms and tooling to maintain close tolerance on a variety of similar operations and work specifications.
  • Maintain work area and equipment in a clean and orderly condition and follow standard safety regulations.
  • Detect faulty operation or defective material and report these and other unusual conditions to group leader or supervisor.
  • Perform other similar and associated duties as required or directed.

JOB TITLE: Maintenance Technician

BASE RATE PER HOUR: $31.30/hour

SHIFT: 3rd Shift

JOB SUMMARY/ JOB DUTIES:

The Facilities Maintenance Technician is responsible for maintaining equipment and facilities to operate in the safest and most productive condition, supporting continuous improvement, production strategies and plant reliability of equipment and building systems.

.

  • Understands and adheres to governmental regulatory programs and policies. These may include but are not limited to: National Electrical Code, Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Uniform Building Code (UBC) and local government environmental agency policies.
  • Practices and complies with all plant and maintenance department safety procedures, including but not limited to: Lock-Out - Tag-Out; Arc Flash and Hot Work Permits.
  • Understands the concept of Permit Required Confined Spaces and assists with proper alternate entry of re-classified confined spaces when necessary.
  • Follows all applicable good manufacturing practices (GMP's) for area assigned.
  • Maintains and uses appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) in accordance with Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), food handling before and after equipment inspection and repair activities.
  • Attends classes, seminars, and in-house training as needed to maintain skill level with changes in the industry.
  • Makes improvements and suggestions to optimize maintenance program.
  • Executes and document planned and unplanned work findings and data during shift via computerized maintenance management system (CMMS).
  • Repairs and installation of parts, tools and equipment. Fabricates or modifies machines, tools, or equipment to manufacture new products or improve existing products.
  • Performs Preventative Maintenance (PM), inspections, corrective repairs, special projects/equipment rebuilds
  • Performs execution and resolution of equipment breakdowns/repairs.
  • Leverages methodologies including, but not limited to: root cause analysis (RCA), break down failure analysis (BDA) and cause maps to identify and resolve equipment issues.
  • Utilizes predictive maintenance technologies to identify failures and takes correct follow-up actions. Predictive maintenance technologies include ultrasound, thermal imaging, oil analysis, and vibration analysis.
  • Documents the cause of the failure and works with maintenance team, planner, supervisor, or other team members to take action to prevent a reoccurrence of the failure.
  • Understands and interprets technical documents and diagrams which include but are not limited to: factory manuals, blueprints, schematics, Single Line Electrical Drawings, mechanical and electrical equipment schematics, pneumatics, hydraulics, and Process and Instrumentation Diagrams (P&ID’s), and etc.
  • Maintains and repairs facility/utility systems such as mechanical, electrical, building systems, water heater/boiler, steam, chilling system, electric power, gas, or compressed air required for operations.
  • Executes PMs and repairs to Heating, Ventilation and Air Conditioning (HVAC) systems, refrigeration, instrumentation, elevator maintenance, painting, plumbing, carpentry, grounds keeping and mechanical repairs - pumps, motors systems.
  • May be required to perform tests, repair and replacement of fire alarm, fire sprinkler, smoke detector, emergency and exit sign lighting system and report any malfunctions to supervisor.
  • Repairs, replaces and/or rebuilds plumbing fixtures and connections.
  • Cleans and replaces traps, drains, vents and drain lines, faucets, and toilets, basic wall board repairs, including wall board installation.
  • Handles plant waste, both hazardous and non-hazardous, in a manner which will ensure compliance with local, state, federal, and EPA regulations.
  • May perform other duties as required.

EDUCATION/EXPERIENCE:

High School Diploma or GED; a minimum of 2 years of experience in a manufacturing facility performing mechanical and electrical inspections, troubleshooting and repairs; pass plant specific maintenance test required.

Preferred Qualifications: Some college or formal technical school education with demonstrated aptitude and skills in mechanical, electrical, pneumatic, carpentry, plumbing, and welding techniques. Ability to deal with problems involving variables in standardized situations, along with two years in food manufacturing environment experience

Sitting: Occasionally Standing: Continuously Walking: Continuously

Driving: Seldomly Using hands: Continuously Climbing: Frequently
Stooping, Kneeling: Frequently Talking, Hearing: Frequently Tasting, Smelling: Seldom


Weight:

Up to 10 lbs.: Frequently Up to 25 lbs.: Frequently Up to 50 lbs.: Frequently

More than 50 lbs. with assistance: Occasionally More than 100 lbs.: Seldom/Never

WORK ENVIRONMENT:

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly exposed to moving mechanical parts. The employee is frequently exposed to wet and/or humid conditions. The employee is occasionally exposed to high, precarious places; fumes or airborne particles; toxic or caustic chemicals; and outside weather conditions. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

title: ASL Interpreter
description:
Position Summary

The ASL Interpreter provides in-person American Sign Language interpreting to deaf and hard-of-hearing students in grades 3 through 12, substituting for district staff interpreters on an as-needed basis. The interpreter facilitates full access to classroom instruction, school activities, and communication between students, teachers, and staff.

Key Responsibilities

• Provide accurate, real-time ASL interpretation during classroom instruction, assemblies, and other school activities as assigned

• Accept assignments only when scheduled through the authorized district process; do not self-schedule or accept assignments from unauthorized parties

• Arrive punctually and be prepared for each assignment, including familiarity with subject matter and any student-specific communication needs where provided

• Maintain professional, age-appropriate conduct and communication with students in grades 3–12

• Maintain confidentiality of student information consistent with FERPA and school policy

• Coordinate with classroom teachers and school staff to support the student's access to instruction

• Document services provided (dates, times, locations, hours) to support vendor invoicing

• Notify the scheduling coordinator promptly of any inability to fulfill an assigned engagement

• Accept that the district may request replacement of an interpreter for a given assignment at its discretion

Qualifications & Requirements

• Demonstrated qualification as an ASL interpreter meeting applicable state requirements for educational interpreting (e.g., state-recognized certification or quality-assurance screening, as required by the state Department of Education)

• Prior experience interpreting in a K-12 or educational setting strongly preferred; experience with the grades 3–12 age range a plus

• Must pass both an FBI fingerprint-based background check and a state-level criminal background check prior to placement; clearance valid two (2) years and subject to renewal

• No felony or other disqualifying-crime conviction or plea, per district policy

• Reliable transportation; ability to report to assigned school buildings within the district

• Strong interpersonal and communication skills; comfortable working with school-age students and staff

• Must hold and maintain any applicable state licenses/certifications; required to self-report any lapse, revocation, or suspension within one business day

Additional Notes

This is a contract/substitute position with no guaranteed minimum hours — assignment volume varies by district need throughout the school year. The district's identity and specific building locations will be shared with candidates upon engagement.

title: Ophthalmic Research Technician/Associate
description:
An exciting opportunity for an Ophthalmic Research Technician/Associate is available at the New England College of Optometry (NECO). We are seeking a motivated individual with experience in ophthalmic testing and/or clinical research to help us lead studies on myopia at NECO’s Children’s Vision Lab.


The research technician/associate will work closely with the principal investigator and the interdisciplinary team in one or more NIH funded studies. The primary study is PICNIC, a longitudinal study in children that aims to understand the intrinsic mechanisms whereby some children develop myopia. This information will be critical for the design of effective myopia prevention and control treatments. The team involves experts in pediatric optometry, neuroscience, vision science and electrophysiology. We use a variety of clinical and laboratory research methodologies, including psychophysics, aberrometry, gaze-contingent eye-tracking and biometry.


The salary for this position is $70,000. This is a full-time position funded for a minimum of 1.5 years (funding is available for a minimum of 5 years). Schedule is somewhat flexible and requires regular in person work, some early evenings and occasional Saturdays. NECO is an independent institution renowned as a leading myopia research and clinical center.


The successful candidate will help the team perform the ophthalmic and vision science tests, analyze data, and participate in data dissemination, all in a collaborative environment. A successful candidate will be a self-starter who possesses keen attention to detail and an ability to learn complex techniques and protocols quickly. Excellent interpersonal skills are necessary.


Responsibilities include:


Perform or assist with ophthalmic and vision-related testing in children, including but not limited to:

  • Conducting testing in pediatric participants following standardized study protocols.
  • Operating ophthalmic instruments and research equipment after appropriate training.
  • Performing refraction-related measurements, ocular biometry, and other vision assessments, as required by the study.
  • Ensuring high-quality, repeatable measurements across study visits.
  • Working effectively with children to obtain reliable data while maintaining participant comfort and cooperation.
  • Preparing participants for testing and explaining procedures in an age-appropriate manner.
  • Documenting testing outcomes accurately and promptly.
  • Identifying and reporting testing issues, unreliable data, equipment problems, or protocol deviations to the study team.

Support research data management and processing, including:

  • Entering, checking, and organizing data. Reviewing datasets for completeness, accuracy, and consistency.
  • Assisting with data formatting, and processing for analysis.
  • Maintaining organized records of study visits, testing outcomes, and data files.
  • Assisting with preparation of data summaries, tables, and figures as needed.
  • Communicating with investigators and study staff regarding missing, questionable, or inconsistent data.
  • Helping prepare materials for presentations, abstracts, reports, and manuscripts when appropriate.

Assist with study operations, including:

  • Scheduling or coordinating study visits as needed.
  • Communicating professionally with children, parents, and study staff.
  • Ensuring that participants complete testing in the appropriate order and within the expected timeframe.
  • Supporting a child-friendly testing environment.
  • Maintaining confidentiality of participant information.
  • Following IRB-approved protocols and institutional research policies.
  • Assisting with inventory, calibration, maintenance, and organization of study equipment and supplies.
  • Recruitment activities, including organizing local school screenings and community outreach.

Requirements

  • Minimum of bachelor’s degree in a relevant, vision or ophthalmic, field.
  • Previous experience in ophthalmic, optometric, or vision related testing.
  • Experience working with pediatric patients or research participants.
  • Ability to interact effectively and patiently with children.
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to follow standardized protocols.
  • Ability to collect accurate and reliable measurements, recognizing when data may be unreliable.
  • Comfort learning new ophthalmic instruments and research procedures.
  • Strong computer data entry skills, including Microsoft Excel. Experience with REDCap is a plus. Experience with statistical analyses is a plus.
  • Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple study-related tasks.
  • Good written and verbal communication skills.
  • Previous experience in clinical research is recommended but not required.
  • Previous experience in patient care or recruitment of research participants are a plus.
  • Ability to work independently while also collaborating with investigators and research staff.
  • Commitment to maintaining participant confidentiality and following research compliance requirements.

**Bilingual proficiency (English/Spanish or English/Mandarin) is preferred but not required.

title: Senior Vice President, Professional Services
description:
Purpose

The Senior Vice President, Professional Services leads Clinisys’ global Professional Services organization, accountable for the successful delivery of all implementation programs, solution deployment, and value‑realization activities. The role ensures that Clinisys delivers consistent, high‑quality services that accelerate time‑to‑value, drive customer adoption, and contribute to sustainable revenue growth. As a member of the Executive Leadership Team, the SVP shapes the future of Clinisys’ services strategy by embedding AI, analytics, automation, and intelligent workflows into delivery practices and customer engagement.

Clinisys’ AI Philosophy:

Building an AI‑first organization is central to Clinisys’ purpose and the impact we deliver. As a global provider of intelligent diagnostic informatics solutions, we build AI‑enabled, cloud‑based platforms to enhance diagnostic workflows across healthcare, life sciences, and public health. By applying intelligent technology thoughtfully and responsibly, we help laboratories and testing environments operate more effectively, generate meaningful insights at scale, and ultimately support healthier and safer communities. Operating across more than 30 countries, Clinisys expects all colleagues—regardless of role or function—to work confidently with AI‑enabled tools, apply digital and analytical thinking, and continuously adapt as technologies evolve, must drive an AI-first sense of purpose and urgency.

Essential Functions:

Leadership & Strategy

  • Set the strategic direction for Clinisys’ global Professional Services organization, including service delivery models, capacity planning, utilization strategies, and global operating frameworks.

  • Define a multi‑year roadmap for transforming Professional Services through AI‑enabled delivery, automation, workflow intelligence, and data‑driven decision‑making

  • Align Professional Services strategy with broader company goals, product strategy, and regional market expectations to ensure repeatable, scalable delivery across all geographies.

  • Establish a global services governance model covering delivery quality, methodology compliance, engagement risk management, and customer‑facing operational cadence.

Professional Services Delivery Excellence

  • Lead the end‑to‑end delivery of all implementation and deployment programs, ensuring predictable execution, high‑quality outcomes, and customer value achievement.

  • Deploy AI‑based tools to improve project health scoring, risk prediction, quality assurance checks, and real‑time project visibility.

  • Drive adoption of AI‑assisted implementation accelerators, including automated configuration recommendations, intelligent test automation, and data migration validation tools.

  • Oversee global project portfolio management, ensuring visibility of risks, budgets, timelines, scope, and customer escalations across all active programs.

  • Define and enforce disciplined delivery lifecycle processes including scoping, estimating, contracting, resource allocation, delivery execution, project closure, and post‑go‑live adoption support.

  • Monitor and improve services performance metrics including utilization, realization, backlog management, delivery margins, on‑time/on-budget delivery, and customer value attainment.

Commercial & Financial Management

  • Own services revenue forecasting, backlog growth, margin performance, and overall contribution to company financial targets.

  • Partner with Sales, Product, and Finance to develop AI‑enhanced scoping, pricing, and commercial governance tools.

  • Identify and develop scalable, profitable service offerings—including AI‑powered services—that strengthen adoption, compliance, interoperability, and operational efficiency.

  • Identify new revenue streams, expansion opportunities, and value‑added services to drive growth and customer adoption.

Customer Outcomes & Strategic Engagement

  • Ensure implementation programs deliver measurable, outcome‑based value aligned to customer objectives, regulatory needs, and operational goals.

  • Build deep executive‑level relationships with strategic customers, acting as a trusted advisor and ensuring delivery excellence throughout the lifecycle.

  • Integrate AI‑driven change management and readiness tools to support customer adoption, workflow optimization, and continuous value realization.

  • Lead the development of post‑implementation transition processes that support smooth customer handoff to operational teams, maximizing adoption and long‑term satisfaction.

People & Talent Leadership

  • Build and scale a world‑class global Professional Services team with strong delivery leadership, Program Management, Consulting, Training, and PMO capability.

  • Drive workforce planning, skills development, and resource management to ensure the right talent mix aligns to customer demand and growth strategies.

  • Develop learning pathways that elevate AI literacy, data‑driven consulting skills, analytical reasoning, and delivery innovation across the team

  • Foster a performance‑driven culture with clear expectations for delivery excellence, customer advocacy, accountability, and continuous improvement.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  • Successful experience working across all levels in internal and external organizations to achieve goals.

  • Strong demonstrated emotional intelligence.

  • Demonstrated excellent written and verbal communication skills that include presentation skills, one on one coaching and exceptional ability to listen.

  • Ability to effectively lead, mentor, and coach teams and individuals, and impact organizational effectiveness.

  • Proven ability to meet deadlines, budget, and plans.

  • Drive to lead and execute on multiple, critical projects simultaneously

  • Effective executive presence

  • Sense of business urgency in delivering on goals/quotas.

  • Creativity in identifying new opportunities.

Education and Experience:

  • Bachelor's degree in business or computer science; or equivalent relevant experience required.

  • 10 years’ experience leading large scale software implementation required.

  • 10 years’ experience in healthcare required; lab experience preferred.

  • 10 years’ proven track record of successfully driving profitability and utilization.

  • Process improvement experience required.

Supervisory Responsibilities:

  • Supervise a globally dispersed team of 4-7 direct reports and responsible for 500-600 indirect reports

Benefits:

Our benefits are designed to help you move forward in your career, and in areas of your life outside of work. From health and wellness benefits, 401 (k) Savings Plan, stock incentive programs, paid time off, parental leave, and tuition assistance, we've got you covered with our total rewards package. For part-timers, your coverage will vary as you may be eligible for some of these benefits depending on your individual circumstances.

The starting pay range for a candidate selected for this position is generally within the range of $240,000 - $300,000 for annual base salary. The successful candidate’s actual pay will be based on various factors, such as work location, qualifications, and experience, so the actual starting pay may be above or below this range.

Physical Requirements:

  • Work is performed in a normal office setting with minimal exposure to health or safety hazards

  • Substantial time is spent working on a computer.

  • International and Domestic travel is required, as much as 25% - 50%.

Onboarding

As part of our onboarding process, all new employees will be required to attend/travel to the office on their first day of employment (Raleigh, NC / Tucson, AZ / Indianapolis, IN). This requirement is essential for onboarding activities, including identity verification, completion of necessary documentation, receiving your IT equipment, introductions to key team members, and orientation to Clinisys policies and procedures.

Clinisys’ Commitment to Equal Opportunity:

Clinisys is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, physical or mental disability, genetic factors, military/veteran status or other characteristics protected by law.

General Guidance:

This job description is meant to provide an accurate depiction of tasks and accountabilities that are most often associated with this role. While we strive to provide an accurate depiction, nothing in this description restricts the company from changing, reassigning, expanding or reducing scope of accountabilities and is subject to change at any time.

title: Cost Management Lead
description:
Cost Management Lead – Strategic Portfolio

Location –Blantyre office (with hybrid work pattern, 3 days in office per week)

Salary from £66,000 - £80,000 + annual bonus (up to 20%) and family private medical cover.

Permanent | Full-time – 37 hours per week

Closing date – 25th September 2026

Help us create a better future, quicker!

SP Energy Networks is delivering one of the UK's largest electricity network investment programmes, with £12 billion being invested over the next five years. As part of this transformation, our SPT Strategic Projects business will deliver a £2.4 billion portfolio of major transmission infrastructure projects across Scotland.

We're looking for a Strategic Portfolio Cost Management Lead to provide functional leadership for cost management across this portfolio. Reporting to the Head of PMO, you'll lead cost control, forecasting and performance reporting activities, ensuring robust financial governance across complex, high-value EPC projects.

This is a unique opportunity to influence some of the UK's most significant energy infrastructure projects while playing a key role in Scotland's transition to Net Zero.

What you'll be doing

  • Lead and continuously improve cost management processes, standards and governance across the Strategic Portfolio.
  • Own and maintain the Portfolio Cost Breakdown Structure (CBS) and related cost management systems.
  • Oversee forecasting, earned value analysis, cost reporting and month-end financial processes.
  • Provide portfolio-wide cost performance insights, identifying trends, risks and opportunities.
  • Work closely with Planning, Risk, Procurement and Project Management teams to align cost and schedule baselines.
  • Monitor contractor performance against budgets and KPIs.
  • Lead the Value of Work Done (VoWD) process, including accruals and prepayments.
  • Recruit, mentor and develop Cost Engineers across the portfolio.
  • Drive the adoption of the Cost Management playbook and support the transition to S/4 HANA.
  • Ensure effective budget control through the approval of purchase requisitions and purchase orders.

What you'll bring

  • Significant experience in Cost Management on major EPC or infrastructure projects.
  • Strong understanding of cost control, estimating, forecasting and earned value management.
  • Experience managing complex cost structures across large, multi-disciplinary programmes.
  • Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to influence at all levels.
  • Knowledge of NEC3/NEC4 contracts.
  • Proficiency in SAP/S4 HANA, Power BI and Microsoft Office.
  • Experience leading and developing cost management teams.
  • Degree qualification in Engineering, Finance, Quantity Surveying or a related discipline is desirable but not essential.
  • Energy sector experience is beneficial, but we welcome applicants from other infrastructure sectors.
  • Willingness to travel across the UK as required.

What's in it for you

As well as an attractive salary which is reviewed annually, you can also enjoy a number of other benefits. With our pension scheme, we'll double match your contribution up to a company contribution of 10%.

At ScottishPower, we believe it's the little things we do in life that make a big difference. From helping you look after your family's wellbeing, save for your future and take personal steps for climate action -- our benefits are designed to help you do just that - so that you have everything you need to take care of your world -- today and tomorrow.

That's why our benefits include:

  • 36 days annual leave
  • Holiday Purchase - perfect your work/life balance with extra annual leave
  • Equity Plans
  • Payroll Giving and Charity Matched Funding
  • Technology Vouchers - save more and spread the cost of your technology purchases
  • Electric Vehicle Schemes - to help you transition to green/clean driving
  • Cycle to Work scheme and Public Transport Season Ticket Loans
  • Healthcare benefit options including: Dental Insurance, Private Medical Insurance, Health Cash Plan and annual Health Assessments
  • Life Assurance (4x salary)
  • Access to Savesmart financial wellbeing assistance
  • Plus shopping, leisure, restaurant and gym discounts, and unique employee deals on travel insurance and more

Why SP Energy Networks

SP Energy Networks is part of the Iberdrola Group, one of the world's largest integrated utility companies and a world leader in wind energy. We keep electricity flowing to homes and businesses through Central and Southern Scotland, North Wales and in the North West of England. We operate over 4000km of cables and lines that make-up the transmission network - infrastructure like wind farms into the electricity system. It's a role that puts us right at the heart of Scotland's goal to be Net Zero by 2044. And we're taking it very seriously.

We're investing £12 billion into our transmission network, directly enabling the rapid growth needed in renewable energy. With diverse opportunities across our businesses and a focus on investing in our own internal talent, ScottishPower can offer people real career opportunities that meet personal and professional goals, in a global organisation.

Inclusion, diversity, and a social purpose are at the heart of everything we do. These values bring us into a stronger, more sustainable business with direct links to the communities we serve. It takes all types of people to build a large-scale business like ours, so whatever your background, you'll fit right in.

We are dedicated to providing reasonable adjustments in our recruiting processes for candidates with disabilities, long term conditions, mental health conditions, or who are neurodivergent or require pregnancy-related support. If you need assistance, please reach out to careers@scottishpower.com.

Mobility
