title: Grinding, Set Up & Operate - 3rd Shift
description:
The TSUBAKI name is synonymous with excellence in quality, dependability and customer service. U.S. Tsubaki Automotive, LLC is an international tier-one supplier of high-speed chain drive systems to the automotive industry.

The Grinding, Setup and Operate position is responsible for running the centerless grinders requiring the planning of duties to perform rough and form grind operations on a variety of similar parts of various materials to meet quality and quantity standards.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities: The essential duties and responsibilities of this job are included but not limited to this job description – other tasks may be assigned and expected to be performed.

  • Work from schedules, prints, specifications and general instructions of department supervisor. Set-ups exacting but not difficult to maintain.
  • Determine operating sequence and select and mount wheels in machine. Set speeds and feeds as prescribed for the type of material and finish requirements.
  • Dress and true up wheels as required.
  • Maintain close tolerances for size and concentricity.
  • Test equipment after set-up to determine conformity to quality and quantity standards. Make any necessary adjustments.
  • Perform all quality checks as defined in the inspection standard.
  • Move and handle materials to provide for continuous operation. Load parts in automatic feed mechanisms and make minor adjustments.
  • Diagnose and remedy ordinary production problems.
  • Provide for minor maintenance of equipment, tooling and accessories.
  • Use various hand tools.
  • Oil parts as necessary; weigh, count, and dispose of as required. Record production, time, and other data. Remove sludge from magnetic separator as required.
  • Responsible for maintaining production schedules, quality control records, chain assembly records, shipping charge numbers, preventive maintenance plans, and the Kan-Ban tool control system for all tools in the department and refers any unusual problems to the departmental supervisor.
  • Preventive maintenance schedules need to be completed timely and accurately each day, week, and month. It is essential to keep the equipment running properly.
  • Work from schedules, prints, specifications and general instructions of department supervisor. Set-ups exacting but not difficult to maintain.
  • Maintain work area and equipment in a clean and orderly condition and follow standard safety regulations.
  • Detect faulty operation or defective material and report these and other unusual conditions to superior.
  • Perform other similar and associated duties as required or directed.
  • Maintain a good shift to shift transition, communicating equipment issues and parts status and other issues to the incoming operator.

title: Staff & Office Management Lead
description:
Staff & Office Management Lead

The Opportunity:

The Staff & Office Management Lead will serve as the coordinator for office personnel onboarding, administrative readiness, business process improvement, and daily office operations for our DoW customer.

This individual will be responsible for ensuring newly assigned personnel are effectively integrated into the organization, staff complete required administrative and training actions, and personnel have the equipment, facility access, and support required to execute daily operations. They will also track staff travel, organize meetings with DoW and industry representatives, and track the progress and completion of tasks assigned by senior leaders in the office.

Through these responsibilities, the individual in this role supports a responsive, organized, and mission-ready office environment.

What You'll Do:

  • Analyze current office workflows and administrative practices to identify inefficiencies, gaps, and opportunities for improvement.

  • Recommend, implement, and sustain business process improvements that increase efficiency, accountability, responsiveness, and staff support.

  • Develop and maintain standard operating procedures (SOPs), continuity materials, and recurring office management processes.

  • Standardize routine administrative processes where appropriate to improve consistency and reduce delays.

  • Lead and manage office onboarding processes for newly assigned military, civilian, and contractor personnel.

  • Develop, maintain, and execute onboarding checklists, in-processing procedures, and orientation materials.

  • Track and monitor completion of required administrative actions, training requirements, and office-specific onboarding tasks.

  • Ensure personnel obtain required access to facilities, workspaces, systems, equipment, and other mission-essential resources.

  • Coordinate with internal and external support offices on badges, workspace setup, equipment issuance, accounts, and related administrative support requirements.

  • Organize and coordinate key meetings, including engagements with DoW and industry representatives, including managing meeting logistics, attendee lists, agendas, background materials, and follow-up actions, as required.

  • Serve as the central point of contact for routine office management and staff support issues.

Join us. The world can’t wait.

You Have:

  • 3+ years of experience in office management, administrative operations, executive support, or staff coordination

  • 2+ years of experience supporting a Department of War (DoW), joint, headquarters, or government office environment

  • Experience developing or maintaining standard operating procedures (SOPs), continuity books, administrative guides, or office process documentation

Nice If You Have:

description:
The Position:

Videographer

Job Summary:

The Office of Communications and Marketing (OCM) at Muhlenberg College seeks a creative and engaged video storyteller. This professional will play a key role in highlighting the people, moments, and experiences of the college through dynamic and compelling video storytelling. As part of the communications and marketing team, the videographer will create energetic and inspirational content that promotes the Muhlenberg brand story, supports marketing efforts, and complements the department’s written and visual media.

Reporting to the director of strategic content, this individual will join a team that partners with admissions, academic programs, advancement, alumni, and the president to share the value and impact of the Muhlenberg experience. The videographer will profile students, faculty, staff, alumni, and others across the programs and experiences that make Muhlenberg a vibrant community. The videographer’s work will support messaging with the college’s prospective and existing community, including through promotion across social media and the college's website.

Characteristic Responsibilities:

Identify and develop stories that support Muhlenberg’s strategic priorities

  • Plan, shoot, and edit short-form and long-form video that supports communications and marketing initiatives
  • Contribute to a storytelling team through video that supports and enhances written and visual media
  • Work with on-campus teams and contracted firms for large-scale video initiatives

Collaborate with partners on campus

  • Work closely with OCM staff (including but not limited to the social media manager, athletics communications staff, and the director of strategic content) on idea generation and execution
  • Work with partners in admissions, advancement, academic and student life, and beyond to produce video for events and other initiatives as needed
  • Create and build a team of student videographers to assist with authentic portrayals of the Muhlenberg College liberal arts experience

Manage a flexible schedule, with occasional travel and weekend or evening events

  • A presence at orientation, Red Door Weekend, commencement, and other key college events is required
  • Occasional travel to capture footage and tell stories of students and alumni is required
  • May perform other duties as assigned.

Institutional Collaboration:

  • Partners with OCM colleagues, senior staff, faculty, and colleagues in admissions, advancement, graduate and continuing education, student life, and beyond to advance institutional priorities and support the college’s mission.
  • Engages regularly with faculty, staff, students, and other campus constituencies to understand needs, coordinate services, and strengthen collaboration.
  • Collaborates on institutional initiatives and special projects that require video support.
  • Builds productive relationships across the college and contributes to an inclusive campus environment where individuals are respected, valued, and supported.

Muhlenberg offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package that includes generous paid holidays, including three days off for Thanksgiving and an extended winter break between Christmas Eve and New Year’s Day; 22 vacation days per year; sick leave; eight weeks of paid parental leave; Life Sports Center membership; undergraduate and graduate tuition opportunities; medical, dental, and vision coverage; flexible spending accounts; short- and long-term disability coverage; life insurance; and retirement benefits. Eligibility requirements and waiting periods may apply.

As a 501(c)(3) nonprofit institution, Muhlenberg is also a qualifying employer under the federal Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program.

The College & Surrounding Area: Founded in 1848, Muhlenberg College is a private, residential, liberal arts college offering baccalaureate and graduate programs. At Muhlenberg, we are committed to a campus community that ensures students, faculty, and staff of all backgrounds feel welcome, respected, valued and included.
The College provides an intensely challenging, supportive environment centered around a rigorous academic curriculum designed to prepare students for lives of leadership and meaning in a dynamic, global society. The academic program is amplified by a range of innovative programming: comprehensive and intentional residence-life programming, expansive experiential learning requirements, and an innovative coaching program designed to maximize every student’s performance and potential.

Part of eastern Pennsylvania’s scenic Lehigh Valley, Allentown is a diverse city of 125,000, Pennsylvania’s third-largest, located just 60 miles north of Philadelphia and 90 miles west of New York City. The Lehigh Valley, which also includes neighboring cities Bethlehem and Easton, is one of the fastest growing regions in the state and the Northeast, leading Pennsylvania in population growth for people aged 18–34. Home to a vibrant arts scene, extensive parks and recreational opportunities, a rich blend of diverse cuisine, and so much more, visit Life in the Lehigh Valley | Muhlenberg College and check out Allentown here.

  • Demonstrated knowledge of video filming and production
  • Professional experience in independent and collaborative video production, including experience with scripting, interviewing, all aspects of audio and video production, lighting, and post-production
  • Proficiency with Adobe CC, including excellent command of Adobe Premiere, Audition, and After Effects
  • Strong storytelling ability and experience crafting compelling video
  • Ability to create video that delights, entertains, and engages viewers

  • Ability to successfully deploy and promote best practices for video on the web and in social media

  • Exceptional communication skills, including the ability to express creative ideas clearly, concisely, and thoughtfully
  • Demonstrated commitment to fostering an inclusive academic and professional environment where all members of our campus community are respected, valued, and can succeed and thrive

title: Software Development Engineer II , Amazon Web Services (AWS)
description:
The AWS Field Experience (AFX) team builds go-to-market tooling that gives the AWS sales and marketing organization superpowers, helping them focus on customers instead of manual processes. As a Software Development Engineer II on AFX, you will design and deliver the distributed systems that power Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) and approval workflows for the AWS field, the backbone of how deals move from proposal to signed, executed contract.

You will own services that generate contract documents, orchestrate multi-stage approval flows, integrate with e-signature and CLM platforms, and enforce the business rules and gates that keep contracting fast, compliant, and auditable at AWS scale. Large language models are redefining how we support go-to-market functions, from drafting and reviewing contract language to automating approval routing, and this is your chance to help shape that transformation. You will work across the full software development lifecycle, writing high-quality code, contributing to system design, and collaborating with partners across the AWS partner business, deal desk, legal, finance, and solutions architecture teams.


Key job responsibilities
- Design and build distributed services and APIs that power contract lifecycle management and approval workflows for one of the largest field sales organizations in the world, covering the full lifecycle from authoring and approval through execution and operations.

- Develop and optimize approval-flow and workflow-orchestration engines , multi-stage routing, delegation, escalation, and gate enforcement, that keep contracting fast, compliant, and fully auditable.

- Build and maintain integrations with e-signature and CLM platforms (e.g., DocuSign) and Salesforce-based contracting systems, synchronizing contract and account data across systems at scale and improving data quality and coverage.

- Implement LLM-powered workflows, MCPs, and automation that reduce manual effort in contract drafting, review, and approval routing, and that generate actionable insights from complex contracting data.

- Participate actively in code reviews, providing constructive feedback that raises engineering standards, and mentor other engineers through documentation, training, and pairing sessions.

- Identify root causes of operational issues and drive permanent fixes, while collaborating with stakeholders across deal desk, legal, finance, the AWS partner business, and solutions architects to ensure your solutions meet real customer needs.


A day in the life
You start by reviewing pull requests from teammates, offering detailed feedback that helps everyone grow. Mid-morning, you dig into a feature in the approval-flow engine. After lunch, you join a design discussion about how an LLM-powered workflow can auto-draft contract clauses and shorten approval cycles for the field team. Later, you investigate an operational alert on the contract-generation service, trace it to its root cause, and ship a lasting fix. You move between focused coding and cross-team collaboration with partners in deal desk, legal, and the partner business.


About the team
The AFX teams sit within AWS Sales, Marketing, and Global Services and build the infrastructure that supports the sales field and AWS customers at massive scale. This team owns the contracting and approval-workflow platform, the systems that take a deal from proposal to signed, executed contract. Our closest partners span deal desk, legal, finance, the AWS partner business, and solutions architecture organizations. We are investing heavily in LLM-driven tooling and large-scale data processing to redefine how go-to-market and contracting teams operate. If you want to build systems that directly shape how AWS contracts with and engages its customers worldwide, this is the team for you.

title: Data Platform Engineer
description:
This is an opportunity for a Data Platform Engineer within First Orion’s Data Engineering organization. This hands-on role is responsible for implementing, automating, operating, and improving our enterprise data platform, with a primary focus on Databricks running on AWS. The engineer will translate platform architecture and governance standards into reliable infrastructure, deployments, access controls, pipelines, and internal data solutions.

You will work closely with the Data Platform Architect, who sets platform direction, architecture, and company process alignment. The Data Platform Engineer provides implementation expertise, builds according to those designs, and owns the operational quality of the platform. We are looking for a collaborative, self-motivated engineer with strong technical judgment and a commitment to secure, reliable, and maintainable solutions.

What you’ll be doing:

  • Implement, operate, and continuously improve the Databricks platform on AWS
  • Build and maintain Terraform modules for Databricks, AWS infrastructure, Unity Catalog, permissions, and supporting integrations
  • Develop and maintain Databricks Asset Bundles and CI/CD pipelines for repeatable deployments across environments
  • Configure and support workspaces, compute policies, SQL warehouses, workflows, jobs, service principals, and platform permissions
  • Implement Unity Catalog governance, including catalogs, schemas, storage credentials, external locations, ownership, and group-based access
  • Build and support foundational data pipelines using Python, SQL, Apache Spark, Delta Lake, and Databricks workflows
  • Develop lightweight internal applications and governed user-input solutions using approved platform services
  • Monitor platform health, reliability, performance, security, and cost; troubleshoot incidents and complete root-cause analysis
  • Create reusable patterns, automation, runbooks, and self-service capabilities for engineering teams
  • Partner with the Data Platform Architect to validate designs, identify risks, and support production-readiness reviews

What you’ll need:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience
  • 5+ years of experience in data engineering, platform engineering, cloud infrastructure, DevOps, or a related discipline
  • 3+ years of hands-on experience with Databricks and Apache Spark in production environments
  • Strong Terraform experience, including modules, state management, provider configuration, and CI/CD
  • Strong knowledge of Unity Catalog, including securable objects, ownership, privilege inheritance, and governance models
  • Strong AWS experience, particularly IAM, S3, networking, encryption, monitoring, and secure service integration
  • Experience with Databricks Asset Bundles, Git-based development, automated testing, and deployment pipelines
  • Strong Python and SQL skills with working knowledge of PySpark, Delta Lake, and distributed data processing
  • Experience with identity and access management, service principals, groups, least privilege, and SSO/SCIM
  • Experience with platform observability, troubleshooting, incident response, performance tuning, and cost optimization
  • Ability to translate architecture and governance requirements into maintainable code, automation, and operating procedures
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills across architecture, engineering, security, and business teams

Bonus Points:

  • Experience migrating Hive Metastore or DBFS-based workloads to Unity Catalog
  • Experience with Databricks Apps, Streamlit, REST APIs, or lightweight Python applications
  • Databricks or AWS certifications
  • Experience with FinOps, Delta Sharing, AI/ML platforms, or high-scale telecom data systems

Company Benefits:

Balancing the work-life flow is key to health and happiness! That is why we offer one of the most competitive packages in our industry with open PTO, company paid holidays, Flex Fridays and flexible work arrangements. title: Principal Worldwide Specialist Solutions Architect, Agentic AI, Data & AI GTM
description:
Do you thrive in defining technical strategies for new services where the problem space is still being written? Are you energized by the challenge of setting adoption strategy for technology that reimagines how AI agents consume governed context at runtime? Are you ready to become the recognized authority for a service that will shape the future of agentic AI?

We are seeking a Principal Solutions Architect to lead the technical adoption strategy for AWS Context, the organization-wide knowledge graph and agentic context layer for AI agents. This is a formative role where you will define how customers across a segment or territory understand, evaluate, and adopt AWS Context. You will guide customers through AWS Glue Data Catalog building blocks, frame complex agentic use cases across their data estates, and work directly with product teams to shape the service roadmap. Your work will set the technical direction that the entire team executes against, establish mechanisms and reference architectures that raise the bar org-wide, and build the external thought leadership that defines how the market understands agentic context. You will convert the most complex early evaluations into committed adoption, mentor senior Solutions Architects, and create sustained influence well beyond individual customer interactions.

Key job responsibilities
- Set the technical adoption strategy for AWS Context, determining which use cases, industries, and customers to prioritize and orchestrating the evaluation motion other Solutions Architects execute
- Lead the highest-stakes customer engagements personally, framing undefined problem spaces with customer architects and executives, designing agentic solutions that leverage governed context across AWS Glue Data Catalog, Amazon Redshift, Amazon Simple Storage Service, Apache Iceberg, Amazon Athena, Amazon Bedrock knowledge bases, and Lake Formation
- Establish reusable mechanisms, reference architectures, and standards that raise the bar for the team org-wide, codifying what works from field experience into artifacts that accelerate future engagements and ensure consistency
- Influence the AWS Context service roadmap as a strategic partner to product and engineering teams, synthesizing field learnings into succinct business and technical requirements and contributing to early product formation
- Build external technical thought leadership through content creation and speaking engagements that position AWS Context in the market, mentor and develop senior Solutions Architects, and contribute to hiring strategy

A day in the life
A typical day blends strategic direction-setting with hands-on technical leadership on the most complex work. You might refine the adoption strategy for your segment in the morning, prioritizing which agentic use cases and customers to focus on. Then you lead a design session with customer architects and executives, framing how governed context and semantic layers improve agent reasoning across their data estate. Between engagements, you resolve escalated governance and security objections, establish reusable reference architectures for the team, and synthesize field patterns for the service team. You mentor senior Solutions Architects on complex evaluations and prepare external technical content that shapes how the market understands agentic context.

About the team
The customer-facing specialist Solutions Architecture team is the technical engine behind AWS Context adoption. Because the service is evolving toward general availability, we meet customers building agentic applications where they are today: guiding them through the AWS Glue Data Catalog and Amazon Bedrock knowledge bases building blocks available today, proving value against real agent use cases, and capturing the customer interest and requirements that shape the service roadmap. The team owns the evaluation motion across collaborative design sessions, tailored demonstrations, hands-on proofs of concept, and acceleration builds, driving clean handoffs into production onboarding as capabilities become available.

As the Principal Solutions Architect, you set the technical strategy and mechanisms the team operates on. We work closely with sales, service, and product teams, feed field learnings back into the roadmap, and hold a high bar for both technical depth and customer trust. It is a collaborative, high-ownership environment where the most senior architects build the capabilities and standards that make the entire team more effective.

Cost Management & Quantity Surveying:

  • Conduct tender analysis and support procurement processes.

  • Prepare interim valuations, payment certificates, and final accounts.

  • Assess variations, claims, and change orders.

  • Monitor project costs and ensure adherence to approved budgets.


Quality Assurance & Compliance:

  • Develop and implement Quality Assurance/Quality Control (QA/QC) plans.

  • Ensure construction activities comply with approved drawings, specifications, and standards.

  • Conduct site inspections to verify quality of materials and workmanship.

  • Monitor testing of materials (concrete, pipes, fittings, etc.) and verify compliance.

  • Ensure corrective actions are implemented where deficiencies are identified.


Contract & Donor Compliance:

  • Ensure adherence to Nigerian procurement regulations and donor guidelines.

  • Maintain proper documentation for audit and reporting purposes.

  • Support project audits and compliance reviews.

  • Assist in ensuring environmental and safety standards are maintained.


Project Coordination:

  • Work closely with Project Managers, Engineers, and contractors.

  • Attend site meetings and provide commercial and quality advisory support.

  • Verify executed quantities and certify works completed.



Requirements

Qualifications & Requirements:

Education & Experience:

  • BSc/HND in Quantity Surveying, Civil Engineering, Construction Management, or related field.

  • Minimum of 7 years of relevant experience in quantity surveying and/or quality assurance for infrastructure projects.

  • Proven experience in water infrastructure, civil works, or public works projects is required.

  • Experience handling donor-funded, NGO-sponsored, or government projects is highly desirable.


Professional Certification (Compulsory):

  • Registered with QSRBN (Quantity Surveyors Registration Board of Nigeria) – Mandatory (for QS background).

  • Strong knowledge of BOQ preparation, cost control, and contract administration.

  • Ability to interpret technical drawings and specifications.

Personal Attributes:

  • High attention to detail and strong analytical skills.

title: Forward Deployed Product Lead
description:
About Us:

ClearRoute is an engineering consultancy bridging Quality Engineering, Cloud Platforms and Developer Experience. We help enterprises reliably bring high-impact digital products to market faster, cheaper, and safer, working with technology leaders facing complex business challenges.

We take as much pride in our people, culture and work-life balance as we do in making better software. We’re not just making better software. We’re making the making of software better. Collaborative, entrepreneurial and dedicated to problem solving, we bring the step change our customer need to sustain innovation. Our values challenge us to do the best we can for ClearRoute, our customers and most importantly our team. This is an opportunity for you to build the organisation from the ground up, use your voice to drive change and help transform organisations and problem domains.

Role:

The Forward Deployed Product Lead owns the product discovery workstream within the pod and is the primary interface between ClearRoute and the client user and domain experts throughout an engagement. They design and facilitate the as-is data gathering activities, shape the findings and open questions that populate the project knowledge space, and lead the translation of raw discovery material into a validated set of assumptions, personas and journeys that the pod can build against. They work in constant partnership with the Technical Lead and are accountable for ensuring the pattern produces outcomes the client recognises, trusts and can act on.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Design and facilitate discovery activities. This includes workshops, interviews, whiteboarding and data mapping sessions to capture broad and deep as-is context with the client team.

  • Define the structure and taxonomy for discovery findings and open questions so they can be captured cleanly in the project knowledge space.

  • Partner with the Technical Lead to specify what goes into the Claude project and file structure and review the resulting client-facing knowledge space for accuracy and narrative clarity.

  • Lead synthesis of raw inputs into a baselined set of validated assumptions, personas and user journeys for the synthesis platform.

  • Own the client relationship throughout discovery and prototyping, managing expectations, surfacing risks, and keeping sponsors engaged

  • Lead prototype testing sessions with client teams, gather feedback, and drive iteration of target-state artefacts based on that feedback.

  • Coach client teams on the forward deployed / agentic discovery methodology so they can engage with and eventually run elements of it themselves.

  • Contribute to proposals and pre-sales conversations, articulating the value of the pattern to prospective clients.

Required Experience:

  • Substantial product discovery or product management experience, including leading discovery on complex, ambiguous engagements.

  • Strong workshop design and facilitation skills, comfortable running sessions with senior client stakeholders as well as delivery teams.

  • Demonstrated ability to synthesise large volumes of unstructured qualitative material (notes, transcripts, diagrams) into clear, structured findings.

  • Working familiarity with AI-assisted analysis and project-based LLM workflows (Claude Projects) sufficient to direct their use, even without building them personally.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, including presenting findings and recommendations to senior client stakeholders.

  • Experience defining personas, journey maps and validated assumptions as inputs to solution design.

Desirable Experience:

  • Prior experience with double-diamond or other structured discovery methods, and an appetite to evolve that practice into a more agentic, pod-based model.

  • Background in consulting or professional services, ideally in embedded or forward-deployed delivery models working directly within client environments.

  • Enough familiarity with prototyping tools to give directional input on clickable prototypes, even where the Technical Lead does the build.

  • Experience in the industries ClearRoute serves, particularly regulated or enterprise environments where discovery involves complex stakeholder landscapes.

Working at ClearRoute

We have grown from six founders to 180+ people across five countries in three years, and what sets us apart isn't the pace, it's how we grow.

  • Real flexibility, in practice. We trust you to perform at your best and still have a life outside of work, with genuine hybrid working, a home office budget, an open feedback culture where your voice shapes decisions, and time off when life needs it (birthday included).

  • When ClearRoute wins, you win. We offer profit share so success is shared, meaningful recognition for great work, and benefits that look after you and your family, including private healthcare, competitive salary benchmarking, and a confidential employee assistance program covering counselling, mental health support, and financial wellbeing.

  • A community you'll genuinely want to be part of. Interest based communities like running and book clubs, Women in Tech group, monthly socials, and cross regional events bring people together across the company. An inclusive, collaborative culture where you don't need to conform to succeed, where people support one another and feel comfortable being themselves.

  • Where meaningful work meets real growth. You will tackle complex, real world problems at the forefront of platform engineering, AI, security, and scalable systems. Your growth is supported by learning budgets, Udemy access, a clear career framework, internal mobility, and thought leadership opportunities that take your impact beyond ClearRoute.

At ClearRoute, we believe diverse perspectives lead to better outcomes, and inclusion creates the conditions for everyone to thrive. We are proud to have built a family friendly working environment and have many employees who have caring responsibilities alongside work. We welcome applications from people who require flexibility and will be happy to discuss needs on an individual basis.

We are committed to fostering a culture where all team members feel respected, supported, and empowered to do their best work. We celebrate individuality and our differences and understand that some differences may mean that you require changes made to the interview process. We are happy to cater to your needs to make the interview accessible, if this is something you require please let us know by emailing us at join@clearroute.io

Job Summary

The Senior Product Owner for Digital sits within the Digital Product Strategy team as part of the Customer Service Experience organization, playing a key role in advancing Avangrid’s digital transformation. This position leads the development, enhancement, and management of high-impact digital products, such as Payments & Collections, Customer Satisfaction (CSAT) experiences, and Energy Manager solutions, driving meaningful outcomes for both customers and the business.

Avangrid, a member of the Iberdrola Group - a global energy leader and the world’s largest producer of wind power—serves over 100 million customers worldwide. In this role, you will help shape the digital experience for more than 3 million U.S. customers, balancing customer needs, regulatory requirements, and business priorities.

You will define product vision, manage and prioritize the product backlog, and deliver solutions that increase digital adoption, improve satisfaction, and streamline customer journeys. Working alongside other Product Owners, you will act as a single, aligned voice across multiple states, ensuring consistency while adapting to local requirements. This includes creating and enhancing digital experiences that provide customers with actionable insights into energy usage, consumption trends, bill drivers, efficiency opportunities, and external factors such as weather, enabling more informed decision-making and greater control over their energy consumption.

Operating in a transforming Agile environment, this role also serves as a driver of business transformation, promoting data-driven decision-making and continuous improvement. • Performs all sales and leasing activities to achieve the community’s revenue and occupancy goals by greeting and qualifying prospects, conducting community tours and showing apartments, processing applications, credit screening, and criminal background checks, preparing the lease and move-in package, and ensuring a smooth resident move-in and lease signing.

• Stays informed about current market and competitor conditions that may impact the community’s occupancy and sales results, develops and implements short- and long-term marketing plans and goals to sustain occupancy, and follows the community’s established policies related to concessions, specials, and other programs to boost occupancy.

title: Naval Program and Trial Specialist
description:
Naval Program and Trial Specialist

The Opportunity:

As a Naval Program and Trial Specialist, you understand the complexities of supporting acquisition, acceptance trials, and deployment activities from concept to completion. That’s why we need you, a skilled program and trial specialist who can ensure mission success through careful analysis, hands-on trial support, and effective communication.

On our team, you will support critical Navy acquisition and test activities for Unmanned Surface Vessels. You will support and coordinate trial events that require frequent travel to shipyards within the continental United States. This role directly supports sea trials, including testing underway at sea and land-based support facilities for periods of up to ten days away from home station. Underway periods require personal protective equipment (PPE) to include hard hat, reflective vest, and steel toe boots.

You’ll leverage resources like MS Office, program management systems such as MS Project and Excel based tools, assess and document test results, and deliver senior-level briefs to government leadership. In this role, you will collaborate regularly with PAPMs, APMs, subject matter experts, INSURV, shipbuilders, trial teams, and acquisition stakeholders.

The real impact of this role comes from communication and disciplined execution, ensuring programs meet quality standards and trial events achieve their objectives. At Booz Allen, we recognize that continuous growth strengthens our team and our client support. Here, you’ll have the resources needed to succeed in a fast-paced environment while contributing to a mission that strengthens the future U.S. Navy. Work with us and help ensure the Navy accomplishes its mission through well-executed program oversight, acquisition rigor, and successful shipboard trial operations.

Join us. The world can't wait.

You Have:

  • 5+ years of experience coordinating or participating in Navy shipboard testing, acceptance trials, inspections, or readiness events

  • 3+ years of experience working in program or project management

  • 3+ years of experience providing direct support to U.S. government Programs Management Offices, PAPMs, and APMs

  • 3+ years of experience preparing and delivering senior-level briefing reports to government staff or corporate leadership

  • 3+ years of experience working with unmanned vehicles such as Unmanned Surface Vessels

  • Experience with MS Office Suite including Outlook, Excel, Word, and PowerPoint

  • Ability to work independently with high attention to detail

  • Secret clearance

We are searching for analytical RF engineers to join the Strategic Systems Operation Division within the Information Advantage Office at the Applied Research Laboratory (ARL) at Penn State. This role will collaborate with technical staff to research, design, develop, integrate, and test advanced wireless RF communications systems.

ARL is an authorized DoD SkillBridge partner and welcomes all transitioning military members to apply.

  • Experience in the use and analysis of passive and active RF systems

  • Knowledge in the areas of RF circuit implementation, design, test, and analysis

  • Agility with link budget theory and RF fundamentals

title: Cloud Business Analyst – Governance, Process Design
description:
Cloud Business Analyst – Governance, Process Design & Azure

Location: Montreal, Canada

Onsite: 5 days a week 8am-5pm

Top 3 Required Skills:

• Business Analysis
• Designing Governance Process & Definitions
• Azure Cloud basic Knowledge

The Cloud First Business Analyst serves as the governance analyst and documentation lead for the Cloud First Program. Working under the direction of the Program Management Team and Program Technical Lead, the role documents governance entities defines inputs and outputs, models governance processes, and develops the artefacts required to operationalize the Cloud First governance framework.

Purpose of the Role

The role identifies information requirements, analyses governance needs, documents agreed outcomes, develops governance artefacts, and models end-to-end processes. Stakeholder engagement, workshop coordination, meeting management, communications, approval follow-up, and final governance decisions remain with the Program Management Team and Program Technical Lead.

Key Responsibilities

1. Governance Operating Model

• Support the Program Management Team and Program Technical Lead in finalizing the definition of all Cloud First governance entities.
• Document the purpose, scope, responsibilities, authority, decision rights, membership, and cadence of each governance entity.
• Maintain the governance catalogue and operating model.

2. Inputs and Outputs Definition

• Define and document the inputs required by each governance entity.
• Define outputs, decisions, approvals, actions, and artefacts produced by each governance entity.
• Produce governance interaction models that show information flows between governance bodies.

3. Governance Process Definition

• Work with the Program Technical Lead to define the processes executed within each governance entity.
• Document process objectives, triggers, activities, approvals, decision points, and outcomes.
• Apply consistent documentation standards across the programme.

4. Process Modelling and Repository Management

• Develop clear process maps and flowcharts for governance processes.
• Document workflow dependencies, approvals, escalations, and hand-offs.
• Maintain the governance process repository and supporting artefacts.

Responsibility Boundaries

The Business Analyst supports analysis and documentation, but is not accountable for:

• Arranging workshops or meetings
• Managing stakeholder communications
• Scheduling sessions or maintaining calendars
• Chasing stakeholders for feedback
• Securing approvals
• Owning governance decisions

These activities remain the responsibility of the Cloud First Program Management Team, with support and direction from the Program Technical Lead.

Required Skills and Competencies

• Strong business analysis, requirements analysis, and structured documentation skills.
• Experience documenting governance operating models, decision rights, RACI matrices, and escalation frameworks.
• Proficiency in process mapping, workflow analysis, and modelling dependencies, approvals, and hand-offs.
• Ability to translate complex governance discussions into clear, consistent, and usable artefacts.
• Strong written communication, attention to detail, version control, and repository management.
• Ability to collaborate effectively with programme management, technical leads, and governance stakeholders.

Preferred Experience and Tools

• Experience supporting cloud transformation, cloud adoption, technology governance, or enterprise change programmes.
• Working knowledge of common process-modelling methods and tools such as Microsoft Visio, Lucidchart, or equivalent.
• Experience with Microsoft 365 collaboration and documentation tools, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams, and SharePoint.
• Understanding of governance controls, approval workflows, decision logs, and document lifecycle management.

Education and Experience

• Bachelor’s degree in business, Information Systems, Computer Science, Engineering, or related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
• Business analysis or process-modelling certification is advantageous.
• Relevant experience level to be aligned with the organization’s role-grading and project requirements.

Success Measures

• Governance artefacts are complete, accurate, consistent, traceable, and ready for review and approval.
• Process models clearly show triggers, activities, decision points, approvals, escalations, dependencies, and outcomes.
• Governance repositories remain current, controlled, and easy for stakeholders to navigate.
• Deliverables are completed in line with agreed programme priorities and documentation standards.

  • Global Team Leadership & Operations: Lead, mentor, and supervise regional Network Operations managers (across North America, EMEA, and APAC), and the global delivery team in India, establishing operational consistency, clear accountability, service level standards, and high performance across distributed global teams.
  • Resiliency, Redundancy & Observability: Drive strategy and operational execution for network resiliency, redundancy, disaster recovery, and fault tolerance; assess, deploy, and leverage emerging AI/AIOps tools and telemetry platforms to enable proactive incident prevention, rapid MTTR, and robust network security.
  • Financial Oversight & Budget Management: Oversee and manage the global network operational budget, conducting continuous cost rationalization, tracking spend against forecasts, and ensuring maximum business value from all infrastructure investments.
  • Strategic Vendor & Partner Management: Forge and maintain strong strategic partnerships with hardware vendors, telecommunications carriers, and Managed Service Providers (MSPs) to negotiate mutually beneficial agreements, enforce strict SLAs, and drive ongoing business value.
  • Portfolio & Delivery Alignment: Collaborate closely with Project Management, Sourcing, and Finance to oversee the network project portfolio, control capital and operational spend, and ensure on-time, on-budget delivery of global network initiatives.
  • Architecture & Engineering Collaboration: Work in close partnership with the Global Head of Network Architecture and Engineering to maintain strategic alignment, ensure operational viability of new technical designs, share resource capacity, and seamlessly transition architecture into production.
  • Infrastructure Operations Leadership: Join and actively participate as a key member of the Infrastructure Operations leadership team, contributing to global infrastructure strategies, cross-functional operational improvements, and company-wide technology initiatives.
  • Major Incident & Problem Management: Provide senior escalation management during critical network incidents, driving swift resolution, transparent executive stakeholder communication, and rigorous post-incident root-cause analysis (RCA) to eliminate recurring failure modes.
  • Governance, Compliance & Security: Partner with Cyber Security (CISO) and Risk teams to enforce patch and vulnerability management, zero-trust access controls, and regulatory compliance across all regional network environments.
Qualifications
  • Education & Experience: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience; 10+ years of progressive IT infrastructure experience with at least 5+ years supervising network managers or leading regional network teams.
  • Technical Expertise: Deep technical knowledge of enterprise network domains, including WAN/LAN/WLAN, SD-WAN, multi-cloud networking (AWS, GCP, Azure), BGP/MPLS, firewalls, network automation, and modern telemetry/observability platforms (e.g., Datadog, ThousandEyes, Cisco Catalyst/Meraki, Splunk, AIOps tools).
  • Leadership & Team Building: Proven track record of leading multi-national network operations and management of global offshore operational hubs (specifically in India) with a strong focus on talent development, role clarity, and operational rigor.
  • Financial & Business Acumen: Strong business acumen with demonstrated experience managing large OPEX/CAPEX budgets, telecom contract negotiations, and vendor governance.
  • Stakeholder Management: Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, with a proven ability to collaborate with and influence stakeholders across autonomous, matrixed business units.
  • Frameworks & Certifications: Strong grounding in ITIL/ITSM best practices and modern Agile delivery models. Relevant technical or management certifications (e.g., CCNP/CCIE, ITIL v4, AWS/GCP Networking) are preferred.
Operational Demands & Work Environment
  • Global 24/7 Incident Escalations: Willingness to serve as a senior escalation point for high-severity global outages across varying time zones outside standard business hours.
  • Decentralized Business Unit Environment: Managing alignment and enforcing global operational standards across distinct Business Units that maintain significant operational autonomy.
  • Occasional Travel: Domestic and international travel (approximately 10–15%) to regional hubs, major data centers, office sites, and vendor summits.

and distributing authoritative and engaging content to consumers and businesses throughout

information services, book publishing, digital real estate services, cable network programming

in Australia and pay-TV distribution in Australia.

  • Are you looking for a career path in public service?

If you answered “yes” to all these questions, then the Department of Driver Services would love for you to become a respected member of our team.

The Georgia Department of Driver Services (DDS) is seeking qualified candidates for:

Position Title: Identity and Driver Credential Specialist 1 MSA

Status: Full-Time

Salary: $32,000 /annually (non-negotiable) +3,500 Supplement

About Georgia Department of Drivers Services (DDS):

The Georgia Department of Driver Services (DDS) is a progressive agency that encompasses a broad range of activities and programs. Our Mission at DDS is to provide secure driver and identity credentials to our customers with excellence and respect.

Job Summary:

As an Identity and Driver Credential Specialists 1 for DDS, you will help make everyday life possible for thousands of State of Georgia residents. The successful candidate in this role can make a positive impact on the lives of their customers whether it’s issuing learner’s permit to teens, welcoming newcomers by converting out-of-state licenses, awarding driver licenses to first-time drivers by administering examinations or issuing identity cards in compliance with state laws and regulations. The focus of this position is working with and through others within established guidelines. The ability to interact comfortably with a diverse population is important. The successful candidate in this position must be friendly and genuinely interested in helping others. Patience and attention to detail is a major focus of the job, and those details need to be handled quickly, accurately and efficiently. High-volume centers cater to a larger customer base and consequently experience higher frequencies of incidents such as dealing with irate customers, slip and falls, road test crashes, sick customers, etc. May serve as team lead to lower-level staff.

Career Mobility:

  • DDS believes in internal mobility and career advancement opportunities for our employees with satisfactory performance to transition from Identity and Driver Credential Specialists 1 to Identity and Driver Credential Specialists 2 with an increase of 10%.

Identity and Driver Credential Specialists 1

After 12 months of employment

$1600

After 18 months of employment (promotion to Identity and Driver Credential Specialist 2)

$1600

Major Service Area (MSA)

DDS Customer Service Centers with a high volume of transactions (minimum of 40,000 annually) are considered MSA Centers. The agency will conduct an MSA Assessment every twenty-four months to determine if CSCs need to be added or removed from the MSA Category. The Team Members assigned to an MSA Center receive a $3,500 supplement.

The following conditions apply to Identity and Driver Credential Specialists hired after July 1, 2026, which will result in loss of the $3,500 supplement:

  • transfer from an MSA Center to a non-MSA Center
  • transfer to Headquarters
  • CSC is removed from the MSA Category

Duties:

  • Working with citizens to ensure applications, records and documents are completed accurately.
  • Accompanying drivers in vehicles, both in a traditional and virtual capacity, to evaluate their ability to adhere to Georgia’s driving laws.
  • Conducting driving examinations for motorcycle and commercial licenses in accordance with state law and regulations.
  • Operating visual testing equipment.
  • Accurately collecting payments via cash or credit cards

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Must be eighteen (18) years of age
  • Completion of a high school diploma or GED is required
  • A valid Georgia Class C or equivalent License is required and must be maintained while employed in this position.
  • At least one (1) year of Face-to-face Customer Service experience within the last five years
  • At least one (1) year of Face-to-face experience with cash transactions including handling cash, daily reconciliation, and processing credit card payments within the last five years.
  • Comfortable working with computer and internet technology.

Preferred Qualifications: Preference will be given to those applicants who, in addition to meeting the minimum qualification above, also possess two or more of the following:

  • At least three (3) years of Face-to-face Customer Service experience within the last five years
  • At least three (3) years of recent Face-to-face experience with cash transactions including handling cash, daily reconciliation, and processing credit card payments within the last five years
  • Live within 30 miles of the Customer Service Center for which you are applying
  • Bilingual skillset preferred

Working Conditions for this position are as follows: Road skills tests are conducted throughout the year in a variety of weather conditions including rain, wind, summer heat and cold winter days. Testing begins in the early morning hours and continues through the early evening hours. The test runs approximately 30 minutes. Walking distances, standing, very little sitting, constantly moving, good vision and hearing, climbing in trucks, bending, squatting, lifting, reaching, turning, riding in cars and trucks, driving cars and trucks, constant interaction with the public and co-workers are prerequisites.

Conditions of Employment:

  • A valid Georgia driver’s license is required and must be maintained while employed in this position. Non-Georgia residents must have a recognized equivalent license. If a valid Georgia driver’s license has not been held for at least three years at the time of application, you will be required to obtain a Motor Vehicle record from the previous state of licensure prior to hire.
  • Successful completion of the CCKE (Certified Commercial Knowledge Examiner) Certification, a national certification is required by all employees who issue driver’s licenses.
  • Employees who conduct CDL (Commercial Driver’s License) road tests must successfully complete the CDL Examiner Certification and the CCE (Certified Commercial Examiner) Certification.
  • Employees must maintain these requirements to continue employment with DDS.
  • Employees must have flexible work availability due to customer service centers having varied operational hours.
  • DDS employees may be required as a term and condition of employment, to assist in meeting the responsibilities of the Department. In addition, they may be required to perform responsibilities that are not regularly assigned to them in order to continue the operations of the agency which includes assisting other centers. Management will work with employee regarding the locations and mode of transportation.

Total compensation: Combines direct compensation with the value of the State’s benefits and work-life options. Total Compensation establishes a win-win partnership that is important to the quality and success of the State programs and services. Most importantly, State employees enjoy the satisfaction that comes with being part of a team that keeps Georgia progressive, prosperous and a place we are all proud to call home.

title: Junior Product Manager (Network Solution) | Dutch Speaking) - Graduate Program
description:

title: Pre Press Technician
description:
Position Summary:


Midstates Printing is seeking a detail-oriented Prepress Technician to prepare customer files for accurate, efficient, and high-quality print production. This position reviews incoming artwork, identifies and corrects potential production issues, and prepares files for digital and offset printing. The ideal candidate has strong graphic-production skills, a solid understanding of commercial printing, and the ability to manage multiple projects in a deadline-driven environment.


Full Time, benefit eligible position - Typically M-F 8:00 a.m. - 5:00 p.m. more or fewer hours may be offered based on workload.


Benefits:

  • Health, dental, vision, life insurance and long term and short term disability
  • Paid time off and paid holidays.
  • Retirement plan.
  • Company-provided training and opportunities for professional development.
  • Additional benefits may be available based on company policy


Key Responsibilities

  • Review and preflight customer-supplied files for accuracy and print readiness.
  • Identify and resolve issues involving fonts, images, bleeds, color spaces, transparency, page size, and resolution.
  • Prepare, impose, and process files for digital and offset printing.
  • Make necessary file corrections while maintaining the customer’s intended design.
  • Create print-ready PDFs and output proofs for customer or internal approval.
  • Apply trapping, color conversions, overprint settings, and other production requirements.
  • Prepare files for plates, digital presses, and finishing equipment.
  • Verify job specifications, including page counts, dimensions, paper, inks, coatings, binding, and finishing requirements.
  • Communicate file concerns and production requirements with customer service representatives, sales staff, customers, and production departments.
  • Perform quality-control checks throughout the prepress process.
  • Maintain organized electronic job files and follow established naming and archiving procedures.
  • Troubleshoot workflow, software, and file-processing issues.
  • Help maintain color consistency and established color-management standards.
  • Meet production schedules while managing multiple jobs and changing priorities.
  • Follow company safety, quality, and confidentiality procedures.
  • Perform other duties as assigned

title: All-Source Analyst
description:
All-Source Analyst

The Opportunity:

With all the information available today, it takes a skilled all-source analyst to know how to find and interpret the best data to give their clients the right answers. With the critical decisions made in our government and military every day, we need an intelligence analyst like you to do just that. As an Order of Battle all-source analyst, you use your specialized functional experience and your attention to detail to conduct all-source analytic production on naval joint capabilities.

As an All-Source Analyst performing database management support on our team, you’ll help your client by providing production on cyberspace installations and facilities in the modernized integrated database (MIDB) and Machine-assisted Analytic Rapid-repository System (MARS) database records. Using your comprehensive understanding of all-source analysis you will discover the infrastructure and create corresponding records within the appropriate systems.

This is a chance to grow your expertise and broaden your skill set in areas like analysis, writing, and communication. You’ll share your expertise with other analysts through leadership and mentoring. We focus on growing as a team to deliver the best support to our customers, so you’ll have resources to learn new skills and tools. Join us as we provide the right information at the right time to support the critical needs of our warfighters and nation’s leaders.

Join us. The world can’t wait.

You Have:

  • 3+ years of experience with the Modernized Integrated Database (MIDB) or the Machine-Assisted Rapid-repository System (MARS)

  • Knowledge of IC and Combatant Command environments

  • Ability to develop high-quality deliverables such as complex written products and formal or informal briefings tailored to clients who range from tactical to strategic levels

  • Active TS/SCI clearance; willingness to take a polygraph exam

  • Bachelor's degree and 3+ years of experience with all-source analysis, or 8+ years of experience with all-source analysis in lieu of a degree

Nice If You Have:

  • 3+ years of experience in cyber analysis

  • Experience with OSINT or GEOINT

  • Knowledge of conventional weapons systems

  • Knowledge of ICD 203/206 analytic tradecraft standards

Clearance:

Applicants selected will be subject to a security investigation and may need to meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information; TS/SCI clearance is required.

At Booz Allen, we celebrate your contributions, provide you with opportunities and choices, and support your total well-being. Our offerings include health, life, disability, financial, and retirement benefits, as well as paid leave, professional development, tuition assistance, work-life programs, and dependent care. The estimate displayed represents the typical salary range for this position and is just one component of Booz Allen’s total compensation package for employees. You are expected to be on camera during interviews and assessments. We reserve the right to take your picture to verify your identity and prevent fraud.

title: Purchasing and Financial Coordinator - College of Engineering - Chemical Engineering
description:
Carnegie Mellon University is a private, global research university that stands among the world’s most renowned education institutions. With ground-breaking brain science, path-breaking performances, creative start-ups, big data, big ambitions, hands-on learning, and a whole lot of robots, CMU doesn’t imagine the future, we invent it. If you’re passionate about joining a community that challenges the curious to deliver work that matters, your journey starts here!

Since its inception in 1905, the Carnegie Mellon Department of Chemical Engineering has been on the leading edge of research and innovation in chemical engineering. Today, this is more true than ever. With research thrusts across fields such as health and medicine, biofuels, air quality and more, CMU chemical engineering students are paving the way to healthier, cleaner, more efficient future for all.

The Department of Chemical Engineering is seeking a Purchasing and Financial Coordinator to support daily research, administrative, and financial operations. This role manages routine purchasing for research laboratories, provides financial and scheduling support, and serves as a backup point of contact for facilities coordination. The position works closely with other members of the Operations team to keep research and department operations running smoothly for faculty, staff, and students. The ideal candidate is someone organized, detail-oriented, and comfortable managing multiple recurring tasks and requests at once.

Research Purchasing:

  • Process routine purchase requests from faculty, PhD students, and research staff, including consumables, general lab supplies, and equipment.
  • Track orders from request through delivery; follow up on delays or issues with vendors.
  • Process reimbursements and departmental purchasing card reconciliations.
  • Assist in negotiations with vendors and ensures completion of contract terms; responsible for merchandise selection. Recommends alternative products and vendors.
  • Responsible for obtaining all documentation needed for purchase completion.
  • Assist finance team to develop improved processes for purchasing and other finance operations.
  • Coordinate freight/equipment deliveries, and outgoing equipment shipments/repairs.
  • Assist with receipt/storage of packages requiring special handling (e.g. temperature sensitive).
  • Assist with other purchasing tasks as needed to support department operations.

Financial support:

  • Engineering Research Accelerator’s post-award team to maintain planned labor allocations.
  • Run recurring monthly financial and budget reports for departmental leadership, faculty, and student groups.
  • Process financial transactions, including account redistributions, cost transfers, and other departmental financial activity, as needed.
  • Assist with other financial tasks as needed to support department operations.

General Department Support:

  • Provide backup to other members of the operations team, including facilities and lab staff.
  • Assist with other administrative tasks as needed to support department operations.

As well as other duties as assigned

Adaptability, excellence, and passion are vital qualities within Carnegie Mellon University. We are looking for someone who shares our values and who will support the mission of the university through their work.

You should demonstrate:

  • Excellent communication, verbal and written, as well interpersonal relationship capabilities.
  • Ability to work independently and resolve issues as they arise.

Unlock your potential with tuition benefits, take well-deserved breaks with ample paid time off and observed holidays, and rest easy with life and accidental death and disability insurance.

description:

Albany Med Health System
Chief Clinical Officer (CCO)
Clinical Operations, Quality, and Clinical Integration
Reports to: Health System Chief Executive Officer
Location: Albany, New York (Systemwide responsibilities)
________________________________________

Albany Med Health System (AMHS) is in the midst of executing First Choice 2030, a bold, multi-year transformation agenda designed to position AMHS as the region’s trusted, connected, and transformative academic health system.

AMHS’s Vision states:

Albany Med Health System will be the region’s trusted, connected, and transformative academic health system—advancing the health and well-being of every community we serve.

We will unite exceptional care, discovery, and education to deliver the highest quality outcomes, expand equitable access, and shape the next generation of healthcare professionals.

Through collaboration, innovation, and compassion, AMHS will set the standard for value-based, patient-centered care and serve as a catalyst for health, hope, and opportunity across Upstate New York.

AMHS will be the first choice for patients seeking exceptional care, for providers pursuing the most rewarding careers, for partners driving the most advanced innovation, for students aspiring to the best education, and for supporters seeking the greatest impact.

The AMHS mission is to provide compassionate, high-quality care; advance medical discovery and education; and improve the health of the communities we serve.

To realize this vision, AMHS must integrate its academic medical center, community hospitals, physician enterprise, and clinical programs into a unified, high-performing system defined by clinical excellence, operational discipline, value-based performance, and physician alignment.

The Chief Clinical Officer will serve as one of the principal architects of this transformation—ensuring that clinical operations across the enterprise are aligned, integrated, measurable, and positioned for long-term excellence.
Position Summary

The Chief Clinical Officer (CCO) is the senior executive responsible for system-wide clinical strategy, operations, quality, patient safety, and patient experience across Albany Med Health System (AMHS). The CCO provides enterprise leadership to ensure clinical excellence, operational effectiveness, provider alignment, and integration across academic and community settings.
The CCO leads the development, implementation, and refinement of the system’s clinical strategy, ensuring alignment of clinical operations, care delivery standards, performance improvement, accreditation readiness, and provider culture with the mission, values, and strategic vision of AMHS. The CCO shapes and accelerates an integrated, system-wide model of care that unites physicians, advanced practice providers, nurses, and interdisciplinary care teams across the enterprise. The CCO will also lead the development of innovative programs for population and community health with the aim of measurably optimizing health outcomes and improving service while minimizing per capita costs to produce the highest value, oversee the clinical aspects of the development of novel insurance products, direct to employer healthcare services, and the management of care delivered to AMHS self-insured employees and their dependents, system-wide clinical leadership development efforts, and oversee the coordination of system-wide quality and safety efforts.

Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer, the CCO partners closely with the Chief Operating Officer, Chief Digital Officer, finance leadership, academic leadership, and service line executives to ensure that clinical operations deliver high-quality, safe, efficient, patient-centered, and value-driven care. Direct reports will include the system Chief Quality Officer and, organization based Chief Medical and Chief Nursing Officers (who will co-report to hospital Presidents) among others.

The CCO ensures that clinical priorities are translated into measurable operational plans with clear accountability, financial discipline, performance metrics, and continuous improvement processes across all inpatient, outpatient, ambulatory, virtual, and post-acute care settings.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities include:

  • Provides executive leadership for system-wide clinical operations across all care settings, including inpatient hospitals, ambulatory and physician practices, virtual/digital platforms, and pre- and post-acute services.

  • Formulates recommendations and manages the implementation of programmatic change across all care settings (inpatient, outpatient, ambulatory/physician practices, virtual / digital care platforms, and pre- and post-acute settings).

  • Collaborates on the development of strategic goals for the clinical enterprise that align with the system vision, mission, and strategic objectives.

  • Leads the development of a patient-centric, value-focused clinical enterprise that integrates academic and community-based care into a cohesive delivery system.

  • Establishes systems and processes to ensure effective clinical operations, seamless transitions of care, optimized provider utilization, capacity management, patient throughput, and care team efficiency across the enterprise.

  • Establishes systems and processes that ensure effective clinical operations and reliable transitions of care between academic and community facilities.

  • Collaborates with executive leadership to define strategic goals for the clinical enterprise aligned with system vision, mission, and long-term objectives.

  • Partners with the Chief Operating Officer, Chief Physician Executive, Chief Digital Officer finance leaders, service line leaders and others across the system to develop and execute the annual operating plan and contribute to system-wide budget planning.

  • Evaluates the clinical value and impact of capital investments, facility renovations, service expansions, and technology deployments.

  • Leads the integration and standardization of clinical programs across the academic medical center and community hospitals to optimize access, quality, outcomes, and financial performance.

  • Shapes and advances care delivery models toward value-based pathways and alternative payment structures that position AMHS for evolving reimbursement mechanisms.

  • Partners with system strategy and corporate development leaders to assess community needs, market demand, referral patterns, payer expectations, and competitive positioning.

  • Works with information technology and digital leadership to deploy and optimize electronic health record functionality, digital health tools, telehealth platforms, AI-enabled solutions, and data analytics capabilities that enhance clinical performance and patient experience.

  • Partners with the Chief Quality Officer to establish system-wide goals for clinical quality, patient safety, and high reliability, ensuring accountability for performance and adherence to evidence-based care standards.

  • Supports accreditation readiness and regulatory compliance across all facilities, ensuring adherence to standards related to infection prevention, medication safety, and environment of care.

  • Provides leadership in fostering a culture of accountability, engagement, collaboration, and innovation among physicians and clinical teams

  • Collaborates with human resources to develop multi-year workforce strategies that support recruitment, retention, succession planning, provider engagement, and professional development.

  • Oversees financial stewardship of clinical programs in partnership with finance leadership, ensuring cost-effective operations, productivity optimization, and alignment of clinical performance with financial sustainability.

  • Provides clinical input into reimbursement strategy, managed care negotiations, value-based arrangements, quality incentive structures, and clinical performance guarantees.

  • Ensures timely, accurate documentation, coding, and charge capture across hospital, ambulatory, and physician services.

  • Oversees, in partnership with medical staff leadership, credentialing, privileging, peer review, and professional practice evaluation processes to ensure safe and high-quality care.

  • Supports and advances graduate medical education programs and academic integration, promoting excellence in training, research translation, and clinical innovation.

  • Fosters a culture of patient-centered care, emphasizing service excellence, communication, respect, and shared decision-making across all care settings.

  • Monitors trends in patient satisfaction and clinical outcomes, intervening as needed to address performance gaps and drive sustainable improvement.

  • Serves on relevant system boards and committees and represents clinical operations in executive and governance forums.

  • Represents AMHS to external organizations and regulatory authorities

Qualifications and Experience:

Required:

  • MD or DO with current, unrestricted licensure and board certification in an applicable specialty.

  • Advanced degree in healthcare administration, business administration, public health, or related field preferred.

  • Minimum of 15 years of progressive leadership and administrative experience in a complex health system that includes both academic and community hospital environments.

  • Demonstrated executive experience managing system-wide clinical operations, physician leadership structures, and multidisciplinary care teams.

  • Strong understanding of value-based care, alternative payment models, and evolving reimbursement structures.

  • Proven ability to lead large-scale clinical integration, program development, and performance improvement initiatives.

  • Demonstrated financial acumen, including experience in budgeting, productivity management, capital planning, and cost-of-care optimization.

  • Experience presenting to Boards and executive leadership with performance dashboards, strategic plans, and operational updates.

Leadership Attributes:

  • Enterprise mindset with strong systems thinking and the ability to integrate academic and community care into a unified clinical strategy.

  • Disciplined, execution-oriented leader capable of translating strategy into measurable operational results.

  • High integrity, credibility, and professional presence with physicians, nurses, executives, and governance bodies. Leads from the front.

  • Collaborative leadership style with the ability to influence across a federated system and build alignment among diverse stakeholders.

  • Courage to address complex clinical, operational, and cultural challenges.

  • Comfort operating in complexity, ambiguity, and large-scale transformation environments.

  • Strong interpersonal, analytical, facilitation, and written and verbal communication skills.

  • Action- and results-oriented, with a demonstrated commitment to clinical excellence, patient safety, and continuous improvement.

Thank you for your interest in Albany Med Health System!​

Albany Med Health System is an equal opportunity employer.

This role may require access to information considered sensitive to Albany Med Health System, its patients, affiliates, and partners, including but not limited to HIPAA Protected Health Information and other information regulated by Federal and New York State statutes. Workforce members are expected to ensure that:

Access to information is based on a “need to know” and is the minimum necessary to properly perform assigned duties. Use or disclosure shall not exceed the minimum amount of information needed to accomplish an intended purpose. Reasonable efforts, consistent with Albany Med Health System policies and standards, shall be made to ensure that information is adequately protected from unauthorized access and modification.

description:
Resident Monitors will assist optometry students in Preclinic and Clinical Training Center (CTC) during designated practice times. Monitors will be responsible for offering helpful instructions and guidance to students with the goal of improving the students’ clinical skills.
